objects.definition:
typedef int GIT_CALLBACK(git_smart_subtransport_cb)(
	git_smart_subtransport **out,
	git_transport *owner,
	void *param);
objects.description: Function pointer type for creating a git_smart_subtransport given an owning git_transport and user parameter.
Configuration describing how to construct a smart subtransport: factory callback, whether it is stateless (RPC style), and an opaque parameter passed to the callback.

functions.name: git_libgit2_version
functions.description: Returns the version of the currently used libgit2 library. Callers provide pointers where the major, minor and patch (revision) numbers will be written. Returns 0 on success, or a negative error code on failure.
requirements: major must be a valid, writable pointer to int.
minor must be a valid, writable pointer to int.
rev must be a valid, writable pointer to int.
Check the return value: 0 indicates success; nonzero indicates an error.

functions.name: git_libgit2_prerelease
functions.description: Returns the prerelease state string for the running libgit2 (e.g., "alpha", "beta", "rc1"). Returns NULL for a final release.
requirements: Caller must handle a possible NULL return (final release).
The returned string is owned by libgit2; do not modify or free it.

functions.name: git_libgit2_features
functions.description: Returns a bitmask of compile-time features enabled in libgit2. Combine values of git_feature_t (e.g., GIT_FEATURE_HTTPS, GIT_FEATURE_SSH, etc.).
requirements: Interpret the return value as a bitwise OR of git_feature_t flags.

functions.name: git_libgit2_feature_backend
functions.description: Returns the provider/backend name for a given compile-time feature (e.g., HTTPS backend like "openssl", "openssl-dynamic", or "builtin"). Returns NULL if the feature is not supported.
requirements: feature must be a valid git_feature_t value.
Caller must handle a possible NULL return when the feature is not supported.
The returned string is owned by libgit2; do not modify or free it.

functions.name: git_libgit2_opts
functions.description: Sets or queries global libgit2 options. This is a variadic API where the additional arguments depend on the option (a git_libgit2_opt_t). Many getters write output to caller-provided buffers or pointers; setters read values provided by the caller. Returns 0 on success, <0 on failure.
requirements: option must be a valid git_libgit2_opt_t selector.
The variadic arguments must match the exact types and count required by the selected option as documented in this header.
For GIT_OPT_GET_MWINDOW_SIZE: pass size_t* out (writable, non-NULL).
For GIT_OPT_SET_MWINDOW_SIZE: pass size_t value.
For GIT_OPT_GET_MWINDOW_MAPPED_LIMIT: pass size_t* out (writable, non-NULL).
For GIT_OPT_SET_MWINDOW_MAPPED_LIMIT: pass size_t value.
For GIT_OPT_GET_MWINDOW_FILE_LIMIT: pass size_t* out (writable, non-NULL).
For GIT_OPT_SET_MWINDOW_FILE_LIMIT: pass size_t value (0 means unlimited).

For GIT_OPT_GET_SEARCH_PATH: pass int level (must be one of GIT_CONFIG_LEVEL_SYSTEM, GIT_CONFIG_LEVEL_GLOBAL, GIT_CONFIG_LEVEL_XDG, GIT_CONFIG_LEVEL_PROGRAMDATA), and git_buf* out (writable, non-NULL).

For GIT_OPT_SET_SEARCH_PATH: pass int level (one of the allowed values) and const char* path (may be NULL to reset to default; list is delimited by GIT_PATH_LIST_SEPARATOR; "$PATH" includes the previous value).
For GIT_OPT_SET_CACHE_OBJECT_LIMIT: pass git_object_t type and size_t size (0 disables caching for that type).
For GIT_OPT_SET_CACHE_MAX_SIZE: pass ssize_t max_storage_bytes.
For GIT_OPT_ENABLE_CACHING: pass int enabled.
For GIT_OPT_GET_CACHED_MEMORY: pass ssize_t* current and ssize_t* allowed (both writable, non-NULL).
For GIT_OPT_GET_TEMPLATE_PATH: pass git_buf* out (writable, non-NULL).
For GIT_OPT_SET_TEMPLATE_PATH: pass const char* path (directory path).
For GIT_OPT_SET_SSL_CERT_LOCATIONS: pass const char* file and const char* path; at least one must be non-NULL (both NULL is invalid).
For GIT_OPT_ADD_SSL_X509_CERT: pass const X509* cert (will be added to in-memory store; cannot be removed).
For GIT_OPT_SET_USER_AGENT: pass const char* user_agent ("" to send no comment; NULL to restore default).
For GIT_OPT_GET_USER_AGENT: pass git_buf* out (writable, non-NULL).
For GIT_OPT_SET_USER_AGENT_PRODUCT: pass const char* user_agent_product ("" to send no product; NULL to restore default).
For GIT_OPT_GET_USER_AGENT_PRODUCT: pass git_buf* out (writable, non-NULL).
For GIT_OPT_SET_WINDOWS_SHAREMODE: pass unsigned long value (ignored on non-Windows).
For GIT_OPT_GET_WINDOWS_SHAREMODE: pass unsigned long* value (writable, non-NULL).
For GIT_OPT_ENABLE_STRICT_OBJECT_CREATION: pass int enabled.
For GIT_OPT_ENABLE_STRICT_SYMBOLIC_REF_CREATION: pass int enabled.
For GIT_OPT_SET_SSL_CIPHERS: pass const char* ciphers (list of enabled ciphers).
For GIT_OPT_ENABLE_OFS_DELTA: pass int enabled.
For GIT_OPT_ENABLE_FSYNC_GITDIR: pass int enabled.
For GIT_OPT_ENABLE_STRICT_HASH_VERIFICATION: pass int enabled.
For GIT_OPT_SET_ALLOCATOR: pass git_allocator* allocator (NULL restores system default).
For GIT_OPT_ENABLE_UNSAVED_INDEX_SAFETY: pass int enabled.
For GIT_OPT_GET_PACK_MAX_OBJECTS: pass size_t* out (writable, non-NULL).
For GIT_OPT_SET_PACK_MAX_OBJECTS: pass size_t objects.
For GIT_OPT_DISABLE_PACK_KEEP_FILE_CHECKS: pass int enabled.
For GIT_OPT_ENABLE_HTTP_EXPECT_CONTINUE: pass int enabled (not available on Windows).
For GIT_OPT_SET_ODB_PACKED_PRIORITY: pass int priority.
For GIT_OPT_SET_ODB_LOOSE_PRIORITY: pass int priority.
For GIT_OPT_GET_EXTENSIONS: pass git_strarray* out (must be released with git_strarray_dispose).
For GIT_OPT_SET_EXTENSIONS: pass const char** extensions and size_t len (entries may be negated with a leading '!').
For GIT_OPT_GET_OWNER_VALIDATION: pass int* enabled (writable, non-NULL).
For GIT_OPT_SET_OWNER_VALIDATION: pass int enabled.
For GIT_OPT_GET_HOMEDIR: pass git_buf* out (writable, non-NULL).
For GIT_OPT_SET_HOMEDIR: pass const char* path (directory path).
For GIT_OPT_GET_SERVER_CONNECT_TIMEOUT: pass int* timeout (writable, non-NULL, milliseconds).
For GIT_OPT_SET_SERVER_CONNECT_TIMEOUT: pass int timeout (milliseconds; 0 uses system default and may not exceed system default).
For GIT_OPT_GET_SERVER_TIMEOUT: pass int* timeout (writable, non-NULL, milliseconds).
For GIT_OPT_SET_SERVER_TIMEOUT: pass int timeout (milliseconds; 0 uses system default).
Always check the return value: 0 indicates success; negative values indicate failure.

functions.name: git_libgit2_buildinfo
functions.description: Returns compile-time build information for libgit2 for the requested category (e.g., CPU or commit). Returns NULL on error.
requirements: info must be a valid git_buildinfo_t value (e.g., GIT_BUILDINFO_CPU or GIT_BUILDINFO_COMMIT).
Caller must handle a possible NULL return on error.
The returned string is owned by libgit2; do not modify or free it.

functions.name: git_oid_from_string
functions.signature: int git_oid_from_string(git_oid *out, const char *str, git_oid_t type)
functions.description: Parse a NUL-terminated hex object ID string into a git_oid, for the specified OID type (SHA1 or SHA256 when experimental is enabled). Intended for full-length IDs only; for prefixes use git_oid_from_prefix. Note: this API is only available when GIT_EXPERIMENTAL_SHA256 is enabled.
requirements: Available only when compiled with GIT_EXPERIMENTAL_SHA256.
out must be a valid, writable pointer to a git_oid.
str must be a valid, NUL-terminated hex string of the exact hex size for the given type (40 for SHA1, 64 for SHA256).
type must be a valid git_oid_t (GIT_OID_SHA1 or GIT_OID_SHA256).
Returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure.

functions.name: git_oid_from_prefix
functions.signature: int git_oid_from_prefix(git_oid *out, const char *str, size_t len, git_oid_t type)
functions.description: Parse the given number of hex characters from a string into a git_oid for the specified OID type, zero-filling the remainder of the oid. Use for partial object ID prefixes that are not necessarily NUL-terminated. Only available with experimental SHA256.
requirements: Available only when compiled with GIT_EXPERIMENTAL_SHA256.
out must be a valid, writable pointer to a git_oid.
str must point to at least len readable bytes of hex characters.
len must be between 0 and the hex size for the given type (0..40 for SHA1, 0..64 for SHA256).
type must be a valid git_oid_t (GIT_OID_SHA1 or GIT_OID_SHA256).
Returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure.

functions.name: git_oid_from_raw
functions.signature: int git_oid_from_raw(git_oid *out, const unsigned char *raw, git_oid_t type)
functions.description: Parse raw object ID bytes into a git_oid for the specified OID type. Reads the appropriate number of bytes for the type (20 for SHA1, 32 for SHA256). Only available with experimental SHA256.
requirements: Available only when compiled with GIT_EXPERIMENTAL_SHA256.
out must be a valid, writable pointer to a git_oid.
raw must point to at least the raw size for the given type (20 bytes for SHA1, 32 bytes for SHA256).
type must be a valid git_oid_t.
Returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure.

functions.name: git_oid_fromstr
functions.description: Parse a hex-formatted object ID from a byte sequence into a git_oid. The sequence need not be NUL-terminated and must contain at least the full hex length (40 for SHA1, 64 for SHA256).
requirements: out must be a valid, writable pointer to a git_oid.
str must point to at least the full hex length for the library’s current OID type (40 or 64) bytes of readable data starting at the hex sequence.
String need not be NUL-terminated.
Returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure.

functions.name: git_oid_fromstrp
functions.description: Parse a NUL-terminated hex string into a git_oid.
requirements: out must be a valid, writable pointer to a git_oid.
str must be a valid, NUL-terminated hex string of the correct full length for the library’s current OID type (40 or 64 characters).
Returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure.

functions.name: git_oid_fromstrn
functions.signature: int git_oid_fromstrn(git_oid *out, const char *str, size_t length)
functions.description: Parse exactly length hex characters from a string into a git_oid. If length is odd, the last byte’s low nibble is set to zero.
requirements: out must be a valid, writable pointer to a git_oid.
str must point to at least length readable bytes of hex characters.
length must be a non-negative size; behavior defined by the function for any length; if odd, low nibble of last byte is zeroed.
Returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure.

functions.name: git_oid_fromraw
functions.description: Copy raw OID bytes into a git_oid. Reads the appropriate number of bytes for the library’s current OID type (20 for SHA1, 32 for SHA256).
requirements: out must be a valid, writable pointer to a git_oid.
raw must point to at least the raw size for the current OID type (20 or 32 bytes).
Returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure.

functions.name: git_oid_fmt
functions.description: Format a git_oid to a hex string without adding a NUL terminator.
requirements: out must point to a buffer with at least the hex size for the current OID type (40 or 64) bytes available.
id must be a valid pointer to a git_oid.
Caller must add a '\0' terminator if needed.
Returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure.

functions.name: git_oid_nfmt
functions.signature: int git_oid_nfmt(char *out, size_t n, const git_oid *id)
functions.description: Format a git_oid into a partial hex string of up to n bytes. Does not add a NUL terminator. If n exceeds GIT_OID_SHA1_HEXSIZE, extra bytes are zeroed (per documentation).
requirements: out must point to a buffer with at least n bytes writable.
id must be a valid pointer to a git_oid.
No NUL terminator is added by this function.
If n > GIT_OID_SHA1_HEXSIZE, extra bytes in out will be zeroed.
Returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure.

functions.name: git_oid_pathfmt
functions.description: Format a git_oid into a loose-object path string of the form "aa/..." where "aa" are the first two hex digits and the remainder follows. Does not add a NUL terminator.
requirements: out must point to a buffer with at least 41 bytes for SHA1 or 65 bytes for SHA256.
id must be a valid pointer to a git_oid.
Only the path characters are written; caller must add a '\0' terminator if required.
Returns 0 on success, a non-zero callback-derived value, or a negative error code on failure.

functions.name: git_oid_tostr_s
functions.description: Format a git_oid into a statically allocated C string owned by the library. May be thread-local when thread support is enabled. The returned pointer must not be freed by the caller.
requirements: oid must be a valid pointer to a git_oid.
Caller must not free or modify the returned buffer.
Return value is NULL on failure.

functions.name: git_oid_tostr
functions.signature: char * git_oid_tostr(char *out, size_t n, const git_oid *id)
functions.description: Format a git_oid into a buffer as a hex C string. Always NUL-terminates if n > 0, truncating to n-1 if the buffer is too small. On invalid parameters (out == NULL, n == 0, id == NULL) returns a pointer to an empty string so the return is always printable.
requirements: If out is non-NULL and n > 0, out must reference a buffer of at least n bytes.
id should be a valid pointer to a git_oid for normal operation; if NULL, function returns pointer to an empty string.
If n is too small, output is truncated to n-1 characters and NUL-terminated.
Return value is the out buffer (for valid inputs) or a pointer to an empty string for parameter errors.

functions.name: git_oid_cpy
functions.description: Copy a git_oid from src to out.
requirements: out must be a valid, writable pointer to a git_oid.
src must be a valid pointer to a git_oid.
Returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure.

functions.name: git_oid_cmp
functions.description: Compare two git_oid values for ordering.
requirements: a must be a valid pointer to a git_oid.
b must be a valid pointer to a git_oid.
Returns < 0 if a < b, 0 if equal, > 0 if a > b.

functions.name: git_oid_equal
functions.description: Check two git_oid values for equality.
requirements: a must be a valid pointer to a git_oid.
b must be a valid pointer to a git_oid.
Returns non-zero (true) if equal, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: git_oid_ncmp
functions.signature: int git_oid_ncmp(const git_oid *a, const git_oid *b, size_t len)
functions.description: Compare the first len hexadecimal characters (nibbles) of two git_oid values.
requirements: a must be a valid pointer to a git_oid.
b must be a valid pointer to a git_oid.
len is the number of hex characters (nibbles) to compare.
Returns 0 in case of a match.

functions.name: git_oid_streq
functions.description: Check whether a git_oid equals the given hex-formatted object ID string.
requirements: id must be a valid pointer to a git_oid.
str must be a hex string representation of an object ID.
Returns 0 on match, -1 otherwise.

functions.name: git_oid_strcmp
functions.description: Compare a git_oid to a hex-formatted object ID string for ordering and equality.
requirements: id must be a valid pointer to a git_oid.
str should be a valid hex string; if not valid, the function returns -1.
Returns: -1 if str is not valid; < 0 if id sorts before str; 0 if they match; > 0 if id sorts after str.

functions.name: git_oid_is_zero
functions.description: Check whether the git_oid is all zeros.
requirements: id must be a valid pointer to a git_oid.
Returns 1 if all zeros, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: git_oid_shorten_new
functions.description: Create a new OID shortener used to determine the minimal unique abbreviation length across a set of text OIDs.
requirements: min_length sets the minimal length that will be reported even if a shorter unique length exists.
Returns a pointer to a new git_oid_shorten instance, or NULL on out-of-memory.

functions.name: git_oid_shorten_add
functions.description: Add a hex OID string to the shortener set and compute the minimal unique length for all added OIDs. Intended for full 40-character hex OIDs.
requirements: os must be a valid pointer to a git_oid_shorten created by git_oid_shorten_new.
text_id is expected to be a 40-character hexadecimal string (per documentation).
There is a hard limit of approximately 32,000 OIDs per set; exceeding this returns GIT_ERROR_INVALID (< 0).
Returns the minimal unique length (>= min_length) on success, or a negative error code on failure.

functions.name: git_oid_shorten_free
functions.description: Free an OID shortener instance created by git_oid_shorten_new.
requirements: os must be a pointer previously returned by git_oid_shorten_new (may be NULL per typical free semantics; behavior not explicitly documented).
After this call, os must not be used.

functions.name: git_buf_dispose
functions.description: Releases the dynamically allocated memory referenced by a git_buf (the buffer->ptr) without freeing the git_buf structure itself. Use this to clean up buffers returned or populated by libgit2 APIs that use git_buf. This function returns no value; callers are responsible for passing a valid git_buf and continuing to manage the lifetime of the git_buf struct. Specific postconditions (e.g., whether fields are reset) are not documented here and are therefore unknown.
requirements: buffer must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a git_buf structure.
The git_buf should be properly initialized (e.g., via GIT_BUF_INIT) or previously populated by a libgit2 function before disposal.
Only call on git_buf instances whose memory (buffer->ptr) is owned by libgit2 and intended to be released via git_buf_dispose; do not pass pointers to memory managed elsewhere.
Do not free the git_buf structure itself; this function only releases the internal buffer memory.
No error is reported (void return); callers cannot rely on return codes or errno for failure information.

functions.name: git_strarray_dispose
functions.description: Frees the strings contained within a git_strarray that was produced by libgit2 APIs. Intended to be called by users to release memory for arrays returned by the library. This function only frees the strings; it does not free the git_strarray struct itself. Typical usage: pass a git_strarray previously filled/returned by libgit2 when you are done with its string contents. After this call, the strings pointer(s) must not be accessed.
requirements: array must point to a valid git_strarray whose string elements were allocated/returned by libgit2 APIs.
array must be initialized (its fields set consistently as provided by libgit2); do not pass an uninitialized struct.
Do not use any string pointers from array after this call (they are freed).
This function does not free the git_strarray object itself; if you allocated the struct, you are responsible for freeing it separately.

functions.name: git_libgit2_init
functions.description: Initializes libgit2’s global state and threading. Must be called before any other libgit2 function. Can be called multiple times; returns the current initialization count (including this call) or an error code. Typical usage: call once at program startup (or per component that needs it), then balance with git_libgit2_shutdown calls when done.
requirements: Must be called before any other libgit2 function is used.
May be called multiple times; each successful call increases the internal init count.
Caller must eventually call git_libgit2_shutdown the same number of times as successful git_libgit2_init calls to fully deinitialize the library.
Caller must check the return value: non-negative indicates the current init count; an error code (implementation-defined) indicates failure.
Do not call other libgit2 APIs if initialization fails (i.e., if an error code is returned).
After the library has been fully shut down (count reaches zero), it must be re-initialized via git_libgit2_init before using libgit2 again.

functions.name: git_libgit2_shutdown
functions.description: Decrements libgit2’s global initialization count and performs cleanup of global state and threading when the count reaches zero. Returns the remaining initialization count after this call or an error code. Call this as many times as git_libgit2_init was successfully called.
requirements: Should be called to balance each successful call to git_libgit2_init.
Must not be called more times than git_libgit2_init has been successfully called (doing so would violate the required pairing).
Caller must check the return value: non-negative indicates the remaining init count; an error code (implementation-defined) indicates failure.
Once the remaining count reaches zero, libgit2 is fully shut down; do not call other libgit2 APIs until re-initialized with git_libgit2_init.
Shutdown cleans up global state and threading context only when the init count reaches zero.

functions.name: git_annotated_commit_from_ref
functions.description: Create a git_annotated_commit representing the given reference in the specified repository. The result embeds how the commit was resolved (via a ref) and must later be released with git_annotated_commit_free. Use when you have a git_reference and want to preserve user intent (eg, merges showing the refname). Returns 0 on success, non-zero on error.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created git_annotated_commit*
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository that contains the reference
ref must be a valid git_reference belonging to repo
On success, the caller owns the resulting object and must call git_annotated_commit_free on *out
Callers must check the return value; non-zero indicates an error

functions.name: git_annotated_commit_from_fetchhead
functions.signature: int git_annotated_commit_from_fetchhead(git_annotated_commit **out, git_repository *repo, const char *branch_name, const char *remote_url, const git_oid *id);
functions.description: Create a git_annotated_commit from fetch-head information: the remote branch name, remote URL, and the fetched commit OID. The result captures how the commit was obtained (from fetchhead) and must be freed with git_annotated_commit_free. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on error.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created git_annotated_commit*
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository that contains the given commit
branch_name must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string naming the (remote) branch
remote_url must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string containing the remote URL
id must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid git_oid of the remote branch tip
On success, the caller owns the resulting object and must call git_annotated_commit_free on *out
Callers must check the return value; non-zero indicates an error

functions.name: git_annotated_commit_lookup
functions.description: Create a git_annotated_commit for the commit identified by id in repo. This variant records only the OID lookup (less context than from_ref or from_fetchhead). Prefer the more specific creators when possible. The result must be freed with git_annotated_commit_free. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on error.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created git_annotated_commit*
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository that contains the commit
id must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid git_oid present in repo
On success, the caller owns the resulting object and must call git_annotated_commit_free on *out
Callers must check the return value; non-zero indicates an error

functions.name: git_annotated_commit_from_revspec
functions.description: Create a git_annotated_commit by resolving a revision string (per gitrevisions syntax) in the given repository. Useful for user-entered revspecs like "HEAD~2". Result must be freed with git_annotated_commit_free. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on error.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created git_annotated_commit*
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository that contains the referenced commit(s)
revspec must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string that conforms to gitrevisions syntax
On success, the caller owns the resulting object and must call git_annotated_commit_free on *out
Callers must check the return value; non-zero indicates an error

functions.name: git_annotated_commit_id
functions.description: Return the commit ID (OID) that the annotated commit refers to. The returned pointer is to internal data and remains valid while the git_annotated_commit is alive.
requirements: commit must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid git_annotated_commit
The returned git_oid pointer must not be freed or modified by the caller
The returned pointer is only valid as long as commit remains alive

functions.name: git_annotated_commit_ref
functions.description: Return the refname associated with the annotated commit, if any (eg, the ref used to resolve it). Returns a const string owned by the annotated commit object.
requirements: commit must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid git_annotated_commit
The returned string pointer must not be freed or modified by the caller
The returned pointer is only valid as long as commit remains alive
If the annotated commit was not created from a ref, the presence or contents of this string may be unspecified (not documented)

functions.name: git_annotated_commit_free
functions.description: Free a git_annotated_commit previously created by one of the creator functions. Releases any resources held by the object.
requirements: commit must be a valid git_annotated_commit pointer previously obtained from a libgit2 creator for annotated commits
After this call, the commit pointer must not be used again

functions.name: git_apply_options_init
functions.description: Initialize a git_apply_options structure to default values. Typical usage is to declare a git_apply_options variable, then call this initializer with version set to GIT_APPLY_OPTIONS_VERSION before optionally customizing fields (callbacks, flags). Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
requirements: opts must be a valid, writable pointer to a git_apply_options structure.
version must be GIT_APPLY_OPTIONS_VERSION.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; -1 indicates failure.
If initialization succeeds, fields are set to default values equivalent to GIT_APPLY_OPTIONS_INIT.

functions.name: git_apply_to_tree
functions.signature: int git_apply_to_tree(git_index **out, git_repository *repo, git_tree *preimage, git_diff *diff, const git_apply_options *options);
functions.description: Apply a git_diff to a git_tree and produce the resulting postimage as a new in-memory index. Use when you want to preview or capture the result of applying a diff against a specific tree without modifying the working directory or existing index. Options may be NULL to use defaults; callbacks and flags in options can control per-delta/hunk decisions and check-only behavior.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to a git_index*; on success, *out is set to the resulting index.
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository.
preimage must be a valid git_tree to which the diff will be applied.
diff must be a valid git_diff describing changes to apply.
options may be NULL or a pointer to an initialized git_apply_options (initialized via GIT_APPLY_OPTIONS_INIT or git_apply_options_init).
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; a non-zero libgit2 error code indicates failure.
If options->flags includes GIT_APPLY_CHECK, no changes are produced beyond validation (behavior per libgit2); details beyond this flag are per the library.

functions.name: git_apply
functions.signature: int git_apply(git_repository *repo, git_diff *diff, git_apply_location_t location, const git_apply_options *options);
functions.description: Apply a git_diff to the given repository, making changes directly to the working directory, the index, or both, depending on location. Use to emulate `git apply` behavior programmatically. Options may be NULL for defaults; callbacks let you accept/reject individual deltas/hunks, and flags can request check-only validation.
requirements: repo must be a valid, opened git_repository to which the diff will be applied.
diff must be a valid git_diff describing the changes to apply.
location must be one of: GIT_APPLY_LOCATION_WORKDIR, GIT_APPLY_LOCATION_INDEX, or GIT_APPLY_LOCATION_BOTH.
options may be NULL or a pointer to an initialized git_apply_options (initialized via GIT_APPLY_OPTIONS_INIT or git_apply_options_init).
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; a non-zero libgit2 error code indicates failure.
If options->flags includes GIT_APPLY_CHECK, the operation validates applicability without making changes (equivalent to `git apply --check`).

functions.name: git_attr_value
functions.description: Return the classification of an attribute value string: TRUE, FALSE, STRING, or UNSPECIFIED. Use this to test results returned by attribute queries; if the type is STRING, the value itself is a standard NUL-terminated C string. Intended usage: call after getting an attribute value pointer from libgit2 to determine its state.
requirements: attr must be a valid NUL-terminated string pointer obtained from libgit2 attribute APIs or NULL to represent unspecified (in which case the function returns GIT_ATTR_VALUE_UNSPECIFIED).
Do not modify or free the string backing attr when it originates from libgit2 attribute APIs.

functions.name: git_attr_get
functions.signature: int git_attr_get(const char **value_out, git_repository *repo, uint32_t flags, const char *path, const char *name);
functions.description: Look up a single git attribute by name for a repository path, returning a pointer to the attribute value or a special state (TRUE, FALSE, or UNSPECIFIED) detectable via git_attr_value/GIT_ATTR_* macros. Use when you need one attribute for a single path.
requirements: value_out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the attribute value pointer; the returned pointer is owned by libgit2 and must not be modified or freed.
repo must be a valid, initialized git_repository instance.

flags is a combination of GIT_ATTR_CHECK_* flags controlling lookup source and order (e.g., GIT_ATTR_CHECK_FILE_THEN_INDEX, GIT_ATTR_CHECK_INDEX_ONLY, GIT_ATTR_CHECK_NO_SYSTEM, GIT_ATTR_CHECK_INCLUDE_HEAD/COMMIT).
path may be relative to the repository root; it need not exist. Non-existent paths are treated as plain files (not directories).
name must be a non-NULL attribute name string.
Return value: 0 on success; non-zero libgit2 error code on failure.

functions.name: git_attr_get_ext
functions.signature: int git_attr_get_ext(const char **value_out, git_repository *repo, git_attr_options *opts, const char *path, const char *name);
functions.description: Look up a single git attribute by name for a repository path, with extended options. Equivalent to git_attr_get but driven by a git_attr_options instance (flags and optional commit selection).
requirements: value_out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the attribute value pointer; the returned pointer is owned by libgit2 and must not be modified or freed.
repo must be a valid, initialized git_repository instance.
opts must be a non-NULL pointer to a properly initialized git_attr_options (initialize with GIT_ATTR_OPTIONS_INIT and set version to GIT_ATTR_OPTIONS_VERSION).
If opts->flags includes GIT_ATTR_CHECK_INCLUDE_COMMIT, set opts->attr_commit_id to the target commit (an oid) before the call.
path may be relative to the repository root; it need not exist. Non-existent paths are treated as plain files (not directories).
name must be a non-NULL attribute name string.
Return value: 0 on success; non-zero libgit2 error code on failure.

functions.name: git_attr_get_many
functions.signature: int git_attr_get_many(const char **values_out, git_repository *repo, uint32_t flags, const char *path, size_t num_attr, const char **names);
functions.description: Look up multiple git attributes for a path in a single call. More efficient than repeated git_attr_get calls. Each output entry can be inspected with git_attr_value/GIT_ATTR_* macros or used as a string when set to a value.
requirements: values_out must point to storage for at least num_attr entries; each entry will be set to a const char* owned by libgit2 and must not be modified or freed.
repo must be a valid, initialized git_repository instance.
flags is a combination of GIT_ATTR_CHECK_* flags controlling lookup source and order.
path may be relative to the repository root; it need not exist. Non-existent paths are treated as plain files (not directories).
num_attr specifies the number of attributes to query; must match the number of strings in names.
names must point to an array of num_attr NUL-terminated attribute name strings; none may be NULL.
Return value: 0 on success; non-zero libgit2 error code on failure.

functions.name: git_attr_get_many_ext
functions.signature: int git_attr_get_many_ext(const char **values_out, git_repository *repo, git_attr_options *opts, const char *path, size_t num_attr, const char **names);
functions.description: Look up multiple git attributes for a path with extended options. Equivalent to git_attr_get_many but driven by a git_attr_options instance.
requirements: values_out must point to storage for at least num_attr entries; each entry will be set to a const char* owned by libgit2 and must not be modified or freed.
repo must be a valid, initialized git_repository instance.
opts must be a non-NULL pointer to a properly initialized git_attr_options (initialize with GIT_ATTR_OPTIONS_INIT and set version to GIT_ATTR_OPTIONS_VERSION).
If opts->flags includes GIT_ATTR_CHECK_INCLUDE_COMMIT, set opts->attr_commit_id to the target commit (an oid) before the call.
path may be relative to the repository root; it need not exist. Non-existent paths are treated as plain files (not directories).
num_attr specifies the number of attributes to query; must match the number of strings in names.
names must point to an array of num_attr NUL-terminated attribute name strings; none may be NULL.
Return value: 0 on success; non-zero libgit2 error code on failure.

functions.name: git_attr_foreach
functions.signature: int git_attr_foreach(git_repository *repo, uint32_t flags, const char *path, git_attr_foreach_cb callback, void *payload);
functions.description: Iterate over all effective git attributes for a given path, invoking a callback once per attribute name with its highest-priority value. Use to enumerate attributes affecting a path.
requirements: repo must be a valid, initialized git_repository instance.
flags is a combination of GIT_ATTR_CHECK_* flags controlling lookup source and order.
path may be relative to the repository root; it need not exist. Non-existent paths are treated as plain files (not directories).
callback must be a valid function pointer; it will be invoked as callback(name, value, payload).
In the callback, value may be NULL when the attribute is explicitly UNSPECIFIED (via '!').
Callback return: return 0 to continue; any non-zero value stops iteration and is propagated as the function's return value.
Any name/value strings passed to the callback are owned by libgit2; do not modify or free them.
Return value: 0 on complete successful iteration, a non-zero value if the callback stopped iteration, or a libgit2 error code on failure before/within iteration.

functions.name: git_attr_foreach_ext
functions.signature: int git_attr_foreach_ext(git_repository *repo, git_attr_options *opts, const char *path, git_attr_foreach_cb callback, void *payload);
functions.description: Iterate over all effective git attributes for a path with extended options. Equivalent to git_attr_foreach but driven by a git_attr_options instance.
requirements: repo must be a valid, initialized git_repository instance.
opts must be a non-NULL pointer to a properly initialized git_attr_options (initialize with GIT_ATTR_OPTIONS_INIT and set version to GIT_ATTR_OPTIONS_VERSION).
If opts->flags includes GIT_ATTR_CHECK_INCLUDE_COMMIT, set opts->attr_commit_id to the target commit (an oid) before the call.
path may be relative to the repository root; it need not exist. Non-existent paths are treated as plain files (not directories).
callback must be a valid function pointer; it will be invoked as callback(name, value, payload).
In the callback, value may be NULL when the attribute is explicitly UNSPECIFIED (via '!').
Callback return: return 0 to continue; any non-zero value stops iteration and is propagated as the function's return value.
Any name/value strings passed to the callback are owned by libgit2; do not modify or free them.
Return value: 0 on complete successful iteration, a non-zero value if the callback stopped iteration, or a libgit2 error code on failure before/within iteration.

functions.name: git_attr_cache_flush
functions.description: Flush (invalidate) the repository’s gitattributes cache so that subsequent attribute queries reload from disk. Use after external changes to attribute files.
requirements: repo must be a valid, initialized git_repository instance.
Return value: 0 on success; non-zero libgit2 error code on failure.

functions.name: git_attr_add_macro
functions.signature: int git_attr_add_macro(git_repository *repo, const char *name, const char *values);
functions.description: Register an attribute macro in the repository (in addition to built-ins and those in the top-level .gitattributes). For example, add a "binary" macro like "-diff -crlf". Use when you need custom attribute shorthands.
requirements: repo must be a valid, initialized git_repository instance.
name must be a non-NULL macro name string.
values must be a non-NULL macro expansion string containing attribute settings.
Return value: 0 on success; non-zero libgit2 error code on failure.

functions.name: git_blame_options_init
functions.description: Initialize a git_blame_options structure to its default values. Use this before calling blame APIs. Pass GIT_BLAME_OPTIONS_VERSION for version. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
requirements: opts must be a valid, writable pointer to a git_blame_options struct
version must be GIT_BLAME_OPTIONS_VERSION
Check the return value: 0 indicates success; nonzero indicates failure

functions.name: git_blame_linecount
functions.description: Return the number of lines described by a blame result object.
requirements: blame must be a valid git_blame pointer previously returned by git_blame_file, git_blame_file_from_buffer, or git_blame_buffer

functions.name: git_blame_hunkcount
functions.description: Return the number of hunks in a blame result object.
requirements: blame must be a valid git_blame pointer previously returned by git_blame_file, git_blame_file_from_buffer, or git_blame_buffer

functions.name: git_blame_hunk_byindex
functions.description: Retrieve the blame hunk at the specified zero-based index. Returns NULL on error.
requirements: blame must be a valid git_blame pointer
index must be less than git_blame_hunkcount(blame)
Caller must check for a NULL return to detect errors or out-of-range access

functions.name: git_blame_hunk_byline
functions.description: Retrieve the blame hunk that covers the specified line number in the newest version of the file. Line numbers are 1-based. Returns NULL on error.
requirements: blame must be a valid git_blame pointer
lineno is 1-based and should refer to an existing line (1 <= lineno <= git_blame_linecount(blame))
Caller must check for a NULL return to detect errors or out-of-range input

functions.name: git_blame_line_byindex
functions.description: Retrieve information about a specific blamed line by 1-based index. Returns NULL on error.
requirements: blame must be a valid git_blame pointer
idx is 1-based and should refer to an existing line (1 <= idx <= git_blame_linecount(blame))
Caller must check for a NULL return to detect errors or out-of-range input

functions.name: git_blame_get_hunk_count
functions.description: Deprecated alias for git_blame_hunkcount. Returns the number of hunks in a blame result object.
requirements: blame must be a valid git_blame pointer
Prefer git_blame_hunkcount for new code

functions.name: git_blame_get_hunk_byindex
functions.description: Deprecated alias for git_blame_hunk_byindex. Retrieve the blame hunk at the specified zero-based index. Returns NULL on error.
requirements: blame must be a valid git_blame pointer
index must be less than git_blame_get_hunk_count(blame)
Caller must check for a NULL return

functions.name: git_blame_get_hunk_byline
functions.description: Deprecated alias for git_blame_hunk_byline. Retrieve the blame hunk that covers the specified 1-based line number. Returns NULL on error.
requirements: blame must be a valid git_blame pointer
lineno is 1-based and should be within the blamed file’s line range
Caller must check for a NULL return

functions.name: git_blame_file
functions.signature: int git_blame_file(git_blame **out, git_repository *repo, const char *path, git_blame_options *options);
functions.description: Compute blame information for a single file in a repository’s history. On success, stores a newly allocated git_blame object in *out. Options may be NULL to use defaults. Returns 0 on success; nonzero error code otherwise.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the allocated git_blame*
repo must be a valid git_repository pointer
path must be a non-NULL C string path to the file within the repository
options may be NULL to use defaults; if non-NULL, it should be initialized (e.g., via git_blame_options_init)
On success, caller is responsible for freeing *out with git_blame_free
Caller must check the integer return value for success or failure

functions.name: git_blame_file_from_buffer
functions.signature: int git_blame_file_from_buffer(git_blame **out, git_repository *repo, const char *path, const char *contents, size_t contents_len, git_blame_options *options);
functions.description: Compute blame information for a file using the given buffer as the file’s uncommitted working directory contents. On success, stores a newly allocated git_blame object in *out. Returns 0 on success; nonzero error code otherwise.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the allocated git_blame*
repo must be a valid git_repository pointer
path must be a non-NULL C string path to the file within the repository
contents must point to a buffer of at least contents_len bytes representing the in-memory file contents
contents_len must be the size in bytes of contents
options may be NULL to use defaults; if non-NULL, it should be initialized (e.g., via git_blame_options_init)
On success, caller is responsible for freeing *out with git_blame_free
Caller must check the integer return value for success or failure

functions.name: git_blame_buffer
functions.signature: int git_blame_buffer(git_blame **out, git_blame *base, const char *buffer, size_t buffer_len);
functions.description: Produce blame data for a file that has been modified in memory, using a precomputed base blame from the object database history. Differences from the committed version are marked with a zero OID in final_commit_id. Returns 0 on success; nonzero error code otherwise (use git_error_last for details).
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the resulting git_blame*
base must be a valid blame object for the file’s history (typically the output of git_blame_file)
buffer must point to a memory region of at least buffer_len bytes containing the modified file contents
buffer_len specifies the number of valid bytes in buffer
On success, caller is responsible for freeing *out with git_blame_free
Caller must check the integer return value for success or failure; use git_error_last for error information as documented

functions.name: git_blame_free
functions.description: Free a git_blame object previously created by git_blame_file, git_blame_file_from_buffer, or git_blame_buffer. After this call, the blame object must not be used.
requirements: blame must be a git_blame pointer previously returned by git_blame_file, git_blame_file_from_buffer, or git_blame_buffer
Do not use the blame object after freeing it

functions.name: git_blob_lookup
functions.description: Lookup a blob object by OID in the given repository and return it via the output parameter. Callers should release the returned blob with git_blob_free when finished.
requirements: blob must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the looked up blob
repo must be a valid repository handle
id must point to a valid git_oid for the target blob
Returns 0 on success; non-zero error code on failure
The returned blob must be freed with git_blob_free to avoid memory leaks

functions.name: git_blob_lookup_prefix
functions.signature: int git_blob_lookup_prefix(git_blob **blob, git_repository *repo, const git_oid *id, size_t len);
functions.description: Lookup a blob object by a short identifier (OID prefix) in the given repository. On success, returns the matching blob via the output parameter. Free the blob with git_blob_free when done.
requirements: blob must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the looked up blob
repo must be a valid repository handle
id must point to a git_oid containing the identifier prefix
len specifies the length of the short identifier prefix
Returns 0 on success; non-zero error code on failure
The returned blob must be freed with git_blob_free to avoid memory leaks

functions.name: git_blob_free
functions.description: Close and free a blob object. Wrapper around git_object_free. Necessary to call when you stop using a blob to avoid memory leaks.
requirements: Call this when you are done with a blob to avoid memory leaks
blob should be a blob previously obtained from libgit2 APIs such as lookup or duplicate

functions.name: git_blob_id
functions.description: Get the OID (SHA-1/ID) of a previously loaded blob. The returned pointer is owned by the blob and should be treated as read-only.
requirements: blob must be a previously loaded blob
The returned pointer is not to be freed or modified by the caller

functions.name: git_blob_owner
functions.description: Return the repository that contains the given blob.
requirements: blob must be a previously loaded blob

functions.name: git_blob_rawcontent
functions.description: Return a read-only pointer to the raw contents of the blob. The memory is owned internally and may be invalidated later; do not free it.
requirements: blob must be a valid, previously loaded blob
The returned buffer is read-only and must not be modified or freed by the caller
The returned pointer may be invalidated later; copy the data if you need to keep it independently

functions.name: git_blob_rawsize
functions.description: Return the size in bytes of the blob’s contents.
requirements: blob must be a valid, previously loaded blob

functions.name: git_blob_filter_options_init
functions.description: Initialize a git_blob_filter_options structure with default values. Equivalent to assigning GIT_BLOB_FILTER_OPTIONS_INIT.
requirements: opts must point to a git_blob_filter_options structure to initialize
version should be GIT_BLOB_FILTER_OPTIONS_VERSION
Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure

functions.name: git_blob_filter
functions.signature: int git_blob_filter(git_buf *out, git_blob *blob, const char *as_path, git_blob_filter_options *opts);
functions.description: Populate a git_buf with the filtered content of a blob as if checking it out at the given path. Applies CRLF and attribute-based filters. If no filters apply, the buffer may reference the blob’s internal data; dispose the buffer when done.
requirements: out must be a valid git_buf to be filled; the caller must dispose it via git_buf_dispose when done
blob must be a valid blob to filter
as_path is used for attribute lookups (path context)
opts controls filtering behavior; initialize with GIT_BLOB_FILTER_OPTIONS_INIT or git_blob_filter_options_init
If no filters apply, out may reference the blob’s internal data; in that case, do not free the blob until done with out or copy the data
Returns 0 on success; non-zero error code on failure

functions.name: git_blob_create_from_workdir
functions.description: Read a file from a repository’s working directory and write it as a blob to the object database. Returns the new blob’s OID in id.
requirements: id must be a valid pointer to receive the new blob id
repo must be a valid repository; this repository cannot be bare
relative_path must point to a file path relative to the repository’s working directory
Returns 0 on success; non-zero error code on failure

functions.name: git_blob_create_from_disk
functions.description: Read a file from the filesystem (not necessarily in the repo workdir) and write it as a blob to the repository’s object database. Returns the new blob’s OID in id.
requirements: id must be a valid pointer to receive the new blob id
repo must be a valid repository; it may be bare or non-bare
path must point to the filesystem path of the file to store
Returns 0 on success; non-zero error code on failure

functions.name: git_blob_create_from_stream
functions.description: Create a writable stream to build and filter a new blob into the object database. If hintpath is provided, it is used to determine which filters to apply. Do not close the stream directly; finalize with git_blob_create_from_stream_commit.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the created git_writestream
repo must be a valid repository (bare or non-bare) where the blob will be written
If hintpath is not NULL, it will be used to select and apply data filters
Do not close/free the stream directly; pass it to git_blob_create_from_stream_commit to finalize
Returns 0 on success; non-zero error code on failure

functions.name: git_blob_create_from_stream_commit
functions.description: Close the given stream and finalize writing the blob to the object database, returning the new blob’s OID. The stream is closed and freed by this call.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the new blob id
stream must be a stream obtained from git_blob_create_from_stream and not already closed
This call will close and free stream
Returns 0 on success; non-zero error code on failure

functions.name: git_blob_create_from_buffer
functions.signature: int git_blob_create_from_buffer(git_oid *id, git_repository *repo, const void *buffer, size_t len);
functions.description: Write the given in-memory buffer as a blob to the repository’s object database and return its OID.
requirements: id must be a valid pointer to receive the new blob id
repo must be a valid repository where the blob will be written
buffer must point to the data to store; len is its length in bytes
Returns 0 on success; non-zero error code on failure

functions.name: git_blob_is_binary
functions.description: Heuristically determine if the blob’s content is binary (per core git’s detection). Returns 1 if binary; 0 otherwise.
requirements: blob must be a valid blob whose content will be analyzed
Returns 1 if detected as binary; 0 otherwise

functions.name: git_blob_data_is_binary
functions.description: Heuristically determine if the given raw data is binary (same logic as git_blob_is_binary). Returns 1 if binary; 0 otherwise.
requirements: data must point to the bytes to analyze; len is the number of bytes
Returns 1 if detected as binary; 0 otherwise

functions.name: git_blob_dup
functions.description: Create an in-memory copy of a blob and return it via out. The copy must be explicitly freed with git_blob_free.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the duplicated blob
source must be a valid blob to copy
The returned blob must be freed with git_blob_free to avoid memory leaks
Returns 0

functions.name: git_branch_create
functions.signature: int git_branch_create(git_reference **out, git_repository *repo, const char *branch_name, const git_commit *target, int force)
functions.description: Create a new local branch reference pointing at a target commit. If force is nonzero and a branch with the given name already exists, it will be replaced. The resulting reference must be freed by the caller (git_reference_free). Branch names are validated per refname rules (see git_tag_create rules). Returns 0 on success or an error code (e.g., GIT_EINVALIDSPEC).
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created git_reference*
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository
branch_name must be a valid branch name; must not conflict with an existing branch name unless force != 0
target must be a valid git_commit that belongs to repo
Caller must free the returned git_reference via git_reference_free on success
Caller must check the return value for errors (nonzero indicates failure)

functions.name: git_branch_create_from_annotated
functions.signature: int git_branch_create_from_annotated(git_reference **ref_out, git_repository *repo, const char *branch_name, const git_annotated_commit *target, int force)
functions.description: Create a new local branch from an annotated commit, preserving the original revision string for reflog messages. Semantics are otherwise the same as git_branch_create. The returned reference must be freed by the caller.
requirements: ref_out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created git_reference*
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository
branch_name must be a valid branch name; must not conflict with an existing branch name unless force != 0
target must be a valid git_annotated_commit that belongs to repo
Caller must free the returned git_reference via git_reference_free on success
Caller must check the return value for errors (nonzero indicates failure)

functions.name: git_branch_delete
functions.description: Delete an existing branch reference. On success, the provided reference object becomes invalid and should be freed immediately by the caller with git_reference_free.
requirements: branch must be a valid git_reference representing a branch
On success, branch becomes invalid; caller should call git_reference_free promptly and must not use it thereafter
Caller must check the return value for errors (0 indicates success)

functions.name: git_branch_iterator_new
functions.description: Create an iterator over branches in a repository, filtered by list_flags (GIT_BRANCH_LOCAL, GIT_BRANCH_REMOTE, or GIT_BRANCH_ALL). The iterator must be freed with git_branch_iterator_free.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created git_branch_iterator*
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository
list_flags must be one of GIT_BRANCH_LOCAL, GIT_BRANCH_REMOTE, or GIT_BRANCH_ALL
Caller must free the iterator with git_branch_iterator_free when done
Caller must check the return value for errors

functions.name: git_branch_next
functions.description: Advance the branch iterator to retrieve the next branch. Returns 0 on success, GIT_ITEROVER when there are no more branches, or an error code. The returned git_reference must be freed by the caller.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive a git_reference* for the branch
out_type must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the branch type (local or remote-tracking)
iter must be a valid git_branch_iterator created by git_branch_iterator_new
On success, caller must free the returned git_reference via git_reference_free
Caller must handle GIT_ITEROVER return specially to detect end of iteration and must not treat it as an error

functions.name: git_branch_iterator_free
functions.description: Free a branch iterator created by git_branch_iterator_new. Safe to call with a valid iterator pointer. Unknown whether NULL is permitted; typical libgit2 patterns allow NULL, but this header does not state it.
requirements: iter must be an iterator previously created by git_branch_iterator_new
Caller should not use iter after freeing it

functions.name: git_branch_move
functions.signature: int git_branch_move(git_reference **out, git_reference *branch, const char *new_branch_name, int force)
functions.description: Rename or move an existing local branch to a new name. If force is nonzero and a branch with the new name exists, it will be overwritten. On success, the old reference becomes invalid and should be freed; a new reference with the updated name is returned and must be freed by the caller.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the new git_reference*
branch must be the current underlying git_reference of the branch to move
new_branch_name must be a valid branch name
If force is 0, new_branch_name must not conflict with an existing branch
On success, the old branch reference becomes invalid; caller should free it and must not use it
Caller must free the returned git_reference via git_reference_free
Caller must check the return value for errors (e.g., GIT_EINVALIDSPEC)

functions.name: git_branch_lookup
functions.signature: int git_branch_lookup(git_reference **out, git_repository *repo, const char *branch_name, git_branch_t branch_type)
functions.description: Look up a branch by name and type in a repository and return its reference. The returned reference must be freed by the caller. Branch names are validated. Returns 0 on success, GIT_ENOTFOUND if no match exists, GIT_EINVALIDSPEC, or another error code.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the git_reference*
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository
branch_name must be a valid branch name for the specified type
branch_type must be GIT_BRANCH_LOCAL or GIT_BRANCH_REMOTE
Caller must free the returned git_reference via git_reference_free on success
Caller must check the return value and handle GIT_ENOTFOUND

functions.name: git_branch_name
functions.description: Given a reference that is a branch (refs/heads/* or refs/remotes/*), return the branch name component. The returned pointer is owned by ref; do not free it. Returns 0 on success, GIT_EINVALID if ref is not a local or remote branch, or another error code.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive a const char*
ref must be a valid git_reference that is a branch under refs/heads/ or refs/remotes/
The returned string is owned by ref; caller must not free or modify it and must keep ref alive while using it
Caller must check the return value for errors (e.g., GIT_EINVALID)

functions.name: git_branch_upstream
functions.description: Get the upstream (remote-tracking) branch for a local branch. Returns a new reference for the tracking branch, which must be freed by the caller. Returns 0 on success, GIT_ENOTFOUND if there is no remote-tracking reference, or another error code.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the upstream git_reference*
branch must be a valid git_reference to a local branch
Caller must free the returned git_reference via git_reference_free on success
Caller must check for GIT_ENOTFOUND and other errors

functions.name: git_branch_set_upstream
functions.description: Configure or unset the upstream branch for a local branch by updating repository configuration. Pass NULL for branch_name to unset. The actual tracking reference must already exist for the operation to succeed.
requirements: branch must be a valid git_reference to a local branch
branch_name may be NULL to unset upstream; otherwise must name an existing remote-tracking or local branch
The tracking reference for branch_name must already exist
Caller must check the return value for errors, including GIT_ENOTFOUND if no branch named branch_name exists

functions.name: git_branch_upstream_name
functions.description: Compute the full reference name of a local branch’s upstream (remote-tracking) branch and write it into out (e.g., refs/remotes/origin/feature/nice). Returns 0 on success, GIT_ENOTFOUND if no remote tracking reference exists, or an error code.
requirements: out must be a valid, initialized git_buf to receive the name
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository
refname must be the reference name of a local branch (full name, e.g., refs/heads/feature)
Caller must check the return value and handle GIT_ENOTFOUND

functions.name: git_branch_is_head
functions.description: Determine whether HEAD points to the given local branch. Returns 1 if HEAD points at the branch, 0 if not, or a negative value on error.
requirements: branch must be a valid git_reference to a local branch
Caller must check for negative return values as error codes

functions.name: git_branch_is_checked_out
functions.description: Determine whether any HEAD (including from linked repositories/worktrees) points to the specified local branch. Returns 1 if checked out, 0 if not, or an error code otherwise.
requirements: branch must be a valid git_reference to a local branch
Caller must check the return value; nonnegative values indicate boolean result, negative indicates error

functions.name: git_branch_remote_name
functions.description: Given the full name of a remote-tracking branch, write the remote’s name that matches its fetch refspec into out (e.g., "refs/remotes/test/master" -> "test"). If refspecs from multiple remotes match, returns GIT_EAMBIGUOUS. Returns 0 on success, GIT_ENOTFOUND when no matching remote was found, GIT_EAMBIGUOUS on ambiguity, or another error code.
requirements: out must be a valid, initialized git_buf to receive the remote name
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository
refname must be the complete name of a remote-tracking branch (e.g., refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>)
Caller must check the return value and handle GIT_ENOTFOUND and GIT_EAMBIGUOUS

functions.name: git_branch_upstream_remote
functions.description: Retrieve the configured branch.*.remote for a given local branch and write it into buf. The branch must be local. Returns 0 on success or an error code.
requirements: buf must be a valid, initialized git_buf to receive the name
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository
refname must be the full name of a local branch
Caller must check the return value for errors

functions.name: git_branch_upstream_merge
functions.description: Retrieve the configured branch.*.merge (merge refspec target) for a given local branch and write it into buf. The branch must be local. Returns 0 on success or an error code.
requirements: buf must be a valid, initialized git_buf to receive the name
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository
refname must be the full name of a local branch
Caller must check the return value for errors

functions.name: git_branch_name_is_valid
functions.description: Validate a branch name. Determines whether the given name, when prefixed with refs/heads/, is a valid reference name and satisfies branch-specific restrictions (e.g., cannot start with '-'). Writes 1/0 to valid to indicate validity. Returns 0 on success or an error code.
requirements: valid must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the validity result (nonzero if valid, 0 if invalid)
name must be a non-NULL branch name to test (without refs/heads/ prefix)
Caller must check the function’s return value for errors before trusting valid

functions.name: git_checkout_options_init
functions.description: Initialize a git_checkout_options structure with default values. Use this before passing options to checkout routines. Pass GIT_CHECKOUT_OPTIONS_VERSION for version. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
requirements: opts must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to writable memory for a git_checkout_options structure.
version must be set to GIT_CHECKOUT_OPTIONS_VERSION.
Call this (or use GIT_CHECKOUT_OPTIONS_INIT) before using the options with checkout functions.
Check the integer return value: 0 indicates success; -1 indicates failure.

functions.name: git_checkout_head
functions.description: Update files in the index and working tree to match the commit pointed to by HEAD. This does not move HEAD; to switch branches, checkout the target then set HEAD separately. If provided, callbacks in opts can report/abort the operation. Returns 0 on success; may return GIT_EUNBORNBRANCH if HEAD points to a non-existing branch; non-zero return from notify_cb is propagated; other errors are < 0.
requirements: repo must be a non-bare repository (have a working directory).
opts may be NULL; if non-NULL, it should be initialized via GIT_CHECKOUT_OPTIONS_INIT or git_checkout_options_init.
Be prepared for the function to return a non-zero value from notify_cb (treated as cancellation) if a notify callback is supplied in opts.
On error, consult git_error_last for details as return codes < 0 indicate errors.

functions.name: git_checkout_index
functions.description: Update files in the working tree to match the content of the index. If index is NULL, the repository’s index is used. Callbacks in opts can report/abort the operation. Returns 0 on success; non-zero return from notify_cb is propagated; other errors are < 0.
requirements: repo must be a non-bare repository (have a working directory).
index may be NULL to use the repository index; otherwise it must be a valid git_index pointer (ownership/association not stated in this header).
opts may be NULL; if non-NULL, it should be initialized via GIT_CHECKOUT_OPTIONS_INIT or git_checkout_options_init.
Be prepared for the function to return a non-zero value from notify_cb (treated as cancellation) if a notify callback is supplied in opts.
On error, consult git_error_last for details as return codes < 0 indicate errors.

functions.name: git_checkout_tree
functions.signature: int git_checkout_tree(git_repository *repo, const git_object *treeish, const git_checkout_options *opts);
functions.description: Update files in the index and working tree to match the content of the tree pointed to by treeish. treeish may be a commit, tag, or tree; if NULL, HEAD is used. Callbacks in opts can report/abort the operation. Returns 0 on success; non-zero return from notify_cb is propagated; other errors are < 0.
requirements: repo must be a non-bare repository (have a working directory).
treeish may be NULL to use HEAD, or must be a valid git_object that is a commit, tag, or tree.
opts may be NULL; if non-NULL, it should be initialized via GIT_CHECKOUT_OPTIONS_INIT or git_checkout_options_init.
Be prepared for the function to return a non-zero value from notify_cb (treated as cancellation) if a notify callback is supplied in opts.
On error, consult git_error_last for details as return codes < 0 indicate errors.

functions.name: git_cherrypick_options_init
functions.description: Initialize a git_cherrypick_options struct with default values. Typical usage is to pass a writable options struct and GIT_CHERRYPICK_OPTIONS_VERSION to obtain defaults equivalent to GIT_CHERRYPICK_OPTIONS_INIT.
requirements: opts must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a writable git_cherrypick_options structure.
version should be GIT_CHERRYPICK_OPTIONS_VERSION.
Caller must check the return value; 0 indicates success, -1 indicates failure. On failure, the contents of opts are unspecified and should not be used.

functions.name: git_cherrypick_commit
functions.signature: int git_cherrypick_commit(git_index **out, git_repository *repo, git_commit *cherrypick_commit, git_commit *our_commit, unsigned int mainline, const git_merge_options *merge_options);
functions.description: Cherry-pick the changes from cherrypick_commit onto our_commit within repo, producing a git_index that reflects the result. The resulting index must be freed by the caller with git_index_free. Use when you want the cherry-pick result as an in-memory index without updating the working directory.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer; on success, *out receives a newly allocated git_index that the caller must free with git_index_free.
repo must be a valid repository that contains the given commits.
cherrypick_commit must be a valid git_commit object (expected to belong to repo).
our_commit must be a valid git_commit object (expected to belong to repo).
mainline identifies the parent of cherrypick_commit to treat as the mainline if cherrypick_commit is a merge; otherwise it is not used.
merge_options may be NULL to use defaults; if non-NULL, it must point to a valid git_merge_options.
Caller must check the return value; 0 indicates success, -1 indicates failure. On failure, do not use *out.

functions.name: git_cherrypick
functions.description: Cherry-pick the given commit into repo, applying changes to the index and working directory. Use this to perform a full cherry-pick operation that updates the checkout according to the supplied options (or defaults).
requirements: repo must be a valid repository to apply the cherry-pick to.
commit must be a valid git_commit to cherry-pick (expected to belong to repo).
cherrypick_options may be NULL to use defaults; if non-NULL, it must point to a properly initialized git_cherrypick_options (e.g., via git_cherrypick_options_init or GIT_CHERRYPICK_OPTIONS_INIT).
This function produces changes in the repository’s index and working directory; callers should be prepared for these modifications.
Caller must check the return value; 0 indicates success, -1 indicates failure.

functions.name: git_clone_options_init
functions.description: Initialize a git_clone_options structure with libgit2’s default values. Use this prior to calling git_clone if you want to customize clone behavior. Pass GIT_CLONE_OPTIONS_VERSION as the version. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure. Intended usage: declare a git_clone_options variable, call git_clone_options_init(&opts, GIT_CLONE_OPTIONS_VERSION), optionally tweak fields (checkout_opts, fetch_opts, bare, local, checkout_branch, repository_cb, remote_cb, and payloads), then pass &opts to git_clone.
requirements: opts must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to writable memory.
version should be GIT_CLONE_OPTIONS_VERSION (currently 1).
On success, opts->checkout_opts and opts->fetch_opts are initialized to their respective library defaults (per GIT_CHECKOUT_OPTIONS_INIT and GIT_FETCH_OPTIONS_INIT).
Callers should check the return value (0 indicates success, -1 failure).
If initialization fails, do not use opts with git_clone until it is successfully initialized.

functions.name: git_clone
functions.signature: int git_clone(git_repository **out, const char *url, const char *local_path, const git_clone_options *options);
functions.description: Clone a remote repository into a new local repository at local_path. By default, creates the repository and initial remote matching git’s defaults; behavior can be customized via options (checkout/fetch options, bare/local mode, branch to checkout, and optional callbacks to create the repository and remote). Returns 0 on success; otherwise returns a negative error code or propagates a non-zero value returned by user callbacks. Intended usage: ensure libgit2 is initialized (git_libgit2_init), prepare optional git_clone_options (via GIT_CLONE_OPTIONS_INIT or git_clone_options_init), then call git_clone(&repo, url, local_path, &opts or NULL).
requirements: libgit2 must be initialized via git_libgit2_init before calling this function.
out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer; on success, *out receives the resulting git_repository object.
url must be a valid, non-NULL string naming the remote repository to clone (e.g., HTTPS/SSH, local path, or file://).
local_path must be a valid, non-NULL path to a directory location where the repository will be created.
options may be NULL; if non-NULL, options->version should be GIT_CLONE_OPTIONS_VERSION.

If options is provided, any embedded callbacks (repository_cb, remote_cb) must adhere to their documented signatures and return 0 on success; non-zero values may abort the clone and be returned by git_clone.
If options->checkout_opts disables checkout (e.g., GIT_CHECKOUT_NONE or GIT_CHECKOUT_DRY_RUN), no working directory checkout will occur.
If options->checkout_branch is NULL, the remote’s default branch will be used; otherwise it should name a branch.
The bare flag, local transport mode, and other fields in options must be set to meaningful values if customized (bare is 0 for standard repo, non-zero for bare; local is one of git_clone_local_t).
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success; a negative value indicates error; non-zero values from callbacks may be returned as-is.
Resource ownership: on success, the caller is responsible for managing and eventually freeing the returned repository object via the appropriate libgit2 API (inferred from libgit2 conventions).

functions.name: git_commit_lookup
functions.signature:
GIT_EXTERN(int) git_commit_lookup(
	git_commit **commit, git_repository *repo, const git_oid *id);
functions.description: Lookup a commit object by oid in the given repository. If id identifies an annotated tag, it will be peeled to the underlying commit. Caller must free the resulting git_commit with git_commit_free.
requirements: commit must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the result
repo must be a valid, initialized git_repository
id must point to a valid git_oid
On success, the returned commit must be released with git_commit_free
Returns 0 on success or an error code on failure

functions.name: git_commit_lookup_prefix
functions.signature:
GIT_EXTERN(int) git_commit_lookup_prefix(
	git_commit **commit, git_repository *repo, const git_oid *id, size_t len);
functions.description: Lookup a commit by a short object id prefix in the repository. If the id refers to an annotated tag, it will be peeled to the commit. Caller must free the resulting git_commit with git_commit_free.
requirements: commit must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the result
repo must be a valid, initialized git_repository
id must point to a git_oid containing the object id whose first len bytes are used as prefix
len is the length of the short identifier prefix
On success, the returned commit must be released with git_commit_free
Returns 0 on success or an error code on failure

functions.name: git_commit_free
functions.description: Release a commit object previously obtained from libgit2 (wrapper around git_object_free). Prevents memory leaks.
requirements: commit may be NULL (no effect) or a commit previously returned by libgit2
Must be called when finished using a git_commit to avoid memory leaks

functions.name: git_commit_id
functions.description: Get the object id (OID) of a previously loaded commit.
requirements: commit must be a valid, previously loaded git_commit
Returns a pointer to an internal git_oid; do not free or modify it

functions.name: git_commit_owner
functions.description: Get the repository that owns the given commit.
requirements: commit must be a valid, previously loaded git_commit
Returned git_repository is owned by libgit2; do not free it

functions.name: git_commit_message_encoding
functions.description: Get the message encoding name from the commit’s headers. May be NULL if missing, in which case UTF-8 is assumed.
requirements: commit must be a valid git_commit
Returned string is owned by the commit; do not free or modify it
May return NULL if no encoding header is present

functions.name: git_commit_message
functions.description: Get the full, slightly prettified commit message (leading newlines removed).
requirements: commit must be a valid git_commit
Returned string is owned by the commit; do not free or modify it

functions.name: git_commit_message_raw
functions.description: Get the full raw commit message without prettification.
requirements: commit must be a valid git_commit
Returned string is owned by the commit; do not free or modify it

functions.name: git_commit_summary
functions.description: Get the short summary (first paragraph) of the commit message with whitespace trimmed and squashed.
requirements: commit must be a valid git_commit
Returns NULL on error

functions.name: git_commit_body
functions.description: Get the body (everything after the first paragraph) of the commit message with leading/trailing whitespace trimmed.
requirements: commit must be a valid git_commit
Returns NULL when the message only consists of a summary

functions.name: git_commit_time
functions.description: Get the committer timestamp of the commit.
requirements: commit must be a valid git_commit

functions.name: git_commit_time_offset
functions.description: Get the committer’s timezone offset in minutes from UTC.
requirements: commit must be a valid git_commit

functions.name: git_commit_committer
functions.description: Get the committer signature embedded in the commit.
requirements: commit must be a valid git_commit
Returned git_signature pointer is owned by the commit; do not free or modify it

functions.name: git_commit_author
functions.description: Get the author signature embedded in the commit.
requirements: commit must be a valid git_commit
Returned git_signature pointer is owned by the commit; do not free or modify it

functions.name: git_commit_committer_with_mailmap
functions.signature:
GIT_EXTERN(int) git_commit_committer_with_mailmap(
	git_signature **out, const git_commit *commit, const git_mailmap *mailmap);
functions.description: Resolve the committer using the given mailmap to canonicalize name and email, returning a new signature. Caller must free the returned signature with git_signature_free.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the allocated git_signature
commit must be a valid git_commit
mailmap may be NULL to skip resolution or use defaults
On success, caller must free *out with git_signature_free
Returns 0 on success or an error code

functions.name: git_commit_author_with_mailmap
functions.signature:
GIT_EXTERN(int) git_commit_author_with_mailmap(
	git_signature **out, const git_commit *commit, const git_mailmap *mailmap);
functions.description: Resolve the author using the given mailmap to canonicalize name and email, returning a new signature. Caller must free the returned signature with git_signature_free.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the allocated git_signature
commit must be a valid git_commit
mailmap may be NULL to skip resolution or use defaults
On success, caller must free *out with git_signature_free
Returns 0 on success or an error code

functions.name: git_commit_raw_header
functions.description: Get the full raw commit header text.
requirements: commit must be a valid git_commit
Returned string is owned by the commit; do not free or modify it

functions.name: git_commit_tree
functions.description: Lookup and return the tree object pointed to by the commit. Caller must free the returned tree with git_tree_free (via git_object_free).
requirements: tree_out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the tree
commit must be a valid git_commit
On success, the returned git_tree must be freed by the caller
Returns 0 on success or an error code on failure

functions.name: git_commit_tree_id
functions.description: Get the id of the tree referenced by the commit without loading it from the object database.
requirements: commit must be a valid git_commit
Returned git_oid pointer is owned by the commit; do not free or modify it

functions.name: git_commit_parentcount
functions.description: Get the number of parent commits.
requirements: commit must be a valid git_commit

functions.name: git_commit_parent
functions.description: Get the nth parent commit of the given commit (0-based). Caller must free the returned parent with git_commit_free.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the parent commit
commit must be a valid git_commit
n must be in the range [0, git_commit_parentcount(commit) - 1]
On success, the returned parent commit must be released with git_commit_free
Returns 0 on success or an error code

functions.name: git_commit_parent_id
functions.description: Get the oid of the nth parent commit without loading the parent from the object database.
requirements: commit must be a valid git_commit
