n must be in the range [0, git_commit_parentcount(commit) - 1]
Returns NULL on error

functions.name: git_commit_nth_gen_ancestor
functions.description: Get the nth-generation ancestor by following only first parents. Passing n=0 returns another instance of the base commit. Caller must free the returned commit.
requirements: ancestor must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the ancestor
commit must be a valid git_commit
n specifies the generation to walk (0 for the same commit)
On success, caller must free the returned commit with git_commit_free
Returns 0 on success, GIT_ENOTFOUND if no matching ancestor exists, or an error code

functions.name: git_commit_header_field
functions.signature: GIT_EXTERN(int) git_commit_header_field(git_buf *out, const git_commit *commit, const char *field);
functions.description: Retrieve an arbitrary header field value from a commit into a git_buf, overwriting any existing content of the buffer.
requirements: out must be a valid git_buf; its existing contents will be overwritten
commit must be a valid git_commit
field must be a non-NULL header field name
Returns 0 on success, GIT_ENOTFOUND if the field does not exist, or an error code

functions.name: git_commit_extract_signature
functions.signature: GIT_EXTERN(int) git_commit_extract_signature(git_buf *signature, git_buf *signed_data, git_repository *repo, git_oid *commit_id, const char *field);
functions.description: Extract the signature block and the signed data from a commit. If field is NULL, the default 'gpgsig' is used. signature and signed_data buffers are overwritten with results.
requirements: signature must be a valid git_buf; its contents will be overwritten
signed_data must be a valid git_buf; its contents will be overwritten
repo must be a valid git_repository containing the commit
commit_id must point to the oid of the commit to inspect
field may be NULL to use the default 'gpgsig' field
Returns 0 on success; returns GIT_ENOTFOUND if the id is not a commit or the commit has no signature; sets error class GIT_ERROR_INVALID if id is not a commit and GIT_ERROR_OBJECT if no signature

functions.name: git_commit_create
functions.description: Create a new commit object in the repository from the given tree and parent commits and update a reference (e.g., HEAD) if requested. The commit is written to the object database; id receives the new oid.
requirements: id must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the new commit oid
repo must be a valid repository that owns tree and parents
update_ref may be NULL to avoid updating any reference; otherwise must be a valid reference name ("HEAD" allowed)
author must be a valid signature
committer must be a valid signature
message_encoding may be NULL to omit the encoding header (UTF-8 assumed)
message must be a non-NULL commit message string
tree must be a non-NULL git_tree owned by repo
parent_count specifies number of parents; may be 0 for a root commit
parents may be NULL only if parent_count == 0; otherwise it must point to an array of parent_count commits all owned by repo
If update_ref exists, the first parent must be the tip of that branch
Returns 0 on success or an error code

functions.name: git_commit_create_v
functions.description: Create a new commit using a variadic list of parent commit pointers (const git_commit*). Otherwise identical to git_commit_create.
requirements: id must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the new commit oid
repo must be a valid repository that owns tree and parents
update_ref may be NULL or a valid reference name; "HEAD" allowed
author must be a valid signature
committer must be a valid signature
message_encoding may be NULL (UTF-8 assumed)
message must be a non-NULL commit message string
tree must be a non-NULL git_tree owned by repo
parent_count specifies how many parent pointers follow in the varargs
The varargs must contain exactly parent_count items, each a (const git_commit *) owned by repo
If update_ref exists, the first parent must be the tip of that branch
Returns 0 on success or an error code
Note: variadic calling may be unsafe for some languages/FFIs

functions.name: git_commit_create_from_stage
functions.description: Commit the repository’s staged changes (akin to `git commit -m`). By default, empty commits are not allowed; this can be overridden via opts->allow_empty_commit.
requirements: id must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the new commit oid
repo must be a valid repository with staged changes to commit
message must be a non-NULL commit message
opts may be NULL or point to a properly initialized git_commit_create_options structure (use GIT_COMMIT_CREATE_OPTIONS_INIT)
Returns 0 on success, GIT_EUNCHANGED if there were no changes to commit, or an error code

functions.name: git_commit_amend
functions.description: Create a new commit that amends an existing commit by replacing only the non-NULL fields (author, committer, message_encoding, message, tree). Parents are copied from the original commit. Optionally update a reference as in git_commit_create.
requirements: id must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the new commit oid
commit_to_amend must be a valid commit
update_ref may be NULL to avoid ref updates; otherwise must be a valid reference name; if updating, the first parent must be the tip of the branch
author/committer/message_encoding/message/tree may be NULL to reuse values from commit_to_amend; non-NULL values must be valid
tree, if provided, must be owned by the same repository as commit_to_amend
Returns 0 on success or an error code

functions.name: git_commit_create_buffer
functions.description: Create a commit as with git_commit_create but write the commit object’s content into a buffer instead of the object database.
requirements: out must be a valid git_buf; its contents will be overwritten with the commit object content
repo must be a valid repository owning tree and parents
author must be a valid signature
committer must be a valid signature
message_encoding may be NULL (UTF-8 assumed)
message must be a non-NULL commit message
tree must be a non-NULL git_tree owned by repo
parent_count specifies number of parents; may be 0
parents may be NULL only if parent_count == 0; otherwise array of parent_count commits owned by repo
Returns 0 on success or an error code

functions.name: git_commit_create_with_signature
functions.description: Attach a signature to the given unsigned commit content, write the signed commit object to the repository, and return its id. If signature is NULL, no signature field is added. If signature_field is NULL, the default header "gpgsig" is used.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the new commit oid
repo must be a valid repository
commit_content must point to the exact content of an unsigned commit object
signature may be NULL to create a commit without adding a signature field; otherwise must be a signature string
signature_field may be NULL to use "gpgsig"; otherwise must be a header field name
Returns 0 on success or an error code

functions.name: git_commit_dup
functions.description: Create an in-memory duplicate of a commit. Caller must free the duplicate with git_commit_free.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the duplicated commit
source must be a valid git_commit
On success, caller must release *out with git_commit_free
Returns 0

functions.name: git_commitarray_dispose
functions.description: Free the commits contained in a git_commitarray provided by the library. Does not free the git_commitarray struct itself.
requirements: array must be a git_commitarray previously provided by the library
Caller should not attempt to free the array struct itself via this function; it only frees contained commits
Must be called to avoid memory leaks when given such arrays

functions.name: git_config_entry_free
functions.description: Free a git_config_entry previously obtained from libgit2 (for example via git_config_get_entry or an iterator).
requirements: entry may be NULL (safe to pass a NULL pointer in typical free-style APIs, but behavior is not explicitly documented).
Do not use the entry pointer after calling this function.

functions.name: git_config_find_global
functions.description: Locate the path to the user/global configuration file (typically $HOME/.gitconfig) if it exists and write it into out.
requirements: out must point to a valid, user-allocated git_buf to receive the path.
Returns 0 if a global configuration file has been found; nonzero on error or if not found.

functions.name: git_config_find_xdg
functions.description: Locate the path to the XDG-compatible configuration file (typically $HOME/.config/git/config) if it exists and write it into out.
requirements: out must point to a valid, user-allocated git_buf to receive the path.
Returns 0 if an XDG configuration file has been found; nonzero on error or if not found.

functions.name: git_config_find_system
functions.description: Locate the path to the system configuration file (usually /etc/gitconfig; on Windows may fall back to %PROGRAMFILES%\Git\etc\gitconfig) if it exists and write it into out.
requirements: out must point to a valid, user-allocated git_buf to receive the path.
Returns 0 if a system configuration file has been found; nonzero on error or if not found.

functions.name: git_config_find_programdata
functions.description: Locate the path to the ProgramData configuration file used by Portable Git on Windows (%PROGRAMDATA%\Git\config) if it exists and write it into out.
requirements: out must point to a valid, user-allocated git_buf to receive the path.
Returns 0 if a ProgramData configuration file has been found; nonzero on error or if not found.

functions.name: git_config_open_default
functions.description: Open a prioritized config that aggregates the global, XDG, and system configuration files for access outside a repository.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the created git_config*.
Returns 0 on success; nonzero on error.

functions.name: git_config_new
functions.description: Allocate a new, empty config object. Add one or more backends (e.g., on-disk files) before using it to read or write settings.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the created git_config*.
The returned config has no backends; callers must add at least one file/backend before operations that need storage.

functions.name: git_config_add_file_ondisk
functions.signature: int git_config_add_file_ondisk(git_config *cfg, const char *path, git_config_level_t level, const git_repository *repo, int force);
functions.description: Add an on-disk Git config file backend at path to cfg at the given priority level. The file is parsed if it exists; if it does not, it is added and will be created on first write. Supports conditional include parsing using repo.
requirements: cfg must be a valid config object created by libgit2.
path must be a valid filesystem path string; may point to a non-existent file (it will be created on first write).
level specifies the priority level; adding more than one file at the same level without force will fail with GIT_EEXISTS.
repo may be NULL; when non-NULL it enables parsing of conditional includes.
If force is non-zero, an existing file at the same level will be replaced.
Returns 0 on success; GIT_EEXISTS if a file already exists at the level and force is 0; GIT_ENOTFOUND when the file doesn't exist (as an error condition per docs) or other error codes.

functions.name: git_config_open_ondisk
functions.description: Create a config instance that contains a single on-disk file backend at path. Convenience wrapper for git_config_new + git_config_add_file_ondisk.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the created git_config*.
path must be a valid filesystem path string.
Returns 0 on success; nonzero on error.

functions.name: git_config_open_level
functions.signature: int git_config_open_level(git_config **out, const git_config *parent, git_config_level_t level);
functions.description: Create a single-level, focused config object that exposes only the specified level from a multi-level parent config for gets/sets/deletes.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the created git_config*.
parent must be a valid multi-level git_config containing the requested level.
level identifies the configuration level to focus on.
Returns 0 on success; returns GIT_ENOTFOUND if the level is not present; nonzero on other errors.
Multiple calls for the same level may return different config instances that share the same underlying config_file.

functions.name: git_config_open_global
functions.description: Open the global/XDG configuration file according to git’s rules for writing (prefers ~/.gitconfig unless the user has explicitly created the XDG file).
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the created git_config*.
config must be a valid config object used to locate the appropriate global/XDG file.
Returns 0 on success; nonzero on error.

functions.name: git_config_set_writeorder
functions.description: Specify the write ordering for configuration backends. This can differ from read ordering (e.g., worktree is high-priority for reads but not written unless chosen).
requirements: cfg must be a valid config object.
levels must point to an array of git_config_level_t values indicating desired write order; array length is len.
len must be the number of elements in levels.
Returns 0 on success; nonzero on error.

functions.name: git_config_snapshot
functions.description: Create a snapshot (read-only, consistent view) of config’s current state for complex lookups. Strings retrieved from a snapshot remain valid until the snapshot is freed.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the snapshot git_config*.
config must be a valid git_config.
Strings returned from queries against the snapshot are valid until the snapshot is freed; do not free them yourself.
Returns 0 on success; nonzero on error.

functions.name: git_config_free
functions.description: Free a git_config and associated resources/backends.
requirements: cfg may be NULL (common free-style behavior; not explicitly stated).
Do not use cfg after freeing.
Freeing a snapshot invalidates any strings previously returned by that snapshot.

functions.name: git_config_get_entry
functions.signature: int git_config_get_entry(git_config_entry **out, const git_config *cfg, const char *name);
functions.description: Retrieve the git_config_entry for a given key name from cfg. Caller must free the entry with git_config_entry_free.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the entry pointer.
cfg must be a valid config object.
name must be the key to query (normalized key format is used internally).
The returned entry must be freed with git_config_entry_free.
Returns 0 on success; nonzero on error.

functions.name: git_config_get_int32
functions.signature: int git_config_get_int32(int32_t *out, const git_config *cfg, const char *name);
functions.description: Get a 32-bit integer value of the first occurrence of a variable named name from cfg, respecting priority of config levels.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the value.
cfg must be a valid config object.
name must identify the config variable.
Returns 0 on success; nonzero on error.

functions.name: git_config_get_int64
functions.signature: int git_config_get_int64(int64_t *out, const git_config *cfg, const char *name);
functions.description: Get a 64-bit integer value of the first occurrence of a variable named name from cfg, respecting priority of config levels.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the value.
cfg must be a valid config object.
name must identify the config variable.
Returns 0 on success; nonzero on error.

functions.name: git_config_get_bool
functions.signature: int git_config_get_bool(int *out, const git_config *cfg, const char *name);
functions.description: Get a boolean value of the first occurrence of variable name from cfg. Uses C convention: 0 is false, non-zero is true.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the value.
cfg must be a valid config object.
name must identify the config variable.
Returns 0 on success; nonzero on error.

functions.name: git_config_get_path
functions.signature: int git_config_get_path(git_buf *out, const git_config *cfg, const char *name);
functions.description: Get a path value of variable name from cfg into out. A leading '~' is expanded to the global search path (usually the user’s home directory, but may be overridden via git_libgit2_opts).
requirements: out must point to a valid git_buf to receive the path.
cfg must be a valid config object.
name must identify the config variable.
Returns 0 on success; nonzero on error.

functions.name: git_config_get_string
functions.signature: int git_config_get_string(const char **out, const git_config *cfg, const char *name);
functions.description: Get a string value of variable name from a snapshot config. The returned pointer is owned by the config and remains valid until the config is freed; do not free it.
requirements: cfg must be a snapshot config object created by git_config_snapshot.
out must be a valid pointer to receive the string pointer.
name must identify the config variable.
Do not free or modify the returned string; it is valid until the snapshot is freed.
Returns 0 on success; nonzero on error.

functions.name: git_config_get_string_buf
functions.signature: int git_config_get_string_buf(git_buf *out, const git_config *cfg, const char *name);
functions.description: Get a string value of variable name from cfg and copy it into out.
requirements: out must be a valid git_buf to receive the copied string.
cfg must be a valid config object.
name must identify the config variable.
Returns 0 on success; nonzero on error.

functions.name: git_config_get_multivar_foreach
functions.signature: int git_config_get_multivar_foreach(const git_config *cfg, const char *name, const char *regexp, git_config_foreach_cb callback, void *payload);
functions.description: Enumerate each value of a multivar named name and invoke callback for each one that matches regexp. Matching is case-sensitive against the normalized key (section and variable lower-cased; subsection unchanged).
requirements: cfg must be a valid config object.
name must identify the multivar key to iterate.
regexp may be NULL to match all; when provided, it is applied case-sensitively to the normalized variable name.
callback must be a valid function pointer; returning non-zero terminates iteration and that value is returned.

functions.name: git_describe_commit
functions.description: Perform a describe operation against a specific committish (eg, a commit or object that can be peeled to a commit), producing a describe result that references the nearest matching tag/reference per the provided options. The returned result must be freed by the caller with git_describe_result_free. Returns 0 on success or an error code on failure.
requirements: result must be a valid, writable pointer to receive an allocated git_describe_result; the caller must free it with git_describe_result_free when done.
committish must be a valid git_object that is a committish (resolves/peels to a commit).
opts may be NULL to use defaults, or, if non-NULL, should be properly initialized (e.g., via git_describe_options_init or GIT_DESCRIBE_OPTIONS_INIT).
Caller must check the integer return value: 0 indicates success; nonzero indicates an error and no usable result should be assumed.

functions.name: git_describe_workdir

Produces a describe result that the caller must free with git_describe_result_free. Returns 0 on success or an error code on failure.
requirements: out must be a valid, writable pointer to receive an allocated git_describe_result; the caller must free it with git_describe_result_free when done.
repo must be a valid pointer to an open git_repository.
opts may be NULL to use defaults, or, if non-NULL, should be properly initialized (e.g., via git_describe_options_init or GIT_DESCRIBE_OPTIONS_INIT).
Caller must check the integer return value: 0 indicates success; nonzero indicates an error and no usable result should be assumed.

requirements: out must be a valid pointer to a git_buf to receive the formatted description. (Typical usage in libgit2 is an initialized buffer; exact initialization requirements are not specified here.)
result must be a valid pointer returned by git_describe_commit or git_describe_workdir.
opts may be NULL to use defaults, or, if non-NULL, should be properly initialized (e.g., via git_describe_format_options_init or GIT_DESCRIBE_FORMAT_OPTIONS_INIT).
Caller must check the integer return value: 0 indicates success; nonzero indicates an error and the buffer contents may be undefined.

	git_tree *new_tree,

functions.description: Create a diff between two tree objects (equivalent to `git diff <old-tree> <new-tree>`). The old_tree is the old_file side; new_tree is the new_file side. Either side may be NULL to indicate an empty tree, but not both. Options may be NULL for defaults.

	git_diff_hunk_cb hunk_cb,
	git_diff_line_cb line_cb,
	void *payload);
functions.description: Iterate through all deltas in a diff and issue callbacks. Text diff (hunks/lines) is only computed when corresponding callbacks are non-NULL; they are not invoked for binary files or pure mode changes. diff must be a valid git_diff.
format must be a valid git_diff_format_t value.

functions.name: git_diff_blobs
functions.description: Run a diff between two blobs and invoke callbacks for file/binary/hunks/lines. Either blob may be NULL to indicate an empty blob; both NULL yields no callbacks. Modes/paths are faked in callbacks (mode=0, path=NULL). Binary detection may suppress hunk/line callbacks unless GIT_DIFF_FORCE_TEXT is set.
requirements: old_blob and/or new_blob may be NULL; passing both NULL results in no callbacks.
old_as_path and new_as_path are optional and may be NULL; they affect presentation only.
options may be NULL to use defaults.
file_cb, binary_cb, hunk_cb, and line_cb are optional; when hunk_cb/line_cb are NULL, text diff is not produced.
Callbacks must return 0 for success; non-zero aborts iteration and is returned.

functions.name: git_diff_blob_to_buffer
functions.description: Run a diff between a blob (old side) and a raw buffer (new side) and invoke callbacks. Passing NULL for old_blob treats it as empty (delta ADDED). Passing NULL for buffer treats new side as empty (delta REMOVED). Paths/mode in callbacks are faked as in git_diff_blobs.
requirements: old_blob may be NULL to represent empty old side.
buffer may be NULL to represent empty new side; buffer_len should match the provided buffer data size.
buffer_len specifies the length for buffer when non-NULL.
old_as_path and buffer_as_path are optional and may be NULL; they affect presentation only.
options may be NULL to use defaults.
Callbacks are optional; non-zero callback return aborts and is propagated.

functions.name: git_diff_buffers
functions.description: Run a diff between two raw buffers and invoke callbacks. As with blob diffs, paths are for presentation; line/hunk callbacks are omitted for binary data unless forced.
requirements: old_buffer and/or new_buffer may be NULL to indicate empty sides; corresponding lengths should describe the provided data.
old_len is the length of old_buffer when non-NULL; new_len is the length of new_buffer when non-NULL.
old_as_path and new_as_path are optional and may be NULL; presentation only.
options may be NULL to use defaults.
Callbacks are optional; non-zero return aborts iteration and is returned.

functions.name: git_diff_from_buffer
functions.description: Parse the contents of a git patch file into a git_diff object. Similar to a computed diff but may have differences (e.g., abbreviated object IDs). Only patch files created by a git implementation are supported; not unified diffs from `diff` or other formats. Note: this API only supports SHA1 patch files.
requirements: out must be a valid output pointer to receive the allocated git_diff.
content must point to the patch file contents produced by a git implementation.
content_len must be the length of content.

functions.name: git_diff_get_stats
functions.description: Accumulate statistics (files changed, insertions, deletions) for all patches in a diff and return a git_diff_stats object.
requirements: out must be a valid output pointer to receive the allocated git_diff_stats.
diff must be a valid git_diff.

functions.name: git_diff_stats_files_changed
functions.description: Get the total number of files changed in a diff from a git_diff_stats object.
requirements: stats must be a valid git_diff_stats generated by git_diff_get_stats.

functions.name: git_diff_stats_insertions
functions.description: Get the total number of insertions in a diff from a git_diff_stats object.
requirements: stats must be a valid git_diff_stats generated by git_diff_get_stats.

functions.name: git_diff_stats_deletions
functions.description: Get the total number of deletions in a diff from a git_diff_stats object.
requirements: stats must be a valid git_diff_stats generated by git_diff_get_stats.

functions.name: git_diff_stats_to_buf
functions.description: Format diff statistics into a git_buf. Supports full, short, number and summary formats; width affects only GIT_DIFF_STATS_FULL.
requirements: out must point to a git_buf to receive the formatted text.
stats must be a valid git_diff_stats.
format must be a valid git_diff_stats_format_t value.
width is a target width and only affects the FULL format.

functions.name: git_diff_stats_free
functions.description: Deallocate a git_diff_stats object created by git_diff_get_stats. The stats pointer must not be used after this call.
requirements: stats must be a git_diff_stats previously returned by git_diff_get_stats.
The stats object must not be used after this call.

functions.name: git_diff_patchid_options_init
functions.description: Initialize a git_diff_patchid_options structure with default values. Equivalent to assigning GIT_DIFF_PATCHID_OPTIONS_INIT. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
requirements: opts must point to a valid, writable git_diff_patchid_options structure.
version must be GIT_DIFF_PATCHID_OPTIONS_VERSION.

functions.name: git_diff_patchid
functions.description: Calculate a stable patch ID for the given diff (as defined in git-patch-id(1)), summing hashes of file diffs while ignoring whitespace and line numbers. Intended to match upstream git’s patch-id results. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: out must point to a writable git_oid to receive the patch ID.
diff must be a valid git_diff.
opts is reserved for future changes; pass an initialized git_diff_patchid_options (currently no options are available).

functions.name: git_email_create_from_commit
functions.description: Generate an mbox-formatted e-mail patch for a single commit. Intended for producing email-ready patches (similar to `git format-patch`) with formatting controlled by git_email_create_options. The target commit must not be a merge commit. On success, writes the formatted patch into the provided git_buf.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a writable git_buf. Initialization requirements for git_buf are not stated here; typical libgit2 usage expects an initialized/zeroed buffer (inferred).
commit must be a valid, non-NULL git_commit object referring to a non-merge commit (explicit: "The commit must not be a merge commit").
opts may be NULL to use defaults is not stated; NULL-ability is unknown (unknown).
If opts is non-NULL, opts->version should match GIT_EMAIL_CREATE_OPTIONS_VERSION (inferred from libgit2 options pattern).
If opts is non-NULL and opts->start_number is provided, it must not be 0 (explicit: "cannot be 0").
Function returns 0 on success or an error code on failure; callers must check the return value and handle non-zero as an error (explicit from @return doc; standard libgit2 error handling inferred).
No merge commits are allowed; commits with multiple parents are invalid for this function (explicit).

functions.name: git_error_last
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the last git_error object recorded for the current thread (or a global instance if libgit2 was built without threading). The pointer is never NULL. Intended for retrieving additional error details (message and class) after a libgit2 call fails. Do not use this to determine whether an error occurred; rely on libgit2 return codes instead. The returned memory is owned and managed by libgit2 and must not be freed by the caller. The information may be stale if called after a successful function call.
requirements: Caller must not free or modify the returned git_error pointer or its contents; memory is managed by libgit2.
Do not use this function to determine if an error occurred; check libgit2 return codes instead.
Call this function only to obtain details immediately following a libgit2 function that reported an error; calling it after a successful call may return stale information.
Be aware that the error object is maintained per-thread when libgit2 is built with threading support; otherwise it is global.

functions.name: git_filter_list_load
functions.signature: int git_filter_list_load(git_filter_list **filters, git_repository *repo, git_blob *blob, const char *path, git_filter_mode_t mode, uint32_t flags);
functions.description: Builds a list of filters that apply to the given path (and optionally blob) for the specified direction (to worktree or to ODB). Returns 0 on success and may set *filters to NULL when no filters are needed. Intended usage: call to obtain a filter list before applying it to data, files, or blobs.
requirements: filters must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the resulting git_filter_list* (it may be set to NULL on success when no filters apply).
repo must be a valid repository that contains the provided path.
blob may be NULL (as documented) if the blob is not known.
path must be a valid path string (relative to the repository).
mode must be a valid git_filter_mode_t value (GIT_FILTER_TO_WORKTREE/GIT_FILTER_TO_ODB).
flags must be a valid combination of git_filter_flag_t values.
Caller must check both the return code and whether *filters is NULL before attempting to use the filter list.

functions.name: git_filter_list_load_ext
functions.signature: int git_filter_list_load_ext(git_filter_list **filters, git_repository *repo, git_blob *blob, const char *path, git_filter_mode_t mode, git_filter_options *opts);
functions.description: Builds a list of filters for the given path using the supplied git_filter_options (supports flags like loading attributes from HEAD or a specific commit). Returns 0 on success and may set *filters to NULL when no filters are needed.
requirements: filters must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the resulting git_filter_list* (it may be set to NULL on success when no filters apply).
repo must be a valid repository that contains the provided path.
blob: the header does not state if NULL is allowed; treat as unknown whether a NULL blob is accepted.
path must be a valid path string (relative to the repository).
mode must be a valid git_filter_mode_t value (GIT_FILTER_TO_WORKTREE/GIT_FILTER_TO_ODB).
opts must point to a valid git_filter_options structure; by libgit2 convention it should be initialized (e.g., via GIT_FILTER_OPTIONS_INIT) and have version set to GIT_FILTER_OPTIONS_VERSION.
Caller must check both the return code and whether *filters is NULL before attempting to use the filter list.

functions.name: git_filter_list_contains
functions.description: Returns 1 if a filter with the given name would run in this list, otherwise 0. Built-in filters include "crlf" and "ident"; other names come from filter attributes.
requirements: filters may be NULL (documented); if NULL, the function will report that no filters are present.
name must be a non-NULL, valid filter name string.

functions.name: git_filter_list_apply_to_buffer
functions.signature: int git_filter_list_apply_to_buffer(git_buf *out, git_filter_list *filters, const char *in, size_t in_len);
functions.description: Applies the filter list to an in-memory buffer and writes the filtered result to out.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a git_buf to receive output.
filters may be NULL (documented); if NULL, the input will effectively pass through unchanged.
in must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to the input data.
in_len must be the length in bytes of the input buffer.
Caller must check the return code for errors before using the contents of out.

functions.name: git_filter_list_apply_to_file
functions.signature: int git_filter_list_apply_to_file(git_buf *out, git_filter_list *filters, git_repository *repo, const char *path);
functions.description: Applies the filter list to the contents of a file in the repository’s working directory and writes the filtered result to out. Relative paths are interpreted relative to the repository workdir.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a git_buf to receive output.
filters must be a valid git_filter_list; the header does not state whether NULL is accepted, so treat NULL-acceptance as unknown.
repo must be a valid repository handle in which the filtering is performed.
path must be a valid path string; if relative, it is taken relative to the repository workdir.
Caller must check the return code for errors before using the contents of out.

functions.name: git_filter_list_apply_to_blob
functions.description: Applies the filter list to the contents of the specified blob and writes the filtered result to out.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a git_buf to receive output.
filters must be a valid git_filter_list; the header does not state whether NULL is accepted, so treat NULL-acceptance as unknown.
blob must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a git_blob whose contents will be filtered.
Caller must check the return code for errors before using the contents of out.

functions.name: git_filter_list_stream_buffer
functions.signature: int git_filter_list_stream_buffer(git_filter_list *filters, const char *buffer, size_t len, git_writestream *target);
functions.description: Applies the filter list to the provided memory buffer and writes the filtered data to the given git_writestream target as a stream.
requirements: filters must be a valid git_filter_list; the header does not state whether NULL is accepted, so treat NULL-acceptance as unknown.
buffer must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to input data.
len must be the size in bytes of buffer.
target must be a valid, non-NULL git_writestream that is ready to accept data.
Caller must check the return code for errors.

functions.name: git_filter_list_stream_file
functions.description: Applies the filter list to the contents of a file (path resolved relative to the repository workdir if relative) and writes the filtered data to the git_writestream target as a stream.
requirements: filters must be a valid git_filter_list; the header does not state whether NULL is accepted, so treat NULL-acceptance as unknown.
repo must be a valid repository handle.
path must be a valid path string; if relative, it is taken relative to the repository workdir.
target must be a valid, non-NULL git_writestream that is ready to accept data.
Caller must check the return code for errors.

functions.name: git_filter_list_stream_blob
functions.description: Applies the filter list to the contents of a blob and writes the filtered data to the git_writestream target as a stream.
requirements: filters must be a valid git_filter_list; the header does not state whether NULL is accepted, so treat NULL-acceptance as unknown.
blob must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a git_blob.
target must be a valid, non-NULL git_writestream that is ready to accept data.
Caller must check the return code for errors.

functions.name: git_filter_list_free
functions.description: Frees a git_filter_list created by git_filter_list_load or git_filter_list_load_ext.
requirements: filters must be a git_filter_list previously created by git_filter_list_load or git_filter_list_load_ext; the header does not state whether NULL is accepted, so treat NULL-acceptance as unknown.
Must not be used after it has been freed.

functions.name: git_graph_ahead_behind
functions.signature: int git_graph_ahead_behind(size_t *ahead, size_t *behind, git_repository *repo, const git_oid *local, const git_oid *upstream);
functions.description: Count the number of unique commits reachable from each of two commit OIDs within a repository, reporting how many commits the local side is ahead of and behind the upstream side (similar to what Git reports for branch ahead/behind). Use to compare two commits or branch tips within the same repository. Returns 0 on success, non-zero error code on failure.
requirements: repo must be a valid, opened git_repository.
ahead and behind must be non-NULL pointers to writable size_t storage.
local and upstream must be non-NULL pointers to git_oid values that identify commit objects present in repo.
The commits referenced by local and upstream do not need any upstream relationship; counts are computed by graph reachability.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; any non-zero value is a libgit2 error code.

functions.name: git_graph_descendant_of
functions.signature: int git_graph_descendant_of(git_repository *repo, const git_oid *commit, const git_oid *ancestor);
functions.description: Determine whether the commit identified by commit is a descendant of the commit identified by ancestor (following parent links). A commit is not considered a descendant of itself. Returns 1 if commit is a descendant of ancestor, 0 if not, otherwise an error code.
requirements: repo must be a valid, opened git_repository.
commit must be a non-NULL pointer to a git_oid identifying a commit that exists in repo.
ancestor must be a non-NULL pointer to a git_oid identifying a commit that exists in repo.
A commit is not considered a descendant of itself.
Caller must inspect the return value: 1 means true, 0 means false, any other non-zero value indicates a libgit2 error.

functions.name: git_graph_reachable_from_any
functions.signature: int git_graph_reachable_from_any(git_repository *repo, const git_oid *commit, const git_oid descendant_array[], size_t length);
functions.description: Test whether the commit identified by commit is reachable (i.e., an ancestor) from any commit in descendant_array by following parent edges. Returns 1 if reachable from at least one, 0 if not, otherwise an error code.
requirements: repo must be a valid, opened git_repository.
commit must be a non-NULL pointer to a git_oid identifying a commit that exists in repo.
descendant_array must point to an array of git_oid entries (each identifying a commit in repo); it may be NULL only if length is 0.
length must be the number of elements in descendant_array.
Caller must check the return value: 1 means reachable, 0 means not reachable, any other non-zero value indicates a libgit2 error.

functions.name: git_ignore_add_rule
functions.description: Adds one or more .gitignore-style rules to the repository’s in-memory internal ignore list. These rules augment the repository’s current ignore processing and do not persist to disk. Multiple rules can be provided in a single string, each terminated by a newline.
requirements: repo must be a valid, initialized git_repository pointer for an open repository.
rules must be a valid NUL-terminated string containing one or more .gitignore-style rules.
If providing multiple rules in the rules string, each rule should be terminated with a newline character ('\n').
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; any negative value indicates an error.
This call only affects the in-memory internal ignore rules; it does not modify any on-disk .gitignore files and will not persist across process restarts.

functions.name: git_ignore_clear_internal_rules
functions.description: Clears any previously added in-memory internal ignore rules for the repository and resets them to the default internal ignores (".", "..", and ".git"). This does not affect or disable rules present in .gitignore files on disk.
requirements: repo must be a valid, initialized git_repository pointer for an open repository.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; any negative value indicates an error.
Clearing internal rules does not disable or modify rules in .gitignore files that exist in the filesystem.

functions.name: git_ignore_path_is_ignored
functions.description: Determines whether the ignore rules would apply to the given path, similar to `git check-ignore --no-index`. The path is evaluated against ignore rules regardless of whether the file exists or is tracked. On success, sets *ignored to 1 if the path would be ignored, or 0 otherwise.
requirements: ignored must be a non-NULL pointer to an int and writable; on success, *ignored is set to 0 or 1.
repo must be a valid, initialized git_repository pointer for an open repository.
path must be a valid NUL-terminated string representing a path relative to the repository’s working directory.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates the ignore rules were processed; any negative value indicates an error (and *ignored may be undefined in that case).

functions.name: git_index_options_init
functions.description: Initialize a git_index_options structure with default values. Use to prepare options before creating/opening an index with extended configuration (eg SHA algorithm when supported). Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
requirements: opts must be a valid, writable pointer to a git_index_options struct.
version should be GIT_INDEX_OPTIONS_VERSION.
On success, opts fields are set to defaults; caller should not assume any prior contents are preserved.
Check the return value: 0 on success; -1 indicates failure.

functions.name: git_index_open
functions.description: Create a new bare git_index object that reflects the index file at index_path, without any backing repository. Only SHA1 indexes are supported by this API. Must be freed with git_index_free.
requirements: index_out must be a valid pointer to receive the created git_index*.
index_path must point to a filesystem path to an index file.
This creates a bare index (no ODB/working directory); methods that require a repository (e.g., git_index_add_bypath) will fail.
Return value must be checked: 0 on success; otherwise an error code.

functions.name: git_index_new
functions.description: Create an in-memory (non-persisted) git_index object that is not readable/writable to the filesystem. Only SHA1 indexes are supported by this API. Must be freed with git_index_free.
requirements: index_out must be a valid pointer to receive the created git_index*.
This index cannot be read/written to disk.
Return value must be checked: 0 on success; otherwise an error code.

functions.name: git_index_free
functions.description: Free a git_index object created or obtained from libgit2.
requirements: index may be NULL or a valid git_index pointer; after return it must not be used.

functions.name: git_index_owner
functions.description: Get the repository that owns the given index, if any.
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer.
Return is a borrowed pointer; do not free it.

functions.name: git_index_caps
functions.description: Read the capability flags affecting index actions (case sensitivity, filemode, symlinks). Returns a combination of GIT_INDEX_CAPABILITY values.
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer.

functions.name: git_index_set_caps
functions.description: Set the capability flags affecting index actions. Passing GIT_INDEX_CAPABILITY_FROM_OWNER loads capabilities from the owning repository's config (core.ignorecase, core.filemode, core.symlinks).
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer.
caps is a combination of GIT_INDEX_CAPABILITY values or GIT_INDEX_CAPABILITY_FROM_OWNER.
Check return: 0 on success; -1 on failure.

functions.name: git_index_version
functions.description: Get the on-disk format version for the index (2, 3, or 4).
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer.
Return is the version currently set for writing.

functions.name: git_index_set_version
functions.description: Set the on-disk index format version (2, 3, or 4). If 2 is given, writing may still use 3 if necessary to represent data.
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer.
version must be 2, 3, or 4.
Check return: 0 on success; -1 on failure.

functions.name: git_index_read
functions.description: Load on-disk index data into the in-memory index. If force is non-zero, discards in-memory changes and reloads from disk (clearing if no on-disk file). If force is zero, reloads only if the on-disk file changed; unsaved in-memory changes may be discarded if disk changed.
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer.
force controls hard (non-zero) vs soft (zero) read semantics.
Caller must handle return value: 0 on success or an error code.
Be aware that a soft read may discard in-memory changes if the on-disk index changed.

functions.name: git_index_write
functions.description: Write the in-memory index back to disk using an atomic file lock.
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer associated with a path (not a purely in-memory index created with git_index_new).
Check return value: 0 on success; otherwise an error code.

functions.name: git_index_path
functions.description: Get the full filesystem path to the on-disk index file, or NULL for an in-memory index.
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer.
Returned pointer is owned by the index; do not free it; may be NULL for in-memory indices.

functions.name: git_index_checksum
functions.description: Deprecated: Get the SHA-1 checksum of the on-disk index file (hash over the file excluding the trailing 20-byte checksum). If the index does not exist on disk, the value will be zeroed. No replacement is provided.
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer.
Do not modify or free the returned git_oid pointer.
Be aware this API is deprecated and may be unavailable if compiled with GIT_DEPRECATE_HARD.

functions.name: git_index_read_tree
functions.description: Replace the index contents with the entries from the given tree.
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer.
tree must be a valid pointer to a git_tree.
This operation replaces current index contents.
Return value must be checked: 0 on success or an error code.

functions.name: git_index_write_tree
functions.description: Write the current index state as tree objects and return the OID of the root tree. The index must be associated with a repository and contain no conflicts.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the resulting tree OID.
index must be a valid git_index pointer associated with an existing repository (not bare/in-memory-only).
The index must not contain any file in conflict; otherwise returns GIT_EUNMERGED.
Check return value: 0 on success; GIT_EUNMERGED or another error code on failure.

functions.name: git_index_write_tree_to
functions.description: Write the index as a tree to the specified repository and return the root tree OID. The index must contain no conflicts.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the resulting tree OID.
index must be a valid git_index pointer.
repo must be a valid git_repository pointer where the tree will be written.
The index must not contain any file in conflict; otherwise returns GIT_EUNMERGED.
Check return value: 0 on success or an error code.

functions.name: git_index_entrycount
functions.description: Get the number of entries currently present in the index.
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer.

functions.name: git_index_clear
functions.description: Clear all entries in the index in memory. Persisting the removal requires writing the index to disk.
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer.
Check return value: 0 on success; negative error code on failure.

functions.name: git_index_get_byindex
functions.description: Return a pointer to the index entry at position n. The returned entry is read-only and must not be freed.
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer.
n should be less than git_index_entrycount(index) to get a non-NULL result.
The returned pointer is only valid as long as the index is not modified in a way that invalidates it; do not free or modify it.

functions.name: git_index_get_bypath
functions.signature: const git_index_entry * git_index_get_bypath(git_index *index, const char *path, int stage)
functions.description: Return a pointer to the index entry that matches the given path and stage. The returned entry is read-only and must not be freed.
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer.
path must be a valid C string path.
stage must be a valid stage; use GIT_INDEX_STAGE_ANY to match any stage, or a specific stage value (0-3).
Returns NULL if not found; caller must handle NULL.
Do not free or modify the returned pointer.

functions.name: git_index_remove
functions.signature: int git_index_remove(git_index *index, const char *path, int stage)
functions.description: Remove the index entry identified by path and stage from the index.
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer.
path must be a valid C string path.
stage must be a valid stage (e.g., GIT_INDEX_STAGE_ANY or 0-3).
Check return value: 0 on success or an error code.

functions.name: git_index_remove_directory
functions.signature: int git_index_remove_directory(git_index *index, const char *dir, int stage)
functions.description: Remove all index entries that are under the given directory path at the specified stage.
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer.
dir must be a valid C string directory path.
stage must be a valid stage (e.g., GIT_INDEX_STAGE_ANY or 0-3).
Check return value: 0 on success or an error code.

functions.name: git_index_add
functions.description: Add or update an index entry from an in-memory git_index_entry. If an existing entry with the same path and stage exists, it will be replaced. A full copy of source_entry (including its path) is inserted.
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer.
source_entry must point to a fully populated git_index_entry, including a valid path and stage.
Check return value: 0 on success or an error code.

functions.name: git_index_entry_stage
functions.description: Return the stage number calculated from the entry's flags.
requirements: entry must be a valid pointer to a git_index_entry.

functions.name: git_index_entry_is_conflict
functions.description: Return 1 if the given index entry represents a conflict (stage > 0), 0 otherwise.
requirements: entry must be a valid pointer to a git_index_entry.

functions.name: git_index_iterator_new
functions.description: Create an iterator over the index entries as they exist at creation time. Entries are returned in path-sorted order. The iterator is backed by a snapshot so the index may be modified while iterating without affecting the iterator.
requirements: iterator_out must be a valid pointer to receive the iterator.
index must be a valid git_index pointer.
Check return value: 0 on success or an error code.
Free the iterator with git_index_iterator_free when done.

functions.name: git_index_iterator_next
functions.description: Get the next index entry from the iterator. On completion, returns GIT_ITEROVER.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive a const git_index_entry pointer.
iterator must be a valid git_index_iterator.
Returned entry is read-only; do not free or modify it.
Handle return values: 0 on success with an entry, GIT_ITEROVER when done, or an error code.

functions.name: git_index_iterator_free
functions.description: Free an index iterator created by git_index_iterator_new.
requirements: iterator may be NULL or a valid git_index_iterator pointer; after return it must not be used.

functions.name: git_index_add_bypath
functions.description: Add or update an index entry from a file on disk at the given path (relative to the repository working directory). Ignores .gitignore (forces add). Marks any existing conflict for that path as resolved and moves conflict data to REUC. Fails for bare index instances.
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer associated with a repository (not bare).
path must be a readable file path relative to the repository's working folder.
This operation forces add regardless of ignore rules.
Check return value: 0 on success or an error code.

functions.name: git_index_add_from_buffer
functions.signature: int git_index_add_from_buffer(git_index *index, const git_index_entry *entry, const void *buffer, size_t len)
functions.description: Create a blob from the provided buffer in the repository owning the index and add/update the index entry at entry->path. Forces add regardless of ignore rules. Resolves any existing conflict for that path (moves data to REUC).
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer that is owned by a repository (the blob is created in that repo).
entry must be a valid git_index_entry describing the target path within the repository.
buffer must point to data of length len.
Check return value: 0 on success or an error code.

functions.name: git_index_remove_bypath
functions.description: Remove the index entry corresponding to a file on disk at path (relative to the repository working folder). Resolves any existing conflict for that path (moves data to REUC).
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer.
path must be a path relative to the repository's working folder.
Check return value: 0 on success or an error code.

functions.name: git_index_add_all
functions.signature: int git_index_add_all(git_index *index, const git_strarray *pathspec, unsigned int flags, git_index_matched_path_cb callback, void *payload)
functions.description: Add or update index entries matching files in the working directory according to the given pathspec. By default, ignored files are skipped; use flags to control behavior (force add, disable pathspec match, check pathspec). Invokes an optional callback before each add/update to allow skipping or aborting. Resolves any existing conflicts for affected paths. Fails for bare index instances.
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer associated with a repository (not bare).
pathspec must be a valid git_strarray of path patterns.

flags is a combination of git_index_add_option_t values; GIT_INDEX_ADD_DISABLE_PATHSPEC_MATCH disables globbing; GIT_INDEX_ADD_FORCE forces add; GIT_INDEX_ADD_CHECK_PATHSPEC validates exact pathspec matches and may cause GIT_EINVALIDSPEC.
If provided, callback is invoked for each match: return 0 to add, >0 to skip, <0 to abort; payload is passed through.
Check return value: 0 on success, negative callback return, or another error code.

functions.name: git_index_remove_all
functions.signature: int git_index_remove_all(git_index *index, const git_strarray *pathspec, git_index_matched_path_cb callback, void *payload)
functions.description: Remove all index entries that match the given pathspec. Invokes an optional callback before each removal to allow skipping or aborting.
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer.
pathspec must be a valid git_strarray of path patterns.
If provided, callback is invoked for each match: return 0 to remove, >0 to skip, <0 to abort; payload is passed through.
Check return value: 0 on success, negative callback return, or another error code.

functions.name: git_index_update_all
functions.signature: int git_index_update_all(git_index *index, const git_strarray *pathspec, git_index_matched_path_cb callback, void *payload)
functions.description: Update existing index entries to match the working directory for files matching the pathspec. Deletes entries for files that no longer exist, updates metadata/content as needed. Optional callback is invoked before each update/remove. Fails for bare index instances.
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer associated with a repository (not bare).
pathspec must be a valid git_strarray of path patterns.
If provided, callback is invoked for each match: return 0 to proceed, >0 to skip, <0 to abort; payload is passed through.
Check return value: 0 on success, negative callback return, or another error code.

functions.name: git_index_find
functions.description: Find the first position of entries that point to the given path in the index. Optionally returns the position in at_pos.
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer.
path must be a valid C string path.
at_pos may be NULL or a valid pointer to receive the position.
Check return value: 0 on success or an error code.

functions.name: git_index_find_prefix
functions.description: Find the first position of entries whose paths match the given prefix. To search within a directory, suffix the prefix with '/'. Optionally returns the position in at_pos.
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer.
prefix must be a valid C string.
at_pos may be NULL or a valid pointer to receive the position.
Check return value: 0 on success or an error code.

functions.name: git_index_conflict_add
functions.signature: int git_index_conflict_add(git_index *index, const git_index_entry *ancestor_entry, const git_index_entry *our_entry, const git_index_entry *their_entry)
functions.description: Add or update index entries to represent a conflict for a single path. Any staged entries at those paths are removed. Each of the entries may be NULL to indicate absence in that side of the merge.
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer.
ancestor_entry, our_entry, their_entry are pointers to git_index_entry instances for the same path; any may be NULL.
Check return value: 0 on success or an error code.

functions.name: git_index_conflict_get
functions.signature: int git_index_conflict_get(const git_index_entry **ancestor_out, const git_index_entry **our_out, const git_index_entry **their_out, git_index *index, const char *path)
functions.description: Get the index entries that represent a conflict for the given path (ancestor, ours, theirs). Returned entries are read-only and must not be freed.
requirements: ancestor_out, our_out, their_out must be valid pointers to receive entry pointers (any of which may be set to NULL).
index must be a valid git_index pointer.
path must be a valid C string path.
Check return value: 0 on success or an error code.
Do not free or modify returned pointers.

functions.name: git_index_conflict_remove
functions.description: Remove the index entries that represent a conflict for the given path.
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer.
path must be a valid C string path.
Check return value: 0 on success or an error code.

functions.name: git_index_conflict_cleanup
functions.description: Remove all conflict entries (entries with stage > 0) from the index.
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer.
Check return value: 0 on success or an error code.

functions.name: git_index_has_conflicts
functions.description: Return 1 if the index contains any conflict entries, 0 otherwise.
requirements: index must be a valid git_index pointer.

functions.name: git_index_conflict_iterator_new
functions.description: Create an iterator over the conflicts in the index.
requirements: iterator_out must be a valid pointer to receive the iterator.
index must be a valid git_index pointer.
The index must not be modified while iterating; results are undefined.
Check return value: 0 on success or an error code.
Free the iterator with git_index_conflict_iterator_free.

functions.name: git_index_conflict_next
functions.signature: int git_index_conflict_next(const git_index_entry **ancestor_out, const git_index_entry **our_out, const git_index_entry **their_out, git_index_conflict_iterator *iterator)
functions.description: Return the current conflict (ancestor, ours, theirs) and advance the conflict iterator. Returns GIT_ITEROVER when iteration is complete.
requirements: ancestor_out, our_out, their_out must be valid pointers to receive entry pointers (any may be NULL).
iterator must be a valid git_index_conflict_iterator.
Do not free or modify the returned entry pointers.
Handle return values: 0 on success with a conflict, GIT_ITEROVER when done, or an error code.

functions.name: git_index_conflict_iterator_free
functions.description: Free a conflict iterator created by git_index_conflict_iterator_new.
requirements: iterator may be NULL or a valid git_index_conflict_iterator pointer; after return it must not be used.

functions.name: git_indexer_options_init
functions.description: Initialize a git_indexer_options structure with default values. Use this before configuring and passing options to git_indexer_new. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
requirements: opts must point to writable storage for a git_indexer_options struct.
version should be GIT_INDEXER_OPTIONS_VERSION.
Check the return value: 0 indicates success; -1 indicates failure.

functions.name: git_indexer_new
functions.description: Create a new indexer instance (experimental SHA-256 configuration variant). The indexer will write the packfile to the given directory and use the provided options (including callback and verification). Returns 0 on success or an error code.
requirements: This overload is compiled when GIT_EXPERIMENTAL_SHA256 is defined.
out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created git_indexer instance on success.
path must be a valid, NUL-terminated filesystem path to a directory where the packfile should be stored.
opts must point to a git_indexer_options struct initialized with git_indexer_options_init or otherwise valid for this build configuration.
Check the return value: 0 indicates success; nonzero indicates an error code.

functions.name: git_indexer_append
functions.signature: int git_indexer_append(git_indexer *idx, const void *data, size_t size, git_indexer_progress *stats);
functions.description: Feed raw packfile data chunk(s) to the indexer. Updates provided progress statistics as data is processed. Returns 0 on success or an error code.
requirements: idx must be a valid git_indexer instance previously created by git_indexer_new and not yet freed.
data must point to a buffer of at least size bytes; size is the number of bytes to append.
stats must point to writable git_indexer_progress storage to receive progress updates (NULL-acceptance is unknown).
May be called repeatedly to provide the full packfile content in multiple chunks.
Check the return value: 0 indicates success; nonzero indicates an error code.
Callers should not use the resulting pack/index until git_indexer_commit succeeds.

functions.name: git_indexer_commit
functions.description: Finalize indexing: resolve pending deltas, perform connectivity checks if enabled, and write out the index file for the pack. Returns 0 on success or an error code.
requirements: idx must be a valid git_indexer instance previously created by git_indexer_new and not yet freed.
stats must point to writable git_indexer_progress storage to receive final progress information (NULL-acceptance is unknown).
Should be called after all data has been appended via git_indexer_append.
The packfile’s final name/hash is only correct after a successful commit.
Check the return value: 0 indicates success; nonzero indicates an error code.

functions.name: git_indexer_hash
functions.description: Return the packfile’s object ID (hash) for the resulting pack. Deprecated in favor of git_indexer_name. Accurate only after the index has been finalized with git_indexer_commit.
requirements: Available only when GIT_DEPRECATE_HARD is not defined (function is deprecated).
idx must be a valid git_indexer instance.
The returned hash corresponds to the finalized pack; calling before a successful commit yields an incorrect value.
Do not modify or free the returned pointer; it points to internal storage.

functions.name: git_indexer_name
functions.description: Get the unique, NUL-terminated name for the resulting packfile (derived from its content). Accurate only after the index has been finalized with git_indexer_commit.
requirements: idx must be a valid git_indexer instance.
Only correct after a successful git_indexer_commit; calling earlier yields an incorrect value.
Do not modify or free the returned string; it points to internal storage.

functions.name: git_indexer_free
functions.description: Free a git_indexer and its associated resources.
requirements: idx must be a git_indexer previously created by git_indexer_new. Whether NULL is accepted is unknown.
After this call, idx must not be used again.

functions.name: git_mailmap_new
functions.description: Allocate a new, empty mailmap object. The returned object contains no entries; populate it (for example with git_mailmap_add_entry or by parsing a file/buffer) before resolving names. The caller owns the resulting object and must free it with git_mailmap_free.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to a git_mailmap* storage location.
On success (return 0), the caller must later call git_mailmap_free on the produced git_mailmap*.
Check the return value: 0 indicates success; any non-zero value is an error code.

functions.name: git_mailmap_free
functions.description: Free a mailmap object and all associated memory. Use to release objects created by git_mailmap_new, git_mailmap_from_buffer, or git_mailmap_from_repository.
requirements: mm must be a valid git_mailmap* previously created by libgit2 allocation routines for mailmaps (e.g., git_mailmap_new, git_mailmap_from_buffer, git_mailmap_from_repository).
Do not use the mailmap pointer after this call (it becomes invalid).
Nullability of mm is not documented; passing NULL is unknown.

functions.name: git_mailmap_add_entry
functions.signature: int git_mailmap_add_entry(git_mailmap *mm, const char *real_name, const char *real_email, const char *replace_name, const char *replace_email);
functions.description: Add or replace a single mapping entry in the given mailmap. Maps an input identity (replace_name/replace_email) to a canonical identity (real_name/real_email). If an entry for the same replace_name/replace_email already exists, it is replaced.
requirements: mm must be a valid, initialized git_mailmap*.
real_name may be NULL (to leave name unmapped/unspecified).
real_email may be NULL (to leave email unmapped/unspecified).
replace_name may be NULL.
replace_email must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string (the email to replace).
Strings passed must remain valid for the duration of the call.
Check the return value: 0 indicates success; any non-zero value is an error code.

functions.name: git_mailmap_from_buffer
functions.signature: int git_mailmap_from_buffer(git_mailmap **out, const char *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Create a new mailmap instance by parsing a single mailmap file provided as a memory buffer. Useful for loading mailmaps from in-memory data.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to a git_mailmap* storage location.
buf must point to a readable memory buffer containing mailmap contents; it need not be NUL-terminated.
len must be the size in bytes of buf; buf must be valid for at least len bytes.
The buffer contents must follow the mailmap file format; malformed data will cause a non-zero error return.
On success (return 0), the caller receives a new git_mailmap* and must free it with git_mailmap_free.
Check the return value: 0 indicates success; any non-zero value is an error code.

functions.name: git_mailmap_from_repository
functions.description: Create a new mailmap instance by loading mailmap information from a repository according to configuration and default locations (working tree .mailmap, mailmap.blob, mailmap.file).
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to a git_mailmap* storage location.
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository*.
Loading occurs in documented order: working directory '.mailmap' (if present), blob from 'mailmap.blob' (defaults to 'HEAD:.mailmap' in bare repositories), then path from 'mailmap.file' (if set).
On success (return 0), the caller receives a new git_mailmap* and must free it with git_mailmap_free.
Check the return value: 0 indicates success; any non-zero value is an error code.

functions.name: git_mailmap_resolve
functions.signature: int git_mailmap_resolve(const char **real_name, const char **real_email, const git_mailmap *mm, const char *name, const char *email);
functions.description: Resolve an input name and email to their canonical (real) name and email using the mailmap. Returns pointers to strings whose lifetimes are tied to the provided mailmap (mm) and/or the input strings. Callers must not free the returned strings.
requirements: real_name must be a non-NULL pointer to storage for a const char* output.
real_email must be a non-NULL pointer to storage for a const char* output.
mm may be NULL (lookup proceeds with default behavior if no mailmap is provided).
name must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string (the name to look up).
email must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string (the email to look up).
The returned pointers are not owned by the caller; do not free them. Their lifetimes are tied to mm, name, and email; keep those alive as required.
Check the return value: 0 indicates success; any non-zero value is an error code.

functions.name: git_mailmap_resolve_signature
functions.description: Produce a new signature where the name and email have been resolved via the mailmap (if applicable). The resulting git_signature must be freed by the caller using git_signature_free.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to a git_signature* storage location.
mm must be a valid git_mailmap* if provided; nullability not specified in the header (unknown whether NULL is allowed).
sig must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid git_signature to resolve.
On success (return 0), the caller receives a newly allocated git_signature* and must free it with git_signature_free.
Check the return value: 0 indicates success; any non-zero value is an error code.

functions.name: git_merge_file_input_init
functions.description: Initialize a git_merge_file_input structure with default values. Use this prior to populating ancestor/ours/theirs inputs for git_merge_file. Pass GIT_MERGE_FILE_INPUT_VERSION as version.
requirements: opts must be a valid, writable pointer.
version should be GIT_MERGE_FILE_INPUT_VERSION.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; -1 indicates failure.

functions.name: git_merge_file_options_init
functions.description: Initialize a git_merge_file_options structure with default values (equivalent to GIT_MERGE_FILE_OPTIONS_INIT). Use to configure file merge behavior (labels, favor, flags, marker size).
requirements: opts must be a valid, writable pointer.
version should be GIT_MERGE_FILE_OPTIONS_VERSION.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; -1 indicates failure.

functions.name: git_merge_options_init
functions.description: Initialize a git_merge_options structure with defaults (equivalent to GIT_MERGE_OPTIONS_INIT). Controls tree/commit merge behavior (flags, rename detection, recursion limit, default driver, file-level merge preferences).
requirements: opts must be a valid, writable pointer.
version should be GIT_MERGE_OPTIONS_VERSION.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; -1 indicates failure.

functions.name: git_merge_analysis
functions.signature: int git_merge_analysis(git_merge_analysis_t *analysis_out, git_merge_preference_t *preference_out, git_repository *repo, const git_annotated_commit **their_heads, size_t their_heads_len);
functions.description: Analyze the given annotated head(s) against the repository’s HEAD to determine whether a merge is needed and which kind (normal, fast-forward, up-to-date, unborn). Also returns user merge preference flags.
requirements: analysis_out must be a valid, writable pointer.
preference_out must be a valid, writable pointer.
repo must point to a valid, opened repository with a HEAD (unless unborn analysis is reported).
their_heads must reference an array of their_heads_len pointers to valid git_annotated_commit objects associated with repo.
their_heads_len must match the number of entries in their_heads.
Return value must be checked: 0 on success, non-zero on error.

functions.name: git_merge_analysis_for_ref
functions.signature: int git_merge_analysis_for_ref(git_merge_analysis_t *analysis_out, git_merge_preference_t *preference_out, git_repository *repo, git_reference *our_ref, const git_annotated_commit **their_heads, size_t their_heads_len);
functions.description: Analyze the given annotated head(s) against a specific reference (our_ref) to determine merge opportunities and preferences (normal, fast-forward, up-to-date, unborn).
requirements: analysis_out must be a valid, writable pointer.
preference_out must be a valid, writable pointer.
repo must be a valid, opened repository.
our_ref must be a valid reference within repo appropriate for analysis.
their_heads must reference an array of their_heads_len valid git_annotated_commit pointers associated with repo.
their_heads_len must match the number of entries in their_heads.
Return value must be checked: 0 on success, non-zero on error.

functions.name: git_merge_base
functions.signature: int git_merge_base(git_oid *out, git_repository *repo, const git_oid *one, const git_oid *two);
functions.description: Compute a merge base OID between two commits identified by OIDs in repo. Writes the found base into out.
requirements: out must be a valid, writable pointer to git_oid.
repo must be a valid, opened repository containing the commits.
one and two must be non-NULL pointers to OIDs that resolve to commits in repo.
Return values: 0 on success; GIT_ENOTFOUND if no base; non-zero error code otherwise. Caller must check return value.

functions.name: git_merge_bases
functions.signature: int git_merge_bases(git_oidarray *out, git_repository *repo, const git_oid *one, const git_oid *two);
functions.description: Find all merge base OIDs between two commits. Results are stored in an output array structure.
requirements: out must be a valid, writable pointer to git_oidarray; the function will populate it (caller responsible for freeing per libgit2 oidarray rules).
repo must be a valid, opened repository containing the commits.
one and two must be non-NULL pointers to OIDs that resolve to commits in repo.
Return values: 0 on success; GIT_ENOTFOUND if none; non-zero on error. Caller must check return value.

functions.name: git_merge_base_many
functions.signature: int git_merge_base_many(git_oid *out, git_repository *repo, size_t length, const git_oid input_array[]);
functions.description: Compute a merge base OID considering a list of commits (pairwise/recursive as defined by git’s merge-base semantics for many inputs). Writes the single resulting base into out.
requirements: out must be a valid, writable pointer to git_oid.
repo must be a valid, opened repository containing the commits.
input_array must point to an array of length OIDs; each OID must resolve to a commit in repo.
length must equal the number of elements in input_array and be >= 1.
Return values: 0 on success; GIT_ENOTFOUND if none; -1 on failure. Caller must check return value.

functions.name: git_merge_bases_many
functions.signature: int git_merge_bases_many(git_oidarray *out, git_repository *repo, size_t length, const git_oid input_array[]);
functions.description: Find all merge base OIDs among a list of commits (similar to `git merge-base` discussion for many inputs). Results are written to out as an oidarray.
requirements: out must be a valid, writable pointer to git_oidarray; the function will populate it (caller responsible for freeing per libgit2 oidarray rules).
repo must be a valid, opened repository containing the commits.
input_array must point to an array of length OIDs; each OID must resolve to a commit in repo.
length must equal the number of elements in input_array and be >= 1.
Return values: 0 on success; GIT_ENOTFOUND if none; -1 on failure. Caller must check return value.

functions.name: git_merge_base_octopus
functions.signature: int git_merge_base_octopus(git_oid *out, git_repository *repo, size_t length, const git_oid input_array[]);
functions.description: Compute a merge base OID suitable for an octopus merge among the given commits. Writes the resulting base OID to out.
requirements: out must be a valid, writable pointer to git_oid.
repo must be a valid, opened repository containing the commits.
input_array must point to an array of length OIDs; each OID must resolve to a commit in repo.
length must equal the number of elements in input_array and be >= 1.
Return values: 0 on success; GIT_ENOTFOUND if none; -1 on failure. Caller must check return value.

functions.name: git_merge_file
functions.signature: int git_merge_file(git_merge_file_result *out, const git_merge_file_input *ancestor, const git_merge_file_input *ours, const git_merge_file_input *theirs, const git_merge_file_options *opts);
functions.description: Three-way merge the in-memory file contents described by ancestor/ours/theirs, producing a git_merge_file_result with merged content and metadata. Does not access repository state; behavior is controlled by opts. The result must be freed with git_merge_file_result_free.
requirements: out must be a valid, writable pointer; on success, caller must free with git_merge_file_result_free.
ancestor, ours, and theirs should be initialized git_merge_file_input structures; fields should describe the file (ptr/size/path/mode). Any side can omit path/mode by setting to NULL/0 as documented.
opts may be NULL to accept defaults; otherwise should be initialized via git_merge_file_options_init.
Caller must check return value: 0 on success; non-zero on error.

functions.name: git_merge_file_from_index
functions.signature: int git_merge_file_from_index(git_merge_file_result *out, git_repository *repo, const git_index_entry *ancestor, const git_index_entry *ours, const git_index_entry *theirs, const git_merge_file_options *opts);
functions.description: Three-way merge the file versions referenced by index entries (stage 1/2/3) in repo, producing a git_merge_file_result with merged content and metadata. The result must be freed with git_merge_file_result_free.
requirements: out must be a valid, writable pointer; on success, caller must free with git_merge_file_result_free.
repo must be a valid, opened repository.
ancestor should be the stage 1 entry; ours stage 2; theirs stage 3. Any of these may be NULL only if the conflict shape implies absence (inferred by index), otherwise they should be valid pointers.
opts may be NULL for defaults; otherwise should be initialized via git_merge_file_options_init.
Caller must check return value: 0 on success; non-zero on error.

functions.name: git_merge_file_result_free
functions.description: Free resources held by a git_merge_file_result previously returned by git_merge_file or git_merge_file_from_index. Safe to call with NULL.
requirements: result may be NULL (no-op).
If non-NULL, result must have been obtained from a libgit2 merge-file API and not freed previously.

functions.name: git_merge_trees
functions.signature: int git_merge_trees(git_index **out, git_repository *repo, const git_tree *ancestor_tree, const git_tree *our_tree, const git_tree *their_tree, const git_merge_options *opts);
functions.description: Merge two trees (ours vs theirs) using an optional common ancestor tree and return a git_index representing the merge result. Conflicts, if any, are recorded in the index. The returned index must be freed with git_index_free.
