requirements: out must be a valid, writable pointer to receive an allocated git_index* on success; caller must free it with git_index_free.
repo must be a valid, opened repository that contains the given trees.
our_tree and their_tree must be valid tree objects belonging to repo; ancestor_tree may be NULL if none.
opts may be NULL for defaults; otherwise should be initialized via git_merge_options_init.
Caller must check return value: 0 on success; non-zero on error.
If the result will be converted to a tree, the caller should resolve any conflicts first.

functions.name: git_merge_commits
functions.signature: int git_merge_commits(git_index **out, git_repository *repo, const git_commit *our_commit, const git_commit *their_commit, const git_merge_options *opts);
functions.description: Merge two commits (ours vs theirs) and return a git_index representing the merge result. Conflicts, if any, are recorded in the index. The returned index must be freed with git_index_free.
requirements: out must be a valid, writable pointer to receive an allocated git_index* on success; caller must free it with git_index_free.
repo must be a valid, opened repository that contains the given commits.
our_commit and their_commit must be valid commit objects belonging to repo.
opts may be NULL for defaults; otherwise should be initialized via git_merge_options_init.
Caller must check return value: 0 on success; non-zero on error.
If the result will be converted to a tree, the caller should resolve any conflicts first.

functions.name: git_merge
functions.signature: int git_merge(git_repository *repo, const git_annotated_commit **their_heads, size_t their_heads_len, const git_merge_options *merge_opts, const git_checkout_options *checkout_opts);
functions.description: Perform a merge of the given annotated commits into the repository’s HEAD, updating the working directory and index. Changes are staged; conflicts are written to the index. The repository enters a merging state compatible with git and should be cleaned up after commit or abort.
requirements: repo must be a valid, opened repository; its working directory will be updated.
their_heads must reference an array of their_heads_len valid git_annotated_commit pointers associated with repo.
their_heads_len must match the number of entries in their_heads.
merge_opts may be NULL for defaults; otherwise should be initialized via git_merge_options_init.
checkout_opts may be NULL; otherwise should be initialized via git_checkout_options init routine.
After completion, caller should inspect and resolve index conflicts as needed and then commit.
The repository merge state should be cleared with git_repository_state_cleanup() after finishing the merge (commit) or aborting.
Caller must check return value: 0 on success; non-zero on error.

functions.name: git_message_prettify
functions.signature: int git_message_prettify(git_buf *out, const char *message, int strip_comments, char comment_char);
functions.description: Cleans up excess whitespace in a commit message and ensures it ends with a trailing newline. Optionally removes lines that start with the given comment character when strip_comments is non-zero. Typical usage: initialize a git_buf, call this function with the message to normalize, then inspect the resulting buffer. Returns 0 on success or a libgit2 error code on failure.
requirements: out must point to a valid, user-allocated git_buf; it should be initialized before use (e.g., via GIT_BUF_INIT or an equivalent libgit2 initializer).
message must be a valid, NUL-terminated string (may be empty).

If strip_comments is non-zero, lines whose first character is comment_char are considered comments and are removed; otherwise, message content is preserved aside from whitespace cleanup and ensuring a trailing newline.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; non-zero indicates an error code as defined by libgit2.
On success, out will be filled with the prettified message (overwriting any prior contents).

functions.name: git_message_trailers
functions.description: Parses key/value trailers from the last paragraph of a commit message (ignoring patches or conflict sections) and fills a git_message_trailer_array with the results. Use this to extract conventional trailers like Signed-off-by, Co-authored-by, etc. Returns 0 on success or non-zero on error.
requirements: arr must point to a pre-allocated git_message_trailer_array to be filled by this function; do not access or modify fields marked private.
message must be a valid, NUL-terminated string containing the commit message to parse.
On success, arr->trailers points to an array of parsed trailers and arr->count specifies its length; the memory must be released by calling git_message_trailer_array_free.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; non-zero indicates an error code.

functions.name: git_message_trailer_array_free
functions.description: Releases any memory allocated within a git_message_trailer_array by a prior call to git_message_trailers. After this call, the array’s contents and any pointers within become invalid.
requirements: arr must be a non-NULL pointer to a git_message_trailer_array that was previously filled by git_message_trailers.
Call exactly once per successful git_message_trailers invocation to avoid memory leaks and undefined behavior.
Do not access arr->trailers, arr->_trailer_block, or any trailer pointers after this function returns.

functions.name: git_note_iterator_new
functions.description: Create a new iterator to traverse notes in a repository, optionally within a specific notes reference (defaults to "refs/notes/commits"). Caller must free the iterator when finished using git_note_iterator_free.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created iterator
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository
notes_ref may be NULL to use the default "refs/notes/commits"
The returned iterator must be freed by the caller with git_note_iterator_free
Function returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure

functions.name: git_note_commit_iterator_new
functions.description: Create a new iterator to traverse notes stored in the tree of the given notes commit. Caller must free the iterator using git_note_iterator_free.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the iterator
notes_commit must be a valid git_commit object that represents a notes commit
The returned iterator must be freed by the caller with git_note_iterator_free
Function returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure

functions.name: git_note_iterator_free
functions.description: Free a note iterator previously created by git_note_iterator_new or git_note_commit_iterator_new.
requirements: it must be a git_note_iterator obtained from the corresponding creation function
After this call, the iterator must not be used again
Behavior when passing NULL is unknown (not specified)

functions.name: git_note_next
functions.description: Advance the iterator and return the current note’s blob id and the annotated object id. Continues until iteration completes.
requirements: note_id must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the id of the blob containing the note message
annotated_id must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the id of the annotated object
it must be a valid note iterator created by a git_note_*iterator*_new function
Returns 0 on success, GIT_ITEROVER when iteration is complete, or a negative error code on failure

functions.name: git_note_read
functions.signature: int git_note_read(git_note **out, git_repository *repo, const char *notes_ref, const git_oid *oid);
functions.description: Read and return the note attached to the specified object in the given repository and notes reference (defaults to "refs/notes/commits"). Caller must free the returned note with git_note_free.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the git_note; set to NULL on error
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository
notes_ref may be NULL to use the default notes reference
oid must be a non-NULL pointer to the target object id
On success, the returned git_note must be freed with git_note_free
Function returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure

functions.name: git_note_commit_read
functions.signature: int git_note_commit_read(git_note **out, git_repository *repo, git_commit *notes_commit, const git_oid *oid);
functions.description: Read and return the note attached to the specified object, looking it up within the provided notes commit. Caller must free the returned note with git_note_free.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the git_note; set to NULL on error
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository
notes_commit must be a valid git_commit that contains a notes tree
oid must be a non-NULL pointer to the target object id
On success, the returned git_note must be freed with git_note_free
Function returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure

functions.name: git_note_author
functions.description: Get the note’s author signature.
requirements: note must be a valid, non-NULL git_note
The returned pointer is const; do not modify it
Lifetime/ownership of the returned pointer is not explicitly stated; commonly it is valid while the note remains alive (inferred)

functions.name: git_note_committer
functions.description: Get the note’s committer signature.
requirements: note must be a valid, non-NULL git_note
The returned pointer is const; do not modify it
Lifetime/ownership of the returned pointer is not explicitly stated; commonly it is valid while the note remains alive (inferred)

functions.name: git_note_message
functions.description: Get the note message text.
requirements: note must be a valid, non-NULL git_note
The returned C string is const; do not modify it
Lifetime/ownership of the returned pointer is not explicitly stated; commonly it is valid while the note remains alive (inferred)

functions.name: git_note_id
functions.description: Get the id of the blob that stores the note message for this note.
requirements: note must be a valid, non-NULL git_note
The returned pointer is const; do not modify it
Lifetime/ownership of the returned pointer is not explicitly stated; commonly it is valid while the note remains alive (inferred)

functions.name: git_note_create
functions.signature: int git_note_create(git_oid *out, git_repository *repo, const char *notes_ref, const git_signature *author, const git_signature *committer, const git_oid *oid, const char *note, int force);
functions.description: Create or update a note for an object in a repository under the given notes reference (defaults to "refs/notes/commits"). Optionally returns the OID of the created/updated note blob. Writes a notes commit updating the notes reference.
requirements: out may be NULL; if non-NULL, it receives the OID of the created note blob
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository
notes_ref may be NULL to use the default notes reference
author must be a valid, non-NULL git_signature for the notes commit author
committer must be a valid, non-NULL git_signature for the notes commit committer
oid must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to the object being annotated
note must be a valid C string containing the note content (may be empty; non-NULL)
force controls overwrite: if an existing note is present and force is 0, the function returns an error; if non-zero, the note is overwritten (inferred from parameter name and docs)
Returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure

functions.name: git_note_commit_create
functions.signature: int git_note_commit_create(git_oid *notes_commit_out, git_oid *notes_blob_out, git_repository *repo, git_commit *parent, const git_signature *author, const git_signature *committer, const git_oid *oid, const char *note, int allow_note_overwrite);
functions.description: Create a notes commit that annotates an object, without creating or updating any reference. Produces a dangling commit containing the notes tree. Optionally returns the new notes commit id and the note blob id.
requirements: notes_commit_out may be NULL; if non-NULL, it receives the id of the created notes commit
notes_blob_out may be NULL; if non-NULL, it receives the id of the created note blob
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository
parent may be NULL to start a new notes tree; otherwise must be a valid notes commit to act as parent
author must be a valid, non-NULL git_signature for the notes commit author
committer must be a valid, non-NULL git_signature for the notes commit committer
oid must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to the object being annotated
note must be a valid C string containing the note content (may be empty; non-NULL)
allow_note_overwrite controls overwrite behavior if a note for oid already exists in the base notes tree (inferred from parameter name and docs)
Function returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure

functions.name: git_note_remove
functions.signature: int git_note_remove(git_repository *repo, const char *notes_ref, const git_signature *author, const git_signature *committer, const git_oid *oid);
functions.description: Remove the note for an object from the notes reference in the repository (defaults to "refs/notes/commits"). Writes a notes commit updating the reference.
requirements: repo must be a valid, opened git_repository
notes_ref may be NULL to use the default notes reference
author must be a valid, non-NULL git_signature for the notes commit author
committer must be a valid, non-NULL git_signature for the notes commit committer
oid must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to the object whose note should be removed
Function returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure

functions.name: git_note_commit_remove
functions.signature: int git_note_commit_remove(git_oid *notes_commit_out, git_repository *repo, git_commit *notes_commit, const git_signature *author, const git_signature *committer, const git_oid *oid);
functions.description: Remove the note for an object from a notes tree derived from the provided notes commit, producing a new commit with the updated notes tree. Optionally returns the id of the newly created notes commit (which may point to an empty tree).
requirements: notes_commit_out may be NULL; if non-NULL, it receives the id of the new notes commit
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository
notes_commit must be a valid git_commit representing the source notes commit
author must be a valid, non-NULL git_signature for the notes commit author
committer must be a valid, non-NULL git_signature for the notes commit committer
oid must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to the object whose note should be removed
Function returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure

functions.name: git_note_free
functions.description: Free a git_note object previously returned by git_note_read or git_note_commit_read.
requirements: note must be a git_note obtained from libgit2
After this call, the note pointer must not be used again
Do not free the same note more than once

functions.name: git_note_default_ref
functions.description: Get the repository’s default notes reference name into the provided buffer.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to a git_buf to receive the name
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository
Initialization/ownership rules for git_buf are not stated here; ensure out refers to a valid buffer structure (exact initialization requirements unknown)
Function returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure

functions.name: git_note_foreach
functions.signature: int git_note_foreach(git_repository *repo, const char *notes_ref, git_note_foreach_cb note_cb, void *payload);
functions.description: Iterate all notes within the specified notes reference (defaults to "refs/notes/commits") and invoke the callback for each note. Iteration stops when the callback returns non-zero or when all notes have been visited.
requirements: repo must be a valid, opened git_repository
notes_ref may be NULL to use the default notes reference
note_cb must be a valid, non-NULL callback function of type git_note_foreach_cb
payload is passed through to the callback and may be NULL
Callback must return 0 to continue; returning non-zero stops iteration
Function returns 0 on success, a non-zero callback return value to indicate early stop, or a negative error code on failure

functions.name: git_object_lookup
functions.signature: int git_object_lookup(git_object **object, git_repository *repo, const git_oid *id, git_object_t type);
functions.description: Look up an object by OID in a repository and return a repository-owned reference. Use git_object_free when finished. The type must match the object in the ODB or be GIT_OBJECT_ANY for automatic detection.
requirements: object must be a valid non-NULL output pointer
repo must be a valid repository pointer
id must point to a valid object ID
type must equal the object's type or be GIT_OBJECT_ANY
On success, the returned object is owned by the repository and must be released with git_object_free (do not free() manually)
Returns 0 on success, otherwise a libgit2 error code

functions.name: git_object_lookup_prefix
functions.signature: int git_object_lookup_prefix(git_object **object_out, git_repository *repo, const git_oid *id, size_t len, git_object_t type);
functions.description: Look up an object by an abbreviated OID prefix in a repository and return a repository-owned reference. The prefix length must uniquely identify an object. Use git_object_free when finished.
requirements: object_out must be a valid non-NULL output pointer
repo must be a valid repository pointer
id must point to a valid (full) object ID whose first len hex nibbles are used
len must be at least GIT_OID_MINPREFIXLEN and must uniquely identify a single object in the repository
type must equal the object's type or be GIT_OBJECT_ANY
On success, the returned object is owned by the repository and must be released with git_object_free (do not free() manually)
Returns 0 on success, otherwise a libgit2 error code

functions.name: git_object_lookup_bypath
functions.signature: int git_object_lookup_bypath(git_object **out, const git_object *treeish, const char *path, git_object_t type);
functions.description: Look up an object addressed by a path relative to a tree-ish (an object peelable to a tree). Returns a new object that the caller must free with git_object_free.
requirements: out must be a valid non-NULL output pointer
treeish must be a valid object that can be peeled to a tree
path must be a valid NUL-terminated relative path from the tree root
type specifies the desired object type and must be compatible with the looked-up entry
The returned object must be freed by the caller using git_object_free
Returns 0 on success, otherwise a libgit2 error code

functions.name: git_object_id
functions.description: Return the OID (ID) of the given object.
requirements: obj must be a valid non-NULL object pointer
The returned pointer remains valid while the object remains alive; freeing/closing the object invalidates it

functions.name: git_object_short_id
functions.description: Compute an unambiguous, abbreviated textual OID for an object, starting at the core.abbrev length and extending as needed. Writes the string to the provided git_buf.
requirements: out must be a valid git_buf for output (typically initialized)
obj must be a valid non-NULL object pointer
Returns 0 on success, <0 on error

functions.name: git_object_type
functions.description: Return the object’s type (blob, tree, commit, tag).
requirements: obj must be a valid non-NULL object pointer

functions.name: git_object_owner
functions.description: Return the repository that owns the given object. Closing the returned repository invalidates the object.
requirements: obj must be a valid non-NULL object pointer
Do not close/free the returned repository while you still need the object, as doing so invalidates the object

functions.name: git_object_free
functions.description: Release an object reference. Objects are repository-owned and may be cached; calling this releases your reference. Required to avoid leaks.
requirements: object must be a git_object previously obtained from libgit2 APIs (e.g., lookup, peel, dup, bypath)
Call exactly once per acquired reference when you are done with the object
Do not free() the object; use git_object_free

functions.name: git_object_type2string
functions.description: Convert an object type to its static string representation. The returned pointer is to static memory and must not be freed.
requirements: type should be a valid git_object_t value
The returned string must not be modified or freed

functions.name: git_object_string2type
functions.description: Convert a string representation of an object type to a git_object_t value.
requirements: str must be a valid non-NULL NUL-terminated string naming an object type

functions.name: git_object_type_is_valid
functions.description: Return 1 if the given type is a valid loose object type, 0 otherwise.
requirements: type may be any git_object_t value

functions.name: git_object_peel
functions.signature: int git_object_peel(git_object **peeled, const git_object *object, git_object_t target_type);
functions.description: Recursively peel an object until reaching the requested target type. Tags peel to their target; commits peel to their tree. Returns a new object that must be freed. Returns GIT_EINVALIDSPEC or GIT_EPEEL if peeling is not possible as requested.
requirements: peeled must be a valid non-NULL output pointer
object must be a valid non-NULL object pointer

target_type may be a specific type or GIT_OBJECT_ANY; with GIT_OBJECT_ANY, peeling continues until the type changes (tags until non-tag; commits to tree). Any other starting type with GIT_OBJECT_ANY yields GIT_EINVALIDSPEC
On success, the returned peeled object must be freed by the caller with git_object_free
Returns 0 on success, GIT_EINVALIDSPEC, GIT_EPEEL, or another error code

functions.name: git_object_dup
functions.description: Create an in-memory duplicate of a git object. The copy must be explicitly freed with git_object_free.
requirements: dest must be a valid non-NULL output pointer
source must be a valid non-NULL object pointer
On success, caller must free the duplicated object with git_object_free
Returns 0 on success or an error code

functions.name: git_object_rawcontent_is_valid
functions.signature: int git_object_rawcontent_is_valid(int *valid, const char *buf, size_t len, git_object_t object_type, git_oid_t oid_type);
functions.description: Experimental: Validate raw object content for the given object_type and OID type. Tree, commit, and tag objects are parsed to ensure validity; blobs are always valid. Sets an informative error message on failure. Signature may change in the future.
requirements: valid must be a non-NULL output pointer where 0/1 validity is stored
buf must point to the raw object content; len specifies its size
object_type specifies the type of content contained in buf (blob/tree/commit/tag)
oid_type specifies the object ID type used in the buffer (applicable when built with experimental SHA-256 support)
Returns 0 on success or an error code; on success, *valid is set to 0 or 1

functions.name: git_odb_new
functions.description: Create a new, empty object database (ODB) with no backends attached. Callers typically add one or more backends before use. This SHA1-only variant exists for compatibility; see git_odb_new_ext for SHA-256 capable creation.
requirements: odb must be a valid pointer to receive the allocated git_odb*
On success, the returned ODB must later be freed with git_odb_free
This API only supports SHA1 object databases (per header note)

functions.name: git_odb_open
functions.description: Create a new ODB and automatically attach the default loose and pack backends rooted at the provided objects directory. Intended to open a standard Git objects/ directory.
requirements: odb_out must be a valid pointer to receive the database; set to NULL by the function if open fails
objects_dir must be a path to the backends' "objects" directory (not a full repository)
On success, the returned ODB must be freed with git_odb_free
This API only supports SHA1 object databases (per header note)

functions.name: git_odb_add_disk_alternate
functions.description: Add an on-disk alternate objects store to an existing ODB. Alternates are searched after primary backends and are read-only.
requirements: odb must be a valid, initialized git_odb*
path must point to an objects directory (…/objects), not a repository root
Objects in alternates are looked up only after main backends
Writing is disabled on alternate backends

functions.name: git_odb_free
functions.description: Close and free an ODB instance. Safe to call with NULL; in that case no action is taken.
requirements: db may be NULL (no-op)
After freeing, the pointer must not be used

functions.name: git_odb_read
functions.description: Read and return an object from the ODB by its OID. The returned git_odb_object is reference-counted and internally cached; the caller must free it when done.
requirements: obj must be a valid pointer to receive the git_odb_object*
db must be a valid ODB
id must point to a valid object ID
Caller must release the returned object with git_odb_object_free

functions.name: git_odb_read_prefix
functions.signature: int git_odb_read_prefix(git_odb_object **obj, git_odb *db, const git_oid *short_id, size_t len)
functions.description: Read an object by an abbreviated OID prefix. The prefix must be long enough to uniquely identify an object across backends.
requirements: obj must be a valid pointer to receive the git_odb_object*
db must be a valid ODB
short_id must contain the prefix; the remaining (GIT_OID_SHA1_HEXSIZE - len) * 4 bits of short_id must be zero
len must be at least GIT_OID_MINPREFIXLEN and long enough to make the prefix unambiguous
Caller must release the returned object with git_odb_object_free

functions.name: git_odb_read_header
functions.signature: int git_odb_read_header(size_t *len_out, git_object_t *type_out, git_odb *db, const git_oid *id)
functions.description: Read only the header of an object (its length and type) without returning full contents. Many backends may read the entire object to provide this information.
requirements: len_out must be a valid pointer to receive the object length
type_out must be a valid pointer to receive the object type
db must be a valid ODB
id must point to a valid object ID

functions.name: git_odb_exists
functions.description: Check if an object exists in the ODB by its OID.
requirements: db must be a valid ODB
id must point to the object ID to check

functions.name: git_odb_exists_ext
functions.signature: int git_odb_exists_ext(git_odb *db, const git_oid *id, unsigned int flags)
functions.description: Check if an object exists in the ODB by its OID with extended lookup flags (e.g., to disable automatic refresh).
requirements: db must be a valid ODB
id must point to the object ID to check
flags controls lookup behavior; see git_odb_lookup_flags_t (e.g., GIT_ODB_LOOKUP_NO_REFRESH)

functions.name: git_odb_exists_prefix
functions.signature: int git_odb_exists_prefix(git_oid *out, git_odb *db, const git_oid *short_id, size_t len)
functions.description: Check for object existence by an abbreviated OID prefix, optionally returning the full OID if the prefix uniquely matches one object.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the full OID when exactly one match is found
db must be a valid ODB
short_id must contain the prefix
len is the length in hex characters of the prefix

functions.name: git_odb_expand_ids
functions.description: Batch-expand one or more abbreviated IDs (and optional types) to full OIDs and types in place. Unique matches are populated; non-unique or not found entries are zeroed. The ODB is not auto-refreshed on misses.
requirements: db must be a valid ODB
ids must point to an array of git_odb_expand_id entries to update in place
count is the number of entries in ids
Each ids[i].length is in nibbles (hex characters)
To query any type, set ids[i].type to 0 or GIT_OBJECT_ANY

functions.name: git_odb_refresh
functions.description: Refresh the ODB to load newly added on-disk data (eg, new packfiles). Typically unnecessary; libgit2 refreshes automatically on lookup failure. Use when an external process may have modified the store.
requirements: db must be a valid ODB

functions.name: git_odb_foreach
functions.description: Iterate over all objects in the ODB, invoking a callback for each. Iteration order is backend index order and may not be efficient for object access. Returning non-zero from the callback stops iteration.
requirements: db must be a valid ODB
cb must be a valid callback of type git_odb_foreach_cb
payload is user data passed to the callback
Callback must return 0 to continue; non-zero stops iteration

functions.name: git_odb_write
functions.signature: int git_odb_write(git_oid *out, git_odb *odb, const void *data, size_t len, git_object_t type)
functions.description: Write a complete object directly to the ODB in one call. Prefer streaming writes for large objects for better performance and memory use. Provided for compatibility with backends that cannot stream writes.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the resulting OID
odb must be a valid ODB
data must point to a buffer of length len
type must be a valid git_object_t for the data being stored

functions.name: git_odb_open_wstream
functions.signature: int git_odb_open_wstream(git_odb_stream **out, git_odb *db, git_object_size_t size, git_object_t type)
functions.description: Open a write-only ODB stream to create a new object with a specified final size and type. Must be finalized to take effect, and must be freed when done.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the stream
db must be a valid ODB
size must be the final size of the object to be written
type must be the intended object type
The returned stream is write-only and is not effective until git_odb_stream_finalize_write succeeds
Caller must free the stream with git_odb_stream_free

functions.name: git_odb_stream_write
functions.signature: int git_odb_stream_write(git_odb_stream *stream, const char *buffer, size_t len)
functions.description: Write data to an ODB write stream opened with git_odb_open_wstream. Fails if total written bytes exceed the declared size.
requirements: stream must be a valid ODB stream created for writing
buffer must point to len bytes to write
The cumulative bytes written must not exceed the size declared to git_odb_open_wstream

functions.name: git_odb_stream_finalize_write
functions.description: Finish writing to an ODB write stream, persist the object, and return its OID. Fails if the total bytes written do not match the declared size.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the resulting OID
stream must be a valid ODB write stream opened by git_odb_open_wstream
Total bytes written must exactly match the size declared at open time

functions.name: git_odb_stream_read
functions.description: Read up to len bytes from an ODB read stream into the provided buffer. Most backends do not support streaming reads.
requirements: stream must be a valid ODB read stream (from git_odb_open_rstream)
buffer must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes
Backend support for streaming reads may be limited

functions.name: git_odb_stream_free
functions.description: Free an ODB stream (read or write). Must always be called to avoid leaks.
requirements: stream may be NULL only if the implementation accepts it; otherwise must be a valid stream returned by ODB APIs
Caller must not use the stream after freeing

functions.name: git_odb_open_rstream
functions.signature: int git_odb_open_rstream(git_odb_stream **out, size_t *len, git_object_t *type, git_odb *db, const git_oid *oid)
functions.description: Open a read-only stream for an object by OID. Many backends do not support streaming reads; prefer git_odb_read for portability. On success, returns the stream along with the object's length and type.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the stream
len must be a valid pointer to receive the object length
type must be a valid pointer to receive the object type
db must be a valid ODB
oid must point to the target object ID
The returned stream must be freed with git_odb_stream_free

functions.name: git_odb_write_pack
functions.signature: int git_odb_write_pack(git_odb_writepack **out, git_odb *db, git_indexer_progress_cb progress_cb, void *progress_payload)
functions.description: Open a writepack to stream a packfile into the ODB. If supported, the ODB will write the pack directly to disk and create an index; otherwise it stores objects in its native format. Provides a progress callback invoked inline during network/indexing.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the writepack functions
db must be a valid ODB
progress_cb may be NULL or a valid git_indexer_progress_cb; it is called inline and may affect performance
progress_payload is passed to progress_cb

functions.name: git_odb_write_multi_pack_index
functions.description: Generate a multi-pack-index file enumerating all objects across packfiles in the ODB to speed up lookups.
requirements: db must be a valid ODB with pack files present for meaningful output

functions.name: git_odb_hash
functions.signature: int git_odb_hash(git_oid *oid, const void *data, size_t len, git_object_t object_type, git_oid_t oid_type)
functions.description: Compute the object ID for a data buffer using the specified OID type (SHA1 or SHA256). This is the ID the buffer would have if written to the ODB as the given type.
requirements: oid must be a valid pointer to receive the result
data must point to the buffer to hash of length len
object_type must specify the intended Git object type
oid_type selects the hash algorithm (SHA1/SHA256)

functions.name: git_odb_hashfile
functions.signature: int git_odb_hashfile(git_oid *oid, const char *path, git_object_t object_type, git_oid_t oid_type)
functions.description: Compute the object ID for a file on disk using the specified OID type (SHA1 or SHA256). Equivalent to hashing the file as if written to the ODB as the given type.
requirements: oid must be a valid pointer to receive the result
path must point to a readable file on disk
object_type must specify the intended Git object type
oid_type selects the hash algorithm (SHA1/SHA256)

functions.name: git_odb_object_dup
functions.description: Create a copy (additional reference) of an ODB object. Due to internal refcounting, the returned pointer equals source; both references must be freed.
requirements: dest must be a valid pointer to receive the duplicated object
source must be a valid git_odb_object*
Each successful duplication increases the reference count; caller must call git_odb_object_free once per reference

functions.name: git_odb_object_free
functions.description: Release a reference to a git_odb_object. Must be called once per acquired reference to avoid leaks.
requirements: object must be a git_odb_object previously obtained (e.g., from read/dup) or NULL if the implementation allows no-op
Do not use the object after freeing the last reference

functions.name: git_odb_object_id
functions.description: Return the OID of the provided ODB object (the ID it was read from).
requirements: object must be a valid git_odb_object*
Returned pointer is owned by the object and remains valid while the object lives

functions.name: git_odb_object_data
functions.description: Return a pointer to the object's uncompressed raw data (without the leading header). The memory is owned by the object.
requirements: object must be a valid git_odb_object*
The returned pointer must not be freed by the caller and is valid while the object remains alive

functions.name: git_odb_object_size
functions.description: Return the size in bytes of the object's data buffer (as returned by git_odb_object_data).
requirements: object must be a valid git_odb_object*

functions.name: git_odb_object_type
functions.description: Return the Git object type of the provided ODB object.
requirements: object must be a valid git_odb_object*

functions.name: git_odb_add_backend
functions.description: Attach a custom backend to an ODB with the given priority. Backends are queried in order of priority. See sys/odb_backend.h for backend interface details.
requirements: odb must be a valid ODB
backend must point to a valid git_odb_backend instance
priority controls the ordering relative to other backends
Caller is responsible for backend lifetime semantics per backend API

functions.name: git_odb_add_alternate
functions.description: Attach a custom backend as an alternate (read-only) to an ODB, searched after main backends, ordered by priority.
requirements: odb must be a valid ODB
backend must point to a valid git_odb_backend instance
priority controls the ordering relative to other alternates and backends
Writing is disabled on alternate backends

functions.name: git_odb_num_backends
functions.description: Return the number of backend objects attached to the ODB.
requirements: odb must be a valid ODB

functions.name: git_odb_get_backend
functions.description: Lookup an ODB backend by index and return it via out.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the backend pointer
odb must be a valid ODB
pos must be a valid index into the ODB's backend list (GIT_ENOTFOUND if invalid)

functions.name: git_odb_set_commit_graph
functions.description: Set or unset the commit-graph for an ODB. On success, ownership of cgraph is transferred to libgit2; pass NULL to unset.
requirements: odb must be a valid ODB
cgraph may be NULL to unset, otherwise must be a valid git_commit_graph*
After a successful call, the caller must not free cgraph (ownership transferred)

functions.name: git_odb_backend_pack
functions.signature: int git_odb_backend_pack(git_odb_backend **out, const char *objects_dir, const git_odb_backend_pack_options *opts);
functions.description: Create an object database backend that serves objects from a directory containing packfiles. Experimental-SHA256 variant. Use when you want to add a packfile-backed storage to an ODB with configurable OID type. On success, stores a backend instance in *out.
requirements: GIT_EXPERIMENTAL_SHA256 must be defined for this signature to be available.
out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created git_odb_backend*.
objects_dir must be a non-NULL path string to a Git repository's objects directory; it should exist and be readable.
opts must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized git_odb_backend_pack_options struct.
git_odb_backend_pack_options.version should be set to GIT_ODB_BACKEND_PACK_OPTIONS_VERSION.
git_odb_backend_pack_options.oid_type may be 0 for default or a supported git_oid_t value.
Return value must be checked: 0 indicates success; non-zero indicates an error code.

functions.name: git_odb_backend_one_pack
functions.signature: int git_odb_backend_one_pack(git_odb_backend **out, const char *index_file, const git_odb_backend_pack_options *opts);
functions.description: Create an object database backend that serves objects from a single packfile given its index (.idx). Experimental-SHA256 variant with configurable OID type. Useful for inspecting a specific packfile. On success, stores a backend instance in *out.
requirements: GIT_EXPERIMENTAL_SHA256 must be defined for this signature to be available.
out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created git_odb_backend*.
index_file must be a non-NULL path string to the packfile's .idx file; it should exist and be readable.
opts must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized git_odb_backend_pack_options struct.
git_odb_backend_pack_options.version should be set to GIT_ODB_BACKEND_PACK_OPTIONS_VERSION.
git_odb_backend_pack_options.oid_type may be 0 for default or a supported git_oid_t value.
Return value must be checked: 0 indicates success; non-zero indicates an error code.

functions.name: git_odb_backend_loose
functions.description: Create an object database backend that serves loose (individual) objects from an objects directory. Experimental-SHA256 variant with configurable flags, compression level, permissions, and OID type. On success, stores a backend instance in *out.
requirements: GIT_EXPERIMENTAL_SHA256 must be defined for this signature to be available.
out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created git_odb_backend*.
objects_dir must be a non-NULL path string to a Git repository's objects directory; it should exist and be readable/writable if this backend will write.
opts may be NULL or point to an initialized git_odb_backend_loose_options struct.
If opts is non-NULL, opts->version should be set to GIT_ODB_BACKEND_LOOSE_OPTIONS_VERSION.
If opts is non-NULL and opts->compression_level is set, valid values are -1 (default), 0 (no compression), or 1-9.
If opts is non-NULL, opts->flags is a bitwise OR of git_odb_backend_loose_flag_t values (e.g., GIT_ODB_BACKEND_LOOSE_FSYNC).
If opts is non-NULL, opts->dir_mode and opts->file_mode are permission modes or 0 for defaults.
If opts is non-NULL, opts->oid_type may be 0 for default or a supported git_oid_t value.
Return value must be checked: 0 indicates success; non-zero indicates an error code.

functions.name: git_packbuilder_new
functions.description: Create and initialize a new packbuilder instance for a given repository. Use this to begin constructing a packfile by inserting objects, then write or iterate the pack. The returned packbuilder must be freed with git_packbuilder_free.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created git_packbuilder*
repo must be a valid, initialized git_repository* associated with the objects to pack
Returns 0 on success; on error, a negative error code is returned and *out is not set or is invalid
Call git_packbuilder_free on the resulting packbuilder when done

functions.name: git_packbuilder_set_threads
functions.description: Configure the number of worker threads the packbuilder may use. By default, no threads are spawned; passing 0 enables autodetection of the number of CPUs. Returns the actual number of threads that will be used.
requirements: pb must be a valid git_packbuilder* created by git_packbuilder_new
n may be 0 to request autodetection; otherwise it is the desired thread count
The return value is the number of threads that will actually be used

functions.name: git_packbuilder_insert
functions.signature: int git_packbuilder_insert(git_packbuilder *pb, const git_oid *id, const char *name)
functions.description: Insert a single object into the pack being built. For optimal pack locality, insert objects in recency order (commits, then trees, then blobs). The optional name can annotate the object.
requirements: pb must be a valid git_packbuilder*
id must be a non-NULL pointer to the object’s oid in the repository
name may be NULL
Returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure
For optimal results (not required), insert in recency order as documented

functions.name: git_packbuilder_insert_tree
functions.description: Insert a root tree object and all trees and blobs it references into the pack.
requirements: pb must be a valid git_packbuilder*
id must be a non-NULL pointer to the oid of a tree object in the repository
Returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure

functions.name: git_packbuilder_insert_commit
functions.description: Insert a commit object and the complete referenced tree into the pack.
requirements: pb must be a valid git_packbuilder*
id must be a non-NULL pointer to the oid of a commit object in the repository
Returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure

functions.name: git_packbuilder_insert_walk
functions.description: Insert all commits produced by the given revwalk and all objects they reference into the pack.
requirements: pb must be a valid git_packbuilder*
walk must be a valid, initialized git_revwalk* configured to iterate the desired commits
Returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure
The revwalk should be associated with the same repository as the packbuilder (inferred from typical libgit2 usage)

functions.name: git_packbuilder_insert_recur
functions.description: Recursively insert an object and all objects it references. The optional name can annotate the root object.
requirements: pb must be a valid git_packbuilder*
id must be a non-NULL pointer to the oid of the root object
name may be NULL
Returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure

functions.name: git_packbuilder_write_buf
functions.description: Write the built packfile contents into a memory buffer. The resulting buffer contains a valid packfile without an accompanying index.
requirements: buf must be a valid, initialized git_buf* to receive data
pb must be a valid git_packbuilder* with objects inserted
Returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure

functions.name: git_packbuilder_write
functions.signature: int git_packbuilder_write(git_packbuilder *pb, const char *path, unsigned int mode, git_indexer_progress_cb progress_cb, void *progress_cb_payload)
functions.description: Write the generated packfile and its index to the specified directory (or the default location if path is NULL). Optionally reports progress through the provided indexer progress callback.
requirements: pb must be a valid git_packbuilder*
path may be NULL to use the default repository location; otherwise it must name a directory path where the pack and index will be stored
mode is the file permission mode for creating the packfile; use 0 for defaults
progress_cb may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must conform to git_indexer_progress_cb and may be called inline during write
progress_cb_payload is passed back to progress_cb
Returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure

functions.name: git_packbuilder_hash
functions.description: Return the packfile’s hash (used to derive its filename). This value is only valid after the packfile has been written. Deprecated in favor of git_packbuilder_name.
requirements: pb must be a valid git_packbuilder*
Must be called only after the packfile has been written (e.g., after git_packbuilder_write or a pack creation routine) to ensure correctness
Function is deprecated; prefer git_packbuilder_name

functions.name: git_packbuilder_name
functions.description: Return the unique name (filename) for the resulting packfile. The name is derived from the pack’s content and is only correct after the packfile has been written.
requirements: pb must be a valid git_packbuilder*
Must be called only after the packfile has been written to ensure the returned name is correct
Returns a NUL-terminated string pointer owned by libgit2 (do not free)

functions.name: git_packbuilder_foreach
functions.description: Create the pack and invoke the callback once for each packed object’s buffer. Iteration stops early if the callback returns non-zero.
requirements: pb must be a valid git_packbuilder*
cb must be a non-NULL function matching git_packbuilder_foreach_cb; returning non-zero terminates iteration
payload is user data passed to cb and may be NULL
Returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure

functions.name: git_packbuilder_object_count
functions.description: Get the total number of objects that the packbuilder will write.
requirements: pb must be a valid git_packbuilder*

functions.name: git_packbuilder_written
functions.description: Get the number of objects the packbuilder has already written out.
requirements: pb must be a valid git_packbuilder*

functions.name: git_packbuilder_set_callbacks
functions.description: Set a progress callback for pack building. The callback may be invoked inline with packbuilding operations; if it returns an error, pack building is aborted and that error is returned from the invoking function.
requirements: pb must be a valid git_packbuilder*
progress_cb may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must match git_packbuilder_progress and be safe to call from packbuilding context (may affect performance)
If progress_cb returns an error, pack building is aborted and the error is propagated; the packbuilder must then be freed and not reused (per documentation)
progress_cb_payload is passed to the progress callback and may be NULL
Returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure

functions.name: git_packbuilder_free
functions.description: Free the packbuilder and all associated resources.
requirements: pb must be a valid git_packbuilder* previously created by git_packbuilder_new (NULL-acceptance is unknown)
After this call, pb must not be used again

functions.name: git_patch_owner
functions.description: Returns the repository that the given patch is associated with (may be NULL). Use to discover the owning repository for context or follow-up operations.
requirements: patch must be a valid pointer to a git_patch (may not be NULL).
Return value may be NULL; callers must handle a NULL repository pointer.

functions.name: git_patch_from_diff
functions.description: Create a git_patch representing the text diff for the delta at index idx in the provided diff. The created patch must be freed with git_patch_free. For unchanged or binary files, no patch is created; *out will be set to NULL and the delta’s binary flag is set.
requirements: diff must be a valid git_diff pointer.
idx must refer to a valid entry within diff (0 <= idx < number of deltas).
out may be NULL; when NULL, the text diff is not calculated.
On success returns 0; on error returns < 0; callers must check the return value.
If the delta is unchanged or binary, *out will be set to NULL; callers must handle this case and must not call git_patch_free on NULL.

functions.name: git_patch_from_blobs
functions.signature: int git_patch_from_blobs(git_patch **out, const git_blob *old_blob, const char *old_as_path, const git_blob *new_blob, const char *new_as_path, const git_diff_options *opts);
functions.description: Generate a patch representing the textual differences between two blobs. Behaves like git_diff_blobs but returns a patch object instead of using callbacks. The resulting patch must be freed with git_patch_free.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the patch; will be set to NULL on error.
old_blob may be NULL to represent an empty blob.
new_blob may be NULL to represent an empty blob.
old_as_path and new_as_path may be NULL; when provided, they are used as display paths in the patch.
opts may be NULL for default options; otherwise must point to a valid git_diff_options.
Returns 0 on success, negative error code on failure; callers must check the return value.
On success, the caller owns the returned patch and must call git_patch_free; do not free on error when *out is NULL.

functions.name: git_patch_from_blob_and_buffer
functions.signature: int git_patch_from_blob_and_buffer(git_patch **out, const git_blob *old_blob, const char *old_as_path, const void *buffer, size_t buffer_len, const char *buffer_as_path, const git_diff_options *opts);
functions.description: Generate a patch representing the textual differences between an existing blob and a raw memory buffer. Similar to git_diff_blob_to_buffer but produces a patch object. The resulting patch must be freed with git_patch_free.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the patch; will be set to NULL on error.
old_blob may be NULL to represent an empty blob.
old_as_path and buffer_as_path may be NULL; when provided, they are used as display paths in the patch.
buffer may be NULL to represent an empty buffer; if NULL, buffer_len is typically ignored (treated as 0).
buffer_len specifies the size of buffer in bytes when buffer is non-NULL.
opts may be NULL for default options; otherwise must point to a valid git_diff_options.
Returns 0 on success, negative error code on failure; callers must check the return value.
On success, the caller owns the returned patch and must call git_patch_free; do not free on error when *out is NULL.

functions.name: git_patch_from_buffers
functions.signature: int git_patch_from_buffers(git_patch **out, const void *old_buffer, size_t old_len, const char *old_as_path, const void *new_buffer, size_t new_len, const char *new_as_path, const git_diff_options *opts);
functions.description: Generate a patch representing the textual differences between two raw memory buffers. Similar to git_diff_buffers but produces a patch object. The resulting patch must be freed with git_patch_free.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the patch; will be set to NULL on error.
old_buffer may be NULL to represent an empty buffer; old_len is treated as 0 in that case.
new_buffer may be NULL to represent an empty buffer; new_len is treated as 0 in that case.
old_as_path and new_as_path may be NULL; when provided, they are used as display paths in the patch.
opts may be NULL for default options; otherwise must point to a valid git_diff_options.
Returns 0 on success, negative error code on failure; callers must check the return value.
On success, the caller owns the returned patch and must call git_patch_free; do not free on error when *out is NULL.

functions.name: git_patch_free
functions.description: Release a git_patch object created by libgit2. Safe to call with NULL.
requirements: patch may be NULL (no operation).
patch must have been allocated/returned by libgit2 patch creation functions; do not free memory you do not own.

functions.name: git_patch_get_delta
functions.description: Return the diff delta associated with the patch. The returned pointer is to internal data owned by the patch and must not be freed by the caller.
requirements: patch must be a valid pointer to a git_patch.
Returned git_diff_delta pointer is borrowed; do not free or modify it; its lifetime is tied to the patch.

functions.name: git_patch_num_hunks
functions.description: Return the number of hunks contained in the given patch.
requirements: patch must be a valid pointer to a git_patch.

functions.name: git_patch_line_stats
functions.signature: int git_patch_line_stats(size_t *total_context, size_t *total_additions, size_t *total_deletions, const git_patch *patch);
functions.description: Compute counts of context, addition, and deletion lines in the patch, useful for numstat-like output. Any of the output pointers may be NULL if that count is not needed.
requirements: patch must be a valid pointer to a git_patch.
total_context may be NULL if not needed.
total_additions may be NULL if not needed.
total_deletions may be NULL if not needed.
Returns 0 on success; returns < 0 on error; callers must check the return value.

functions.name: git_patch_get_hunk
functions.signature: int git_patch_get_hunk(const git_diff_hunk **out, size_t *lines_in_hunk, git_patch *patch, size_t hunk_idx);
functions.description: Retrieve information about the hunk at index hunk_idx in the patch. Optionally returns the number of lines in that hunk. Any output pointer may be NULL if not needed.
requirements: patch must be a valid pointer to a git_patch.
hunk_idx must be less than git_patch_num_hunks(patch); otherwise returns GIT_ENOTFOUND.
out may be NULL if the hunk data is not needed; otherwise must be a valid pointer to receive a borrowed git_diff_hunk pointer.
lines_in_hunk may be NULL if the count is not needed; otherwise must be a valid pointer to receive the line count.
Returned git_diff_hunk pointer is borrowed; do not free or modify it; its lifetime is tied to the patch.
Returns 0 on success, GIT_ENOTFOUND if hunk_idx is out of range, or < 0 on other errors; callers must check the return value.

functions.name: git_patch_num_lines_in_hunk
functions.description: Return the number of lines in the specified hunk of the patch, or GIT_ENOTFOUND if hunk_idx is invalid.
requirements: patch must be a valid pointer to a git_patch.
hunk_idx must be less than git_patch_num_hunks(patch).
Callers must check for negative return values indicating errors or GIT_ENOTFOUND.

functions.name: git_patch_get_line_in_hunk
functions.signature: int git_patch_get_line_in_hunk(const git_diff_line **out, git_patch *patch, size_t hunk_idx, size_t line_of_hunk);
functions.description: Return detailed information about a specific line within a hunk in the patch. The returned line data is borrowed from the patch.
requirements: patch must be a valid pointer to a git_patch.
hunk_idx must be less than git_patch_num_hunks(patch).
line_of_hunk must be less than the number of lines in the specified hunk (as returned by git_patch_num_lines_in_hunk).
out must be a valid pointer to receive a borrowed git_diff_line pointer.
Returns 0 on success; returns < 0 on failure (e.g., out-of-range indices).
Returned git_diff_line pointer is borrowed; do not free or modify it; its lifetime is tied to the patch.

functions.name: git_patch_size
functions.signature: size_t git_patch_size(git_patch *patch, int include_context, int include_hunk_headers, int include_file_headers);
functions.description: Return the size in bytes of the textual patch data. By toggling include_context, include_hunk_headers, and include_file_headers, you can compute sizes for changed lines only or for the full patch output.
requirements: patch must be a valid pointer to a git_patch.
include_context is treated as boolean (non-zero to include context lines).
include_hunk_headers is treated as boolean (non-zero to include hunk headers).
include_file_headers is treated as boolean (non-zero to include file headers).

functions.name: git_patch_print
functions.description: Serialize the patch to text, invoking the provided callback for file headers, hunk headers, and diff lines. If the callback returns non-zero, iteration is terminated and that value is returned.
requirements: patch must be a valid pointer to a git_patch.
print_cb must be a valid function conforming to git_diff_line_cb; it will be invoked for each output line.
payload is an opaque pointer passed through to the callback and may be NULL.
Returns 0 on success, a non-zero value returned by the callback, or a negative error code; callers must check the return value.
The callback must be prepared to be called multiple times and should not assume null-termination of provided buffers unless guaranteed by git_diff_line_cb semantics (details not specified here).

functions.name: git_patch_to_buf
functions.description: Render the patch to a single diff text stored in a git_buf.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to a git_buf to receive the output; ownership of the internal buffer remains with out and must be managed per git_buf conventions.
patch must be a valid pointer to a git_patch.
Returns 0 on success; returns < 0 on failure; callers must check the return value.

functions.name: git_pathspec_new
functions.description: Compile a pathspec from a string array of patterns into an opaque git_pathspec object for reuse in matching operations. Typical usage: prepare a git_strarray of path patterns, call this function to obtain a compiled pathspec, use it with the match APIs, then free it with git_pathspec_free.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the resulting git_pathspec on success.
pathspec must point to a valid, initialized git_strarray whose strings are valid C strings.
Return value must be checked: 0 indicates success, a negative value indicates failure.
On success, the returned git_pathspec must be released with git_pathspec_free to avoid memory leaks.

functions.name: git_pathspec_free
functions.description: Free a compiled git_pathspec created by git_pathspec_new. After this call, the git_pathspec pointer must not be used.
requirements: ps must be a git_pathspec previously returned by git_pathspec_new.
Behavior for ps == NULL is unknown/not documented; callers should avoid passing NULL unless confirmed by library guarantees.

functions.name: git_pathspec_matches_path
functions.signature: int git_pathspec_matches_path(const git_pathspec *ps, uint32_t flags, const char *path);
functions.description: Test whether a single path matches a compiled pathspec, using only the specified flags for case sensitivity and globbing. This function does not fall back to platform-native case sensitivity unless you choose the appropriate flags; by default it is case sensitive.
requirements: ps must be a valid compiled git_pathspec.
flags is a bitwise OR of git_pathspec_flag_t values (e.g., GIT_PATHSPEC_IGNORE_CASE, GIT_PATHSPEC_USE_CASE, GIT_PATHSPEC_NO_GLOB, etc.).
path must be a valid, NUL-terminated C string representing the pathname to test.
Return value is 1 if the path matches, 0 if it does not. Error conditions are not documented; callers should treat non-1/0 returns as unknown/unsupported.

functions.name: git_pathspec_match_workdir
functions.description: Match a compiled pathspec against the current working directory of a repository, honoring git ignores (ignored files will not match unless tracked in the index). Optionally returns a git_pathspec_match_list with results and/or failures, depending on flags.
requirements: repo must be a valid, non-bare repository; calling this on a bare repository is an error.
ps must be a valid compiled git_pathspec.

flags is a bitwise OR of git_pathspec_flag_t values. Use GIT_PATHSPEC_NO_MATCH_ERROR to get GIT_ENOTFOUND when there are no matches; use GIT_PATHSPEC_FIND_FAILURES to track unmatched patterns; use GIT_PATHSPEC_FAILURES_ONLY to omit matched filenames and only track failures or presence of matches.
out may be NULL to ignore detailed results; if non-NULL and the call succeeds, the returned list must be freed with git_pathspec_match_list_free.
Return values: 0 on success, -1 on error, or GIT_ENOTFOUND if there are no matches and GIT_PATHSPEC_NO_MATCH_ERROR is specified.

functions.name: git_pathspec_match_index
functions.description: Match a compiled pathspec against entries in a git index. Optionally returns a git_pathspec_match_list with results and/or failures. Note: currently, case sensitivity is governed by the index’s own setting; USE_CASE and IGNORE_CASE flags have no effect (subject to change in a future release).
requirements: index must be a valid git_index object to match against.
ps must be a valid compiled git_pathspec.
flags is a bitwise OR of git_pathspec_flag_t values. Be aware that case-sensitivity flags currently do not affect index matching.
out may be NULL to ignore detailed results; if non-NULL and the call succeeds, the returned list must be freed with git_pathspec_match_list_free.
Return values: 0 on success, -1 on error, or GIT_ENOTFOUND if there are no matches and GIT_PATHSPEC_NO_MATCH_ERROR is specified.

functions.name: git_pathspec_match_tree
functions.description: Match a compiled pathspec against files contained in a given tree object. Optionally returns a git_pathspec_match_list with results and/or failures.
requirements: tree must be a valid root-level git_tree to match against.
ps must be a valid compiled git_pathspec.
flags is a bitwise OR of git_pathspec_flag_t values.
out may be NULL to ignore detailed results; if non-NULL and the call succeeds, the returned list must be freed with git_pathspec_match_list_free.
Return values: 0 on success, -1 on error, or GIT_ENOTFOUND if there are no matches and GIT_PATHSPEC_NO_MATCH_ERROR is specified.

functions.name: git_pathspec_match_diff
functions.description: Match a compiled pathspec against file changes in a generated diff. Optionally returns a git_pathspec_match_list with results and/or failures. Use git_pathspec_match_list_diff_entry to read results from a diff-generated list.
requirements: diff must be a valid, already generated git_diff object.
ps must be a valid compiled git_pathspec.
flags is a bitwise OR of git_pathspec_flag_t values.
out may be NULL to ignore detailed results; if non-NULL and the call succeeds, the returned list must be freed with git_pathspec_match_list_free.
Return values: 0 on success, -1 on error, or GIT_ENOTFOUND if there are no matches and GIT_PATHSPEC_NO_MATCH_ERROR is specified.

functions.name: git_pathspec_match_list_free
functions.description: Free a git_pathspec_match_list created by a pathspec match function. After this call, the list pointer must not be used.
requirements: m must be a git_pathspec_match_list previously returned by a match function (e.g., git_pathspec_match_workdir/index/tree/diff).
Behavior for m == NULL is unknown/not documented; callers should avoid passing NULL unless confirmed by library guarantees.

functions.name: git_pathspec_match_list_entrycount
functions.description: Return the number of items in a match list. If GIT_PATHSPEC_FAILURES_ONLY was used, this may be zero even when matches existed, as the list may omit matched filenames.
requirements: m must be a valid git_pathspec_match_list returned by a match function.

functions.name: git_pathspec_match_list_entry
functions.description: Get a matched filename by index from a match list. This is not applicable to lists generated by git_pathspec_match_diff; in that case, this function always returns NULL.
requirements: m must be a valid git_pathspec_match_list.
m must have been generated by a non-diff match function; if generated by git_pathspec_match_diff, this function will always return NULL.
pos must be within [0, git_pathspec_match_list_entrycount(m)); out-of-range behavior is unspecified (NULL on failure is implied by general libgit2 patterns but not explicitly stated).
If the list was created with GIT_PATHSPEC_FAILURES_ONLY, filenames may not be retained and this may yield no entries.

functions.name: git_pathspec_match_list_diff_entry
functions.description: Get a git_diff_delta by index from a match list created by git_pathspec_match_diff. For lists not created by the diff match function, this will always return NULL.
requirements: m must be a valid git_pathspec_match_list.
m must have been generated by git_pathspec_match_diff; otherwise this function will always return NULL.
pos must be within [0, git_pathspec_match_list_entrycount(m)); out-of-range behavior is unspecified (NULL on failure is implied by general libgit2 patterns but not explicitly stated).

functions.name: git_pathspec_match_list_failed_entrycount
functions.description: Return the number of pathspec items that did not match anything. This will be zero unless the match list was created with GIT_PATHSPEC_FIND_FAILURES.
requirements: m must be a valid git_pathspec_match_list.
Meaningful non-zero results require that the match was performed with GIT_PATHSPEC_FIND_FAILURES.

functions.name: git_pathspec_match_list_failed_entry
functions.description: Return the original pathspec pattern that had no matches, by index within the failures list. Returns NULL for out-of-range positions.
requirements: m must be a valid git_pathspec_match_list.
Meaningful results require that the match was performed with GIT_PATHSPEC_FIND_FAILURES; otherwise the failures list will be empty.
pos must be within [0, git_pathspec_match_list_failed_entrycount(m)]; positions out of range return NULL.

functions.name: git_proxy_options_init
functions.description: Initializes a git_proxy_options structure with libgit2’s default values, equivalent to assigning GIT_PROXY_OPTIONS_INIT. Typical usage is to call this before customizing fields (type, url, callbacks) and then passing the struct to APIs that accept proxy options. Returns 0 on success and -1 on failure (reason not specified).
requirements: opts must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to writable memory for a git_proxy_options structure.
version must be GIT_PROXY_OPTIONS_VERSION.
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success, -1 indicates failure.
If initialization succeeds, the structure will be set to default values as per GIT_PROXY_OPTIONS_INIT before any caller modifications.

functions.name: git_rebase_options_init
functions.description: Initialize a git_rebase_options struct with default values. Callers pass the struct to configure subsequent rebase operations.
requirements: opts must point to writable storage for a git_rebase_options structure.
version must be GIT_REBASE_OPTIONS_VERSION.
Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure (caller should handle nonzero as error).

functions.name: git_rebase_init
functions.signature: int git_rebase_init(git_rebase **out, git_repository *repo, const git_annotated_commit *branch, const git_annotated_commit *upstream, const git_annotated_commit *onto, const git_rebase_options *opts);
functions.description: Create and initialize a rebase operation to transplant commits from branch relative to upstream onto onto. After creation, iterate operations with git_rebase_next; when done, free with git_rebase_free.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the allocated git_rebase object.
repo must be a valid, open git_repository.
branch may be NULL to rebase the current branch.
upstream may be NULL to rebase all reachable commits.
onto may be NULL to rebase onto upstream.
opts may be NULL or point to an initialized git_rebase_options (if provided).
On success, the returned git_rebase must later be released with git_rebase_free.
Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure.

functions.name: git_rebase_open
functions.description: Open an existing in-progress rebase in the given repository that was started earlier (by libgit2 or another client).
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the git_rebase object.
repo must reference a repository that currently has a rebase in progress.
opts must point to a git_rebase_options (the header does not state that NULL is accepted).
On success, the returned git_rebase must be released with git_rebase_free.
Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure.

functions.name: git_rebase_orig_head_name
functions.description: Retrieve the original HEAD reference name for merge-style rebases.
requirements: rebase must be a valid, in-progress git_rebase instance.
Only meaningful for merge rebases; value for other modes is not described.
Returned pointer is owned by the rebase; lifetime tied to the git_rebase object.

functions.name: git_rebase_orig_head_id
functions.description: Retrieve the original HEAD commit id (OID) for merge-style rebases.
requirements: rebase must be a valid, in-progress git_rebase instance.
Only meaningful for merge rebases; value for other modes is not described.
Returned pointer is owned by the rebase; lifetime tied to the git_rebase object.

functions.name: git_rebase_onto_name
functions.description: Retrieve the onto reference name for merge-style rebases.
requirements: rebase must be a valid, in-progress git_rebase instance.
Only meaningful for merge rebases; value for other modes is not described.
Returned pointer is owned by the rebase; lifetime tied to the git_rebase object.

functions.name: git_rebase_onto_id
functions.description: Retrieve the onto commit id (OID) for merge-style rebases.
requirements: rebase must be a valid, in-progress git_rebase instance.
Only meaningful for merge rebases; value for other modes is not described.
Returned pointer is owned by the rebase; lifetime tied to the git_rebase object.

functions.name: git_rebase_operation_entrycount
functions.description: Return the total number of rebase operations to be applied in this rebase session.
requirements: rebase must be a valid, in-progress git_rebase instance.

functions.name: git_rebase_operation_current
functions.description: Return the index (0-based) of the operation currently being applied, or GIT_REBASE_NO_OPERATION if none have been applied yet.
requirements: rebase must be a valid, in-progress git_rebase instance.
Caller should handle the special value GIT_REBASE_NO_OPERATION (SIZE_MAX) when init was called but next has not yet been called.

functions.name: git_rebase_operation_byindex
functions.description: Retrieve the rebase operation at the given index. Returns NULL if the index is out of bounds.
requirements: rebase must be a valid, in-progress git_rebase instance.
idx must be within [0, git_rebase_operation_entrycount(rebase)) to get a non-NULL result.
Returned pointer refers to internal data owned by the rebase; do not free.

functions.name: git_rebase_next
functions.description: Advance to and perform the next rebase operation, returning information about it. For non-EXEC operations, applies the patch, updating the index and (if not in-memory) working directory. Resolve any conflicts before committing.
requirements: operation must be a valid pointer to receive the current operation descriptor.
rebase must be a valid, in-progress git_rebase instance.
Caller must resolve any conflicts produced before calling git_rebase_commit.
Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure.

functions.name: git_rebase_inmemory_index
functions.description: Get the result index produced by the last git_rebase_next operation for in-memory rebases. Useful for resolving conflicts before committing. Caller owns the returned index and must free it.
requirements: index must be a valid pointer to receive the git_index result.
rebase must be a valid, in-progress git_rebase instance.
Only applicable for in-memory rebases; for working-directory rebases, changes are applied to the repository index.
Caller must call git_index_free on the returned index when finished.
Returns 0 on success or a libgit2 error code on failure.

functions.name: git_rebase_commit
functions.signature: int git_rebase_commit(git_oid *id, git_rebase *rebase, const git_signature *author, const git_signature *committer, const char *message_encoding, const char *message);
functions.description: Commit the current patch produced by the last git_rebase_next. Optionally override author, message encoding, and message. May be influenced by rebase options (eg, commit_create_cb, signing).
requirements: id must be a valid pointer to receive the OID of the newly created commit.
rebase must be a valid, in-progress git_rebase instance.
All conflicts from the preceding git_rebase_next must be resolved before calling.
author may be NULL to keep the original commit's author.
committer must be provided (non-NULL) per the parameter description.
message may be NULL to use the original commit message.
If message is NULL, message_encoding must be NULL to keep the original encoding; if message is provided, message_encoding may be NULL to imply UTF-8.
Returns 0 on success; returns GIT_EUNMERGED if there are unmerged changes, GIT_EAPPLIED if the commit is already applied, or -1 on other failures.

functions.name: git_rebase_abort
functions.description: Abort the in-progress rebase, resetting the repository and working directory to their pre-rebase state (matching git semantics, with checkout options implying FORCE during abort).
requirements: rebase must be a valid, in-progress git_rebase instance.
Returns 0 on success; returns GIT_ENOTFOUND if a rebase is not in progress; returns -1 on other errors.

functions.name: git_rebase_finish
functions.description: Finish an in-progress rebase after all patches have been applied, optionally recording the identity that finished the rebase.
requirements: rebase must be a valid, in-progress git_rebase instance.
signature may be NULL or a valid git_signature to attribute the finish operation.
Returns 0 on success; -1 on error.

functions.name: git_rebase_free
functions.description: Free a git_rebase object and release its resources.
requirements: rebase may be NULL or a valid git_rebase pointer previously returned by git_rebase_init or git_rebase_open (NULL handling is typical in libgit2 but not explicitly stated here; callers should avoid double-free).
After calling, the rebase pointer must not be used.

functions.name: git_refdb_new
functions.description: Create a new, empty reference database object for the given repository without attaching any backend. Intended for advanced use where a custom backend will be installed via git_refdb_set_backend() before any read/write operations. Returns 0 on success and a negative error code on failure; on failure, *out is set to NULL. The returned refdb must be freed with git_refdb_free when no longer needed.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a git_refdb* storage location; the function writes the created handle to *out on success and sets *out to NULL on failure.
repo must be a valid, initialized git_repository* corresponding to the repository for which the refdb is created.
After successful creation, a backend must be set with git_refdb_set_backend() before using the refdb for reading or writing references.
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success; non-zero indicates an error and that *out is NULL.
The resulting refdb handle, if created, must be released with git_refdb_free.

functions.name: git_refdb_open
functions.description: Create a new reference database for the given repository and automatically attach the default on-disk backends (loose and packed refs). Suitable for typical usage where the standard files-based backend is desired. Returns 0 on success and a negative error code on failure; on failure, *out is set to NULL. The returned refdb must be freed with git_refdb_free when done.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a git_refdb* storage location; the function writes the created handle to *out on success and sets *out to NULL on failure.
repo must be a valid, initialized git_repository* for which the default ref storage will be opened.
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success; non-zero indicates an error and that *out is NULL.
The resulting refdb handle, if created, must be released with git_refdb_free.

functions.name: git_refdb_compress
functions.description: Request the reference database to compress or optimize its references. The exact behavior is implementation-specific; for file-based ref storage this may pack loose references. Returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure.
requirements: refdb must be a valid, initialized git_refdb* previously created/opened (e.g., by git_refdb_new with a backend set, or by git_refdb_open).
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success; non-zero indicates an error.

functions.name: git_refdb_free
functions.description: Close and free a reference database object, releasing all associated resources. It is safe to pass NULL; in that case, no action is taken.
requirements: refdb may be NULL; passing NULL is a no-op.
refdb must not be used after this call; all references to it become invalid.

functions.name: git_reflog_read
functions.description: Reads the reflog for the given reference name from the repository into a new in‑memory git_reflog object. If the reference has no reflog file yet, returns an empty reflog object. The caller owns the returned object and must free it with git_reflog_free().
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the allocated git_reflog*
repo must be a valid, initialized git_repository* opened by the caller
name must be a valid reference name string identifying the target reference
On success returns 0; on failure returns a libgit2 error code which the caller must check
The resulting reflog object must be freed with git_reflog_free()

functions.name: git_reflog_write
functions.description: Atomically writes an existing in‑memory reflog object back to disk using a file lock. Use after modifying a reflog (e.g., via git_reflog_append or git_reflog_drop) to persist changes.
requirements: reflog must be a valid, non-NULL git_reflog* previously obtained (e.g., via git_reflog_read)
On success returns 0; on failure returns a libgit2 error code which the caller must check

functions.name: git_reflog_append
functions.signature: int git_reflog_append(git_reflog *reflog, const git_oid *id, const git_signature *committer, const char *msg);
