functions.description: Appends a new entry to the in‑memory reflog for a reference. The new entry records that the reference now points to id, along with the committer and an optional message. Changes are in-memory until written with git_reflog_write().
requirements: reflog must be a valid, non-NULL git_reflog*
id must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to the destination git_oid
committer must be a valid, non-NULL git_signature*
msg may be NULL; if non-NULL it must point to a NUL-terminated string
Returns 0 on success; otherwise a libgit2 error code which the caller must check
Appending only affects memory; call git_reflog_write() to persist

functions.name: git_reflog_rename
functions.signature: int git_reflog_rename(git_repository *repo, const char *old_name, const char *name);
functions.description: Renames an existing reflog within a repository from old_name to name. The new name is validated using the same rules as reference name validation (see git_reference_create_symbolic()).
requirements: repo must be a valid, initialized git_repository*
The reflog identified by old_name is expected to already exist
name must be a valid new reference name per libgit2 reference naming rules; invalid names result in GIT_EINVALIDSPEC or another error code
On success returns 0; on failure returns GIT_EINVALIDSPEC or another libgit2 error code which the caller must check

functions.name: git_reflog_delete
functions.description: Deletes the reflog for the given reference name from the repository.
requirements: repo must be a valid, initialized git_repository*
name must be the name of the reflog/reference to delete
Returns 0 on success; otherwise a libgit2 error code which the caller must check

functions.name: git_reflog_entrycount
functions.description: Returns the number of log entries currently present in the given in‑memory reflog.
requirements: reflog must be a valid, non-NULL git_reflog* previously loaded
Caller should not assume thread-safety; call from a context where the reflog is not concurrently modified
Return value is the count; no error code is returned

functions.name: git_reflog_entry_byindex
functions.description: Returns the reflog entry at the given index. Index 0 corresponds to the most recently created entry. Returns NULL if the index is out of range.
requirements: reflog must be a valid, non-NULL git_reflog*
idx must be less than git_reflog_entrycount(reflog); 0 is the most recent entry
The returned pointer is const and must not be freed by the caller; it remains valid as long as the owning reflog is not modified or freed
Returns NULL if not found; caller must check for NULL before dereferencing

functions.name: git_reflog_drop
functions.signature: int git_reflog_drop(git_reflog *reflog, size_t idx, int rewrite_previous_entry);
functions.description: Removes a log entry at the specified index from the in‑memory reflog. If rewrite_previous_entry is 1, the previous entry’s old_oid (if any) is rewritten to match the next entry’s new_oid to avoid gaps in history. Persist changes with git_reflog_write().
requirements: reflog must be a valid, non-NULL git_reflog*
idx must be less than git_reflog_entrycount(reflog); 0 is the most recent entry
rewrite_previous_entry must be 0 or 1 to select behavior
Returns 0 on success; returns GIT_ENOTFOUND if the entry does not exist, or another libgit2 error code
Dropping only affects memory; call git_reflog_write() to persist

functions.name: git_reflog_entry_id_old
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the old object ID (OID) recorded in the given reflog entry (the OID the reference pointed to before the change).
requirements: entry must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a git_reflog_entry
Returned pointer is owned by the entry/reflog; caller must not free it and must not use it after the owning reflog is modified or freed

functions.name: git_reflog_entry_id_new
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the new object ID (OID) recorded in the given reflog entry (the OID the reference points to after the change).
requirements: entry must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a git_reflog_entry
Returned pointer is owned by the entry/reflog; caller must not free it and must not use it after the owning reflog is modified or freed

functions.name: git_reflog_entry_committer
functions.description: Returns the committer signature associated with the given reflog entry.
requirements: entry must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a git_reflog_entry
Returned pointer is owned by the entry/reflog; caller must not free it and must not use it after the owning reflog is modified or freed

functions.name: git_reflog_entry_message
functions.description: Returns the message string associated with the given reflog entry, or possibly NULL if no message was recorded.
requirements: entry must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a git_reflog_entry
Returned pointer is owned by the entry/reflog; caller must not free it and must not use it after the owning reflog is modified or freed
Caller must check for NULL before using the returned pointer

functions.name: git_reflog_free
functions.description: Frees a git_reflog object previously returned by git_reflog_read. After this call, any pointers obtained from the reflog or its entries become invalid.
requirements: reflog must be a valid git_reflog* previously allocated by libgit2; behavior on NULL is unspecified in this header, so pass non-NULL to be safe
Caller must not use the reflog or any pointers returned from it after freeing

functions.name: git_reference_lookup
functions.description: Lookup a reference by its fully qualified name in the given repository and return a reference object. The name is validated. The returned reference must be freed by the caller with git_reference_free. Typical usage is to resolve refs like "HEAD" or "refs/heads/main".
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the git_reference* result
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository*
name must be a valid reference name per git_reference_symbolic_create() rules; function may return GIT_EINVALIDSPEC if invalid
Caller must free the returned reference with git_reference_free on success
Check return value: 0 on success; GIT_ENOTFOUND if ref missing; GIT_EINVALIDSPEC or other error codes on failure

functions.name: git_reference_name_to_id
functions.signature:
GIT_EXTERN(int) git_reference_name_to_id(
	git_oid *out, git_repository *repo, const char *name);
functions.description: Resolve a reference name directly to the OID it points to without allocating a git_reference object. Useful for fast lookups like resolving tags or branches to their tip OID.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to a git_oid to be filled
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository*
name must be a valid reference name; invalid names yield GIT_EINVALIDSPEC
Check return value: 0 on success; GIT_ENOTFOUND or GIT_EINVALIDSPEC or other error code on failure

functions.name: git_reference_dwim
functions.description: Resolve a shorthand reference name (DWIM) using git precedence rules and return the matching reference. The returned reference must be freed by the caller.
requirements: out must be non-NULL
repo must be a valid git_repository*
shorthand must be a non-NULL C string
Caller must free the returned reference with git_reference_free
Check return value: 0 on success; non-zero on failure

functions.name: git_reference_symbolic_create_matching
functions.signature: GIT_EXTERN(int) git_reference_symbolic_create_matching(git_reference **out, git_repository *repo, const char *name, const char *target, int force, const char *current_value, const char *log_message);
functions.description: Create or update a symbolic reference to point to another reference name, conditionally ensuring the current value matches current_value. Writes to disk and returns the created reference. The name and target are validated. Overwrites existing ref if force is non-zero.
requirements: out must be non-NULL to receive the new reference
repo must be a valid repository
name must be a valid reference name per rules documented (top-level caps/underscore or refs/* without forbidden characters and sequences)
target must be a valid reference name
If force is zero and a reference with name exists, function returns GIT_EEXISTS
If current_value is all zeros, function returns GIT_EMODIFIED if the ref already exists
Function returns GIT_EMODIFIED if the ref’s stored value does not match current_value at update time
Reflog message may be ignored for refs without a reflog
Caller must free the returned reference with git_reference_free on success
Check return value for 0 on success; GIT_EEXISTS, GIT_EINVALIDSPEC, GIT_EMODIFIED, or other error codes on failure

functions.name: git_reference_symbolic_create
functions.signature: GIT_EXTERN(int) git_reference_symbolic_create(git_reference **out, git_repository *repo, const char *name, const char *target, int force, const char *log_message);
functions.description: Create a symbolic reference pointing to another reference name. Writes to disk and returns the created reference. Validates name and target. Overwrites existing ref if force is non-zero.
requirements: out must be non-NULL
repo must be valid
name must be a valid reference name per documented rules
target must be a valid reference name
If force is zero and name exists, returns GIT_EEXISTS
Reflog message may be ignored for refs without a reflog
Caller must free the returned reference with git_reference_free
Check return value: 0 on success; GIT_EEXISTS, GIT_EINVALIDSPEC or other error codes

functions.name: git_reference_create
functions.signature: GIT_EXTERN(int) git_reference_create(git_reference **out, git_repository *repo, const char *name, const git_oid *id, int force, const char *log_message);
functions.description: Create a direct (OID) reference pointing to the given object id. Writes to disk and returns the created reference. Validates the reference name. Overwrites existing ref if force is non-zero.
requirements: out must be non-NULL
repo must be valid
name must be a valid reference name per documented rules
id must point to a valid git_oid
If force is zero and name exists, returns GIT_EEXISTS
Reflog message may be ignored for refs without a reflog
Caller must free the returned reference with git_reference_free
Check return value: 0 on success; GIT_EEXISTS, GIT_EINVALIDSPEC or error code

functions.name: git_reference_create_matching
functions.signature: GIT_EXTERN(int) git_reference_create_matching(git_reference **out, git_repository *repo, const char *name, const git_oid *id, int force, const git_oid *current_id, const char *log_message);
functions.description: Create or update a direct (OID) reference to id, conditionally ensuring the stored value matches current_id. Writes to disk and returns the created/updated reference. Overwrites if force is non-zero.
requirements: out must be non-NULL
repo must be valid
name must be a valid reference name
id must be a valid git_oid pointer
current_id must be a git_oid pointer specifying the expected current value; if the ref’s current value differs, returns GIT_EMODIFIED
If force is zero and name exists, may return GIT_EEXISTS (per documented errors)
Reflog message may be ignored for refs without a reflog
Caller must free the returned reference with git_reference_free
Check return value: 0 on success; GIT_EMODIFIED, GIT_EEXISTS, GIT_EINVALIDSPEC, or other error codes

functions.name: git_reference_target
functions.description: Return the OID target of a direct reference. Returns NULL for symbolic references.
requirements: ref must be a valid git_reference*
Only valid for direct references; returns NULL otherwise
Returned pointer is owned by the reference; do not free or modify

functions.name: git_reference_target_peel
functions.description: Return the peeled OID of a direct reference that points to a tag object; otherwise may be NULL. This is the OID reached by peeling a tag reference.
requirements: ref must be a valid git_reference*
Applies to direct references pointing to tag objects; returns NULL if not applicable
Returned pointer is owned by the reference; do not free or modify

functions.name: git_reference_symbolic_target
functions.description: Return the referenced name (target) of a symbolic reference. Returns NULL if the reference is not symbolic.
requirements: ref must be a valid git_reference*
Only available for symbolic references; returns NULL otherwise
Returned string is owned by the reference; do not free or modify

functions.name: git_reference_type
functions.description: Return the type of the reference (GIT_REFERENCE_DIRECT or GIT_REFERENCE_SYMBOLIC).
requirements: ref must be a valid git_reference*

functions.name: git_reference_name
functions.description: Return the full name of the reference (e.g., "refs/heads/main").
requirements: ref must be a valid git_reference*
Returned string is owned by the reference; do not free or modify

functions.name: git_reference_resolve
functions.description: Resolve a symbolic reference by following targets until a direct reference is reached and return a new reference object. If a direct reference is provided, returns a copy. Caller must free the returned reference.
requirements: out must be non-NULL
ref must be a valid git_reference*
Caller must free the returned reference with git_reference_free
Check return value: 0 on success; non-zero error code on failure

functions.name: git_reference_owner
functions.description: Return the repository that owns the reference.
requirements: ref must be a valid git_reference*
Returned git_repository* is owned by libgit2; do not free

functions.name: git_reference_symbolic_set_target
functions.description: Overwrite a symbolic reference with a new symbolic target and return the updated reference. The reference must be symbolic. Writes to disk and overwrites the given reference.
requirements: out must be non-NULL
ref must be an existing symbolic git_reference*; call fails if not symbolic
target must be a valid reference name
Reflog message may be ignored for refs without a reflog
Caller must free the returned reference with git_reference_free
Check return value: 0 on success; GIT_EINVALIDSPEC or other error codes

functions.name: git_reference_set_target
functions.description: Overwrite a direct reference with a new OID target and return the updated reference. The reference must be direct. Writes to disk and is conditional, returning GIT_EMODIFIED if the reference changed since it was read.
requirements: out must be non-NULL
ref must be an existing direct (OID) git_reference*; fails if not direct
id must be a valid git_oid pointer for the new target
May return GIT_EMODIFIED if the ref’s value changed since it was read
Caller must free the returned reference with git_reference_free
Check return value: 0 on success; GIT_EMODIFIED or other error codes

functions.name: git_reference_rename
functions.description: Rename a reference (direct or symbolic) to new_name and return the renamed reference. Validates the new name. If force is zero and a reference with new_name exists, the operation fails. Reflog is renamed if it exists; the caller is responsible for writing an appropriate reflog entry if enabled.
requirements: new_ref must be non-NULL
ref must be a valid git_reference*
new_name must be a valid reference name per documented rules
If force is zero and new_name exists, returns GIT_EEXISTS
Caller must free the returned reference with git_reference_free
Check return value: 0 on success; GIT_EINVALIDSPEC, GIT_EEXISTS or other error codes

functions.name: git_reference_delete
functions.description: Delete the given reference from disk. Works for direct and symbolic references. Does not free the in-memory object; caller must still call git_reference_free. Returns GIT_EMODIFIED if the reference has changed since it was looked up.
requirements: ref must be a valid git_reference* previously looked up
Caller must still call git_reference_free to free memory after deletion
Check return value: 0 on success; GIT_EMODIFIED or other error codes

functions.name: git_reference_remove
functions.description: Delete a reference by name in the given repository without consulting its old value.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
name must be a non-NULL C string naming the reference
Check return value: 0 on success; non-zero error code on failure

functions.name: git_reference_list
functions.description: Populate the provided git_strarray with the names of all references in the repository. The caller owns and must free the strings with git_strarray_free when done.
requirements: array must be a non-NULL pointer to a git_strarray to fill
repo must be a valid repository
Caller must free results with git_strarray_free when no longer needed
Check return value: 0 on success; non-zero error code on failure

functions.name: git_reference_foreach
functions.signature:
GIT_EXTERN(int) git_reference_foreach(
	git_repository *repo,
	git_reference_foreach_cb callback,
	void *payload);
functions.description: Iterate all references in the repository and invoke the callback for each, passing a git_reference* and the payload. Returning non-zero from the callback stops iteration. The callback is responsible for calling git_reference_free on each reference it receives.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
callback must be a valid function pointer of type git_reference_foreach_cb
Callback must call git_reference_free on each provided reference
Callback return non-zero terminates iteration; function returns that non-zero value (GIT_EUSER semantics not stated here)
Check return value: 0 on success; non-zero callback return or error code on failure

functions.name: git_reference_foreach_name
functions.signature:
GIT_EXTERN(int) git_reference_foreach_name(
	git_repository *repo,
	git_reference_foreach_name_cb callback,
	void *payload);
functions.description: Iterate all references in the repository and invoke the callback with each reference’s name (const char*), avoiding allocation of git_reference objects. Non-zero callback return stops iteration.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
callback must be a valid function pointer of type git_reference_foreach_name_cb
Check return value: 0 on success; non-zero callback return or error code

functions.name: git_reference_dup
functions.description: Create a duplicate of the given reference object.
requirements: dest must be non-NULL
source must be a valid git_reference*
Caller must free the duplicated reference with git_reference_free
Check return value: 0 on success; non-zero error code on failure

functions.name: git_reference_free
functions.description: Free a git_reference object previously created or returned by libgit2.
requirements: ref may be NULL or a valid git_reference*; if non-NULL it must not be used after free

functions.name: git_reference_cmp
functions.description: Compare two references. Returns 0 if they are the same; otherwise returns a stable but unspecified ordering value.
requirements: ref1 and ref2 must be valid git_reference pointers

functions.name: git_reference_iterator_new
functions.description: Create an iterator over all references in the repository.
requirements: out must be non-NULL to receive the iterator
repo must be a valid repository
Caller must free the iterator with git_reference_iterator_free
Check return value: 0 on success; error code on failure

functions.name: git_reference_iterator_glob_new
functions.signature:
GIT_EXTERN(int) git_reference_iterator_glob_new(
	git_reference_iterator **out,
	git_repository *repo,
	const char *glob);
functions.description: Create an iterator over references whose names match the given glob pattern.
requirements: out must be non-NULL
repo must be valid
glob must be a non-NULL C string pattern (fnmatch-style)
Caller must free the iterator with git_reference_iterator_free
Check return value: 0 on success; error code on failure

functions.name: git_reference_next
functions.description: Advance the iterator and return the next reference object. Returns GIT_ITEROVER when there are no more references. The caller must free each returned reference.
requirements: out must be non-NULL
iter must be a valid git_reference_iterator*
Caller must free each returned reference with git_reference_free
Check return value: 0 on success; GIT_ITEROVER when done; error code on failure

functions.name: git_reference_next_name
functions.description: Advance the iterator and return the next reference name, avoiding allocation of reference objects. Returns GIT_ITEROVER when exhausted.
requirements: out must be non-NULL
iter must be a valid git_reference_iterator*
Returned string lifetime/ownership is not explicitly stated; treat as valid until iterator is advanced or freed (inferred from typical iterator patterns; details unknown)
Check return value: 0 on success; GIT_ITEROVER when done; error code on failure

functions.name: git_reference_iterator_free
functions.description: Free a reference iterator and its associated resources.
requirements: iter may be NULL or a valid iterator pointer; after free it must not be used

functions.name: git_reference_foreach_glob
functions.description: Iterate over reference names that match the glob pattern and invoke the callback for each. Pattern uses fnmatch-style globbing (*, ?, and character ranges). Non-zero callback return terminates iteration.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
glob must be a non-NULL pattern string
callback must be a valid function pointer
Check return value: 0 on success; returns GIT_EUSER on non-zero callback, or other error codes

functions.name: git_reference_has_log
functions.description: Check if a reflog exists for the specified reference name.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
refname must be a non-NULL C string
Return values: 1 if reflog exists; 0 if not; otherwise an error code
Caller must check for negative (error) return values

functions.name: git_reference_ensure_log
functions.description: Ensure that a reflog exists for the specified reference, creating it if necessary so that future updates will append to the log.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
refname must be a non-NULL C string
Check return value: 0 on success; error code on failure

functions.name: git_reference_is_branch
functions.description: Return 1 if the reference lives under refs/heads (local branch); 0 otherwise.
requirements: ref must be a valid git_reference*

functions.name: git_reference_is_remote
functions.description: Return 1 if the reference lives under refs/remotes (remote-tracking branch); 0 otherwise.
requirements: ref must be a valid git_reference*

functions.name: git_reference_is_tag
functions.description: Return 1 if the reference lives under refs/tags (tag); 0 otherwise.
requirements: ref must be a valid git_reference*

functions.name: git_reference_is_note
functions.description: Return 1 if the reference lives under refs/notes (note); 0 otherwise.
requirements: ref must be a valid git_reference*

functions.name: git_reference_normalize_name
functions.description: Normalize a reference name (remove leading '/', collapse duplicate slashes) and validate it according to flags. On success, writes the normalized name into the caller-provided buffer.
requirements: buffer_out must point to a caller-allocated buffer
buffer_size must be large enough to hold the normalized name including NUL; GIT_EBUFS if too small
name must be a non-NULL C string
flags control validation per git_reference_format_t (e.g., ALLOW_ONELEVEL, REFSPEC_PATTERN, REFSPEC_SHORTHAND)
Check return value: 0 on success; GIT_EBUFS, GIT_EINVALIDSPEC, or other error codes

functions.name: git_reference_peel
functions.description: Peel the reference to the first object of the requested type, following tags as needed. If type is GIT_OBJECT_ANY, peel until a non-tag object. The resulting git_object is owned by the repository and must be freed with git_object_free.
requirements: out must be non-NULL
ref must be a valid git_reference*
type must be a valid git_object_t value (COMMIT, TAG, TREE, BLOB, or ANY)
Caller must free the resulting object with git_object_free
Check return value: 0 on success; GIT_EAMBIGUOUS, GIT_ENOTFOUND, or other error codes

functions.name: git_reference_name_is_valid
functions.description: Validate a reference name and report whether it is well-formed according to reference naming rules.
requirements: valid must be a non-NULL pointer to receive 0/1 validity
refname must be a non-NULL C string
Check return value: 0 on success; error code on failure

functions.name: git_reference_shorthand
functions.description: Return a human-readable short name for the reference when applicable; otherwise returns the full name. The returned string is owned by the reference.
requirements: ref must be a valid git_reference*
Returned string must not be freed or modified by the caller

functions.name: git_refspec_parse
functions.signature: int git_refspec_parse(git_refspec **refspec, const char *input, int is_fetch);
functions.description: Parse a refspec string into a git_refspec object. Use to interpret fetch or push refspecs before matching or transforming reference names. Returns 0 on success, -1 on parse failure.
requirements: refspec must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created git_refspec* handle.
input must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated C string containing the refspec.
is_fetch indicates direction: nonzero for a fetch refspec, 0 for a push refspec.
On success, the caller owns the resulting git_refspec* and must free it with git_refspec_free.
Caller must check the return value (0 success, -1 failure) before using *refspec.

functions.name: git_refspec_free
functions.description: Free a git_refspec previously created by git_refspec_parse. Releases any memory associated with the refspec.
requirements: refspec must be a valid git_refspec* returned by git_refspec_parse.
Do not use the refspec after calling this function.
Behavior for a NULL refspec is unknown; pass a valid pointer.

functions.name: git_refspec_src
functions.description: Return the source specifier (left-hand side) of the refspec. The returned pointer is owned by the refspec and remains valid while the refspec is alive.
requirements: refspec must be a non-NULL, valid git_refspec pointer.
Do not free or modify the returned string; it is const and owned by the refspec.
The returned pointer becomes invalid once the refspec is freed.

functions.name: git_refspec_dst
functions.description: Return the destination specifier (right-hand side) of the refspec. The returned pointer is owned by the refspec and remains valid while the refspec is alive.
requirements: refspec must be a non-NULL, valid git_refspec pointer.
Do not free or modify the returned string; it is const and owned by the refspec.
The returned pointer becomes invalid once the refspec is freed.

functions.name: git_refspec_string
functions.description: Return the original refspec string as provided at parse time. The returned pointer is owned by the refspec and remains valid while the refspec is alive.
requirements: refspec must be a non-NULL, valid git_refspec pointer.
Do not free or modify the returned string; it is const and owned by the refspec.
The returned pointer becomes invalid once the refspec is freed.

functions.name: git_refspec_force
functions.description: Return whether the refspec has the force-update flag set. Returns 1 if forced, 0 otherwise.
requirements: refspec must be a non-NULL, valid git_refspec pointer.
Caller should treat any nonzero return as true and zero as false.

functions.name: git_refspec_direction
functions.description: Return the direction of the refspec (fetch or push). The result is one of GIT_DIRECTION_FETCH or GIT_DIRECTION_PUSH.
requirements: spec must be a non-NULL, valid git_refspec pointer.
Caller must handle only the documented enum values GIT_DIRECTION_FETCH and GIT_DIRECTION_PUSH.

functions.name: git_refspec_src_matches_negative
functions.description: Check if the refspec’s source descriptor matches a negative reference pattern (exclusion). Returns 1 on match, 0 otherwise.
requirements: refspec must be a non-NULL, valid git_refspec pointer.
refname must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated reference name string.
Caller must interpret 1 as match, 0 as no match; no other return values are documented.

functions.name: git_refspec_src_matches
functions.description: Check if the refspec’s source descriptor matches a given reference name. Returns 1 on match, 0 otherwise.
requirements: refspec must be a non-NULL, valid git_refspec pointer.
refname must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated reference name string.
Caller must interpret 1 as match, 0 as no match; no other return values are documented.

functions.name: git_refspec_dst_matches
functions.description: Check if the refspec’s destination descriptor matches a given reference name. Returns 1 on match, 0 otherwise.
requirements: refspec must be a non-NULL, valid git_refspec pointer.
refname must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated reference name string.
Caller must interpret 1 as match, 0 as no match; no other return values are documented.

functions.name: git_refspec_transform
functions.signature: int git_refspec_transform(git_buf *out, const git_refspec *spec, const char *name);
functions.description: Transform a source reference name to its target reference following the refspec’s rules (e.g., map remote refs to local or vice versa depending on direction). Writes the result into the provided git_buf. Returns 0 on success, GIT_EBUFS if the buffer is too small, or another error code.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized git_buf suitable for writing the result.
spec must be a non-NULL, valid git_refspec pointer.
name must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated reference name string to transform.
Caller must check the return value and handle nonzero errors, including GIT_EBUFS.
The contents of out are only valid on success; on error, out may be unchanged or partially written.

functions.name: git_refspec_rtransform
functions.signature: int git_refspec_rtransform(git_buf *out, const git_refspec *spec, const char *name);
functions.description: Reverse-transform a target reference name to its source reference according to the refspec’s rules. Writes the result into the provided git_buf. Returns 0 on success, GIT_EBUFS if the buffer is too small, or another error code.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized git_buf suitable for writing the result.
spec must be a non-NULL, valid git_refspec pointer.
name must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated target reference name string to reverse-transform.
Caller must check the return value and handle nonzero errors, including GIT_EBUFS.
The contents of out are only valid on success; on error, out may be unchanged or partially written.

functions.name: git_remote_create
functions.description: Add a persistent remote with the default fetch refspec to the repository’s configuration. Returns the created git_remote via out.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the created remote
repo must be a valid repository
name must be a valid remote name (validity is checked)
url must be a valid remote URL
On success, caller must free the resulting remote with git_remote_free
May return 0, GIT_EINVALIDSPEC, GIT_EEXISTS or another error code

functions.name: git_remote_create_options_init
functions.description: Initialize a git_remote_create_options structure with default values (equivalent to GIT_REMOTE_CREATE_OPTIONS_INIT).
requirements: opts must point to a git_remote_create_options to initialize
version must be GIT_REMOTE_CREATE_OPTIONS_VERSION
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure

functions.name: git_remote_create_with_opts
functions.description: Create a remote with fine-grained control via options; passing NULL for opts creates a detached remote.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the created remote
url must be the remote URL
opts may be NULL to produce a detached remote; otherwise must point to a valid git_remote_create_options
May return 0, GIT_EINVALIDSPEC, GIT_EEXISTS or another error code
On success, caller must free the resulting remote with git_remote_free

functions.name: git_remote_create_with_fetchspec
functions.description: Add a persistent remote with the provided fetch refspec (or the default if NULL) to a repository’s configuration.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the created remote
repo must be a valid repository
name must be a valid remote name (validity is checked)
url must be a valid remote URL
fetch may be NULL to use the default fetch refspec
May return 0, GIT_EINVALIDSPEC if refspec is invalid, GIT_EEXISTS, or another error code
On success, caller must free the resulting remote with git_remote_free

functions.name: git_remote_create_anonymous
functions.signature:
GIT_EXTERN(int) git_remote_create_anonymous(
		git_remote **out,
		git_repository *repo,
		const char *url);
functions.description: Create an in-memory (anonymous) remote associated with a repository for a given URL; does not persist in config.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the new remote
repo must be a valid repository
url must be a valid remote URL
Returns 0 or an error code
On success, caller must free the resulting remote with git_remote_free

functions.name: git_remote_create_detached
functions.description: Create an in-memory detached remote (not associated with a repository and ignoring repo configuration like url.insteadOf).
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the new remote
url must be a valid remote URL
Returns 0 or an error code
On success, caller must free the resulting remote with git_remote_free

functions.name: git_remote_lookup
functions.description: Lookup a configured remote by name in a repository; validates the name and returns a git_remote object.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the remote
repo must be a valid repository
name must be a valid remote name; validity is checked per tag naming rules referenced
Returns 0, GIT_ENOTFOUND, GIT_EINVALIDSPEC or an error code
On success, caller must free the resulting remote with git_remote_free

functions.name: git_remote_dup
functions.description: Create a deep copy of an existing remote (internal strings duplicated); callbacks are not duplicated.
requirements: dest must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the copy
source must be a valid remote
On success, caller must free the copy with git_remote_free
Returns 0 or an error code

functions.name: git_remote_owner
functions.description: Get the repository that owns the remote.
requirements: remote must be a valid remote
Returns a pointer to the repository (no transfer of ownership)

functions.name: git_remote_name
functions.description: Get the remote’s name; for in-memory remotes, returns NULL.
requirements: remote must be a valid remote
Returned pointer is owned by the remote and must not be freed by the caller

functions.name: git_remote_url
functions.description: Get the effective remote URL for fetching; applies url.*.insteadOf rules and ignores any pushurl.
requirements: remote must be a valid remote
Returned pointer is owned by the remote and must not be freed by the caller

functions.name: git_remote_pushurl
functions.description: Get the remote’s URL used for pushing; applies url.*.pushInsteadOf or instance pushurl if set; may be NULL if unset.
requirements: remote must be a valid remote
Returned pointer is owned by the remote and must not be freed by the caller

functions.name: git_remote_set_url
functions.signature: GIT_EXTERN(int) git_remote_set_url(git_repository *repo, const char *remote, const char *url);
functions.description: Set the remote’s fetch URL in the repository configuration (affects single-URL remotes only). In-memory remote instances are not affected.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
remote is the remote’s name
url is the new URL to set
Assumes single-URL remotes; otherwise returns an error
Returns 0 or an error code

functions.name: git_remote_set_pushurl
functions.signature: GIT_EXTERN(int) git_remote_set_pushurl(git_repository *repo, const char *remote, const char *url);
functions.description: Set the remote’s push URL in the repository configuration (single-URL remotes). In-memory remote instances are not affected.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
remote is the remote’s name
url is the new push URL to set
Assumes single-URL remotes; otherwise returns an error
Returns 0 or an error code

functions.name: git_remote_set_instance_url
functions.description: Set the effective URL for this remote instance only; ignores and does not modify configuration.
requirements: remote must be a valid remote
url is the URL to set for this instance
Returns 0 or an error value

functions.name: git_remote_set_instance_pushurl
functions.description: Set the effective push URL for this remote instance only; ignores and does not modify configuration.
requirements: remote must be a valid remote
url is the push URL to set for this instance
Returns 0 or an error value

functions.name: git_remote_add_fetch
functions.signature: GIT_EXTERN(int) git_remote_add_fetch(git_repository *repo, const char *remote, const char *refspec);
functions.description: Add a fetch refspec to the remote’s configuration; does not affect loaded remote instances.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
remote is the name of the remote to change
refspec must be a valid fetch refspec (validated)
Returns 0, GIT_EINVALIDSPEC if refspec is invalid, or an error value

functions.name: git_remote_get_fetch_refspecs
functions.description: Retrieve the list of fetch refspecs for a remote into a git_strarray owned by the caller.
requirements: array must be a valid pointer to receive strings
remote must be a valid remote
The returned git_strarray memory is owned by the caller and must be freed with git_strarray_free
Returns 0 or an error code

functions.name: git_remote_add_push
functions.signature: GIT_EXTERN(int) git_remote_add_push(git_repository *repo, const char *remote, const char *refspec);
functions.description: Add a push refspec to the remote’s configuration; does not affect loaded remote instances.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
remote is the name of the remote to change
refspec must be a valid push refspec (validated)
Returns 0, GIT_EINVALIDSPEC if refspec is invalid, or an error value

functions.name: git_remote_get_push_refspecs
functions.description: Retrieve the list of push refspecs for a remote into a git_strarray owned by the caller.
requirements: array must be a valid pointer to receive strings
remote must be a valid remote
The returned git_strarray memory is owned by the caller and must be freed with git_strarray_free
Returns 0 or an error code

functions.name: git_remote_refspec_count
functions.description: Get the number of refspecs configured on a remote.
requirements: remote must be a valid remote

functions.name: git_remote_get_refspec
functions.description: Get the nth refspec from a remote.
requirements: remote must be a valid remote
n selects which refspec to get (0-based)
Returned pointer is owned by the remote and must not be freed by the caller

functions.name: git_remote_ls
functions.description: Get the list of references (advertised heads) from the remote after connecting. The memory is owned by the remote and is valid until a new connection is initiated.
requirements: remote must have connected its transport to the remote repository (list available once connection is initiated)
out must be a valid pointer to receive the array
size must be a valid pointer to receive the number of entries
Caller should copy data if needed beyond the next connection
Returns 0 on success, or an error code

functions.name: git_remote_connected
functions.description: Check whether the remote’s underlying transport is currently connected to the remote host.
requirements: remote must be a valid remote
Returns 1 if connected, 0 otherwise

functions.name: git_remote_stop
functions.description: Request cancellation of the current network operation. Network code may check and stop the operation.
requirements: remote must be a valid remote
Returns 0 on success, or an error code

functions.name: git_remote_disconnect
functions.description: Close the connection to the remote.
requirements: remote must be a valid remote
Returns 0 on success, or an error code

functions.name: git_remote_free
functions.description: Free the memory associated with a remote; also disconnects if still connected.
requirements: remote may be NULL or a valid remote (signature does not state NULL handling; typical free semantics apply but are not explicitly stated)
After this call, the remote pointer must not be used again

functions.name: git_remote_list
functions.description: Get the list of configured remote names for a repository into a git_strarray owned by the caller.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the names
repo must be a valid repository
The returned git_strarray must be freed by the user (with git_strarray_free)
Returns 0 or an error code

functions.name: git_remote_init_callbacks
functions.description: Initialize a git_remote_callbacks structure with default values (equivalent to GIT_REMOTE_CALLBACKS_INIT).
requirements: opts must point to a git_remote_callbacks to initialize
version must be GIT_REMOTE_CALLBACKS_VERSION
Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure

functions.name: git_fetch_options_init

version must be GIT_FETCH_OPTIONS_VERSION
Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure

functions.name: git_push_options_init

version must be GIT_PUSH_OPTIONS_VERSION
Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure

functions.name: git_remote_connect_options_init

version must be GIT_REMOTE_CONNECT_OPTIONS_VERSION
Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure

functions.name: git_remote_connect

direction must be GIT_DIRECTION_FETCH or GIT_DIRECTION_PUSH
callbacks may be NULL or a valid pointer to callbacks to use for this connection
proxy_opts may be NULL or a valid pointer to proxy settings
custom_headers may be NULL or a valid pointer to extra HTTP headers
Returns 0 or an error code

functions.name: git_remote_connect_ext
functions.signature:
GIT_EXTERN(int) git_remote_connect_ext(
	git_remote *remote,
	git_direction direction,
	const git_remote_connect_options *opts);
functions.description: Open a connection to a remote with an options struct that supplies defaults for connection and callbacks; callers can override with subsequent fetch/push options.
requirements: remote must be a valid remote
direction must be GIT_DIRECTION_FETCH or GIT_DIRECTION_PUSH
opts may be NULL? (Header does not specify; description implies a provided options structure; treat as must point to remote connection options)

functions.name: git_remote_download

refspecs may be NULL or an empty array to use base refspecs
opts may be NULL or a valid pointer to git_fetch_options
Returns 0 or an error code

functions.name: git_remote_upload

requirements: remote must be a valid remote
refspecs may be NULL or an empty array to use base refspecs

functions.name: git_remote_update_tips

callbacks may be NULL or a valid pointer; if NULL and remote was connected, uses previous callbacks
Returns 0 or an error code

functions.name: git_remote_push

requirements: remote must be a valid remote
refspecs may be NULL or empty to use configured refspecs
opts must be a valid pointer to git_push_options (header does not state NULL allowed)
Returns 0 or an error code

functions.name: git_remote_stats

requirements: remote must be a valid remote

functions.name: git_remote_autotag

requirements: repo must be a valid repository
remote is the remote’s name
value is the new auto-tag setting
Returns 0 or an error code

functions.name: git_remote_prune_refs
functions.description: Retrieve the remote’s ref-prune setting.
requirements: remote must be a valid remote

functions.name: git_remote_rename
functions.description: Rename a remote and update its remote-tracking branches and configuration. Non-default refspecs that cannot be renamed are returned via problems.
requirements: problems must be a valid pointer; on successful return it will hold refspecs that could not be renamed and must always be freed by the caller
repo must be a valid repository
name must be the current remote name
new_name must be a valid new remote name (validity is checked)
No loaded instances of the remote with the old name will change their name or list of refspecs
Returns 0, GIT_EINVALIDSPEC, GIT_EEXISTS or an error code

functions.name: git_remote_name_is_valid
functions.description: Validate that a remote name is well-formed.
requirements: valid must be a valid pointer to receive 0/1 validity
remote_name is the name to check
Returns 0 on success or an error code

functions.name: git_remote_delete
functions.description: Delete a persisted remote from a repository; removes all remote-tracking branches and configuration settings for that remote.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
name is the name of the remote to delete
Returns 0 on success, or an error code

functions.name: git_remote_default_branch
functions.description: Retrieve the name of the remote’s default branch (the branch that HEAD points to). Must be called after connecting. May guess similarly to git when not directly supported by the remote.
requirements: remote must be connected before calling
out must be a valid git_buf to receive the reference name
Returns 0, GIT_ENOTFOUND if no references or none point to HEAD’s commit, or an error code

functions.name: git_repository_open
functions.description: Open an existing git repository at the given path or its working directory. Automatically detects bare vs non-bare repositories. Must call git_libgit2_init before use.
requirements: git_libgit2_init must have been called prior to this function
out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the repository handle
path must point to a valid git repository directory or a working directory
Caller must check the return value for 0 (success) or an error code
On success, the returned git_repository* must be freed with git_repository_free

functions.name: git_repository_open_from_worktree
functions.description: Open the working directory of the given worktree as a normal repository.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the repository handle
wt must be a valid git_worktree pointer
Caller must check the return value for 0 (success) or an error code
On success, the returned repository must be freed with git_repository_free

functions.name: git_repository_wrap_odb
functions.description: Create a repository object that wraps an existing object database (ODB) for use with APIs that require a repository. This repo has no paths associated with it.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the repository handle
odb must be a valid, initialized git_odb pointer
Caller must check return value; 0 on success or an error code on failure
On success, free the repository with git_repository_free when done

functions.name: git_repository_discover
functions.signature: int git_repository_discover(git_buf *out, const char *start_path, int across_fs, const char *ceiling_dirs)
functions.description: Search upward from start_path to find a git repository and write its path into out. Honors ceiling_dirs and optionally stops at filesystem boundaries unless across_fs is non-zero.
requirements: out must point to a user-allocated git_buf
start_path must be a valid path to start the search
across_fs controls whether search crosses filesystem device boundaries (non-zero to allow)
ceiling_dirs may be NULL or a GIT_PATH_LIST_SEPARATOR-separated list of absolute, symlink-free paths; search stops upon reaching any of them
git_libgit2_init must have been called prior to use
Caller must check return value: 0 on success; otherwise an error code

functions.name: git_repository_open_ext
functions.signature: int git_repository_open_ext(git_repository **out, const char *path, unsigned int flags, const char *ceiling_dirs)
functions.description: Find and open a repository with extended search and behavior controls. Supports flags to control search behavior and environment-based discovery.
requirements: git_libgit2_init must have been called prior to use
out may be NULL if only the error code is needed; otherwise must be a valid pointer to receive the repository
path may be NULL only if flags includes GIT_REPOSITORY_OPEN_FROM_ENV; otherwise must be a path to open or search from
flags must be a combination of git_repository_open_flag_t values
ceiling_dirs is a GIT_PATH_LIST_SEPARATOR-delimited list of path prefixes where search should stop (ignored if GIT_REPOSITORY_OPEN_FROM_ENV is set)
Caller must check return value: 0 on success; GIT_ENOTFOUND if not found; -1 for other failures
On success, free the repository with git_repository_free

functions.name: git_repository_open_bare
functions.description: Fast open of a bare repository at bare_path, intended for server-side usage.
requirements: git_libgit2_init must have been called prior to use
out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the repository
bare_path must point directly to a bare repository
Caller must check return value; 0 on success or an error code
On success, free the repository with git_repository_free

functions.name: git_repository_free
functions.description: Free a previously allocated repository handle. Objects created from the repository remain valid until individually freed, but accessing their attributes without a backing repository is undefined.
requirements: repo may be NULL (no operation)
Caller must ensure that any objects spawned from repo are managed and freed appropriately after freeing the repository

functions.name: git_repository_init
functions.signature: int git_repository_init(git_repository **out, const char *path, unsigned is_bare)
functions.description: Create a new git repository at path. Creates a bare repository if is_bare is non-zero; otherwise creates a working directory with a .git directory.
requirements: git_libgit2_init must have been called prior to use
out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the repository
path must be a valid path where the repository will be created
Caller must check return value; 0 on success or an error code
On success, free the repository with git_repository_free

functions.name: git_repository_init_options_init
functions.description: Initialize a git_repository_init_options structure to default values, equivalent to GIT_REPOSITORY_INIT_OPTIONS_INIT. Use GIT_REPOSITORY_INIT_OPTIONS_VERSION for version.
requirements: opts must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a git_repository_init_options struct to initialize
version should be set to GIT_REPOSITORY_INIT_OPTIONS_VERSION
Caller must check return value: 0 on success; -1 on failure

functions.name: git_repository_init_ext
functions.description: Create or reinitialize a git repository at repo_path with extended options (flags, modes, workdir, templates, etc.). Auto-detects filesystem case sensitivity and file mode support.
requirements: git_libgit2_init must have been called prior to use
out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the repository
repo_path must be a path to the repository to create or reinitialize
opts must point to a git_repository_init_options structure (initialized with git_repository_init_options_init or equivalent)
Caller must check return value; 0 on success or an error code
On success, free the repository with git_repository_free

functions.name: git_repository_head
functions.description: Retrieve and resolve the reference pointed to by HEAD. Caller owns the returned reference and must free it with git_reference_free.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the reference
repo must be a valid repository
Caller must check return value: 0 on success; GIT_EUNBORNBRANCH if HEAD points to a non-existing branch; GIT_ENOTFOUND if HEAD is missing; other error codes possible
On success, free the returned git_reference with git_reference_free

functions.name: git_repository_head_for_worktree
functions.description: Retrieve the HEAD reference for the specified linked worktree of the repository.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the reference
repo must be a valid repository
name must be the name of the worktree to query
Caller must check return value (0 on success, non-zero error code)
On success, free the returned git_reference with git_reference_free

functions.name: git_repository_head_detached_for_worktree
functions.description: Return whether the named worktree’s HEAD is detached (points directly to a commit).
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
name must be the name of the worktree to query
Caller must check return value: 1 if detached, 0 if not; error code on failure

functions.name: git_repository_head_unborn
functions.description: Check if the current branch is unborn (HEAD refers to a branch name that does not yet exist).
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
Caller must check return value: 1 if unborn, 0 if not; error code on failure

functions.name: git_repository_is_empty
functions.description: Determine if the repository is empty (no references except HEAD, which must point to an unborn default branch).
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
Caller must check return value: 1 if empty, 0 if not; error code if the repository is corrupted

functions.name: git_repository_item_path
functions.signature: int git_repository_item_path(git_buf *out, const git_repository *repo, git_repository_item_t item)
functions.description: Get the filesystem path for a specific repository item (gitdir, workdir, objects, hooks, etc.), honoring gitdir/commondir layout. Returns GIT_ENOTFOUND if the path cannot exist for the item (e.g., workdir in a bare repo).
requirements: out must point to a git_buf to receive the path
repo must be a valid repository pointer
item must be a valid git_repository_item_t value
Caller must check return value: 0 on success; GIT_ENOTFOUND if the path cannot exist; other error codes possible

functions.name: git_repository_path
functions.description: Return the path to the repository’s gitdir (for normal repos) or the repository root (for bare repos).
requirements: repo must be a valid repository pointer
Returned pointer is owned by the repository; do not free it
May return NULL only if unspecified by implementation (not documented as NULL)

functions.name: git_repository_workdir
functions.description: Return the path of the repository’s working directory, or NULL if the repository is bare.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository pointer
Returned pointer is owned by the repository; do not free it
May return NULL if the repository is bare

functions.name: git_repository_commondir
functions.description: Return the path to the repository’s common directory. For bare repos, this is the repo root; for worktrees, the parent repo’s gitdir; otherwise, the gitdir.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository pointer
Returned pointer is owned by the repository; do not free it

functions.name: git_repository_set_workdir
functions.signature: int git_repository_set_workdir(git_repository *repo, const char *workdir, int update_gitlink)
functions.description: Set the working directory path for the repository. If the repo is bare, setting a workdir converts it into a normal repository. Optionally create/update the gitlink and set core.worktree.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
workdir must be a valid path to the desired working directory
update_gitlink non-zero to create/update gitlink and set core.worktree when workdir is not the parent of the .git directory
Caller must check return value for success or error

functions.name: git_repository_is_bare
functions.description: Return whether the repository is bare.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository pointer
Return value is 1 if bare, 0 otherwise

functions.name: git_repository_is_worktree
functions.description: Return whether the repository is a linked worktree.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository pointer
Return value is 1 if linked worktree, 0 otherwise

functions.name: git_repository_config
functions.description: Get the repository’s configuration. If none set explicitly, returns the default config hierarchy (local, global, system). Caller must free the config when done.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the config
repo must be a valid repository
Caller must check return value for success or error
On success, free the returned git_config when no longer needed

functions.name: git_repository_config_snapshot
functions.description: Get an immutable snapshot of the repository’s configuration whose contents do not change even if underlying files do. Caller must free the snapshot.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the config snapshot
repo must be a valid repository
Caller must check return value for success or error
On success, free the returned git_config when no longer needed

functions.name: git_repository_odb
functions.description: Get the repository’s object database (ODB). If no custom ODB is set, returns the default ODB (.git/objects). Caller must free the ODB when done.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the ODB
repo must be a valid repository
Caller must check return value for success or error
On success, free the returned git_odb when no longer needed

functions.name: git_repository_refdb
functions.description: Get the repository’s reference database backend. If none set, returns the default refs database in .git. Caller must free the refdb when done.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the refdb
repo must be a valid repository
Caller must check return value for success or error
On success, free the returned git_refdb when no longer needed

functions.name: git_repository_index
functions.description: Get the repository’s index. If no custom index is set, returns the default index (.git/index). Caller must free the index when done.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the index
repo must be a valid repository
Caller must check return value for success or error
On success, free the returned git_index when no longer needed

functions.name: git_repository_message
functions.description: Read git’s prepared message (e.g., MERGE_MSG) from the repository into out. Used after operations like revert/cherry-pick/merge -n.
requirements: out must point to a git_buf to receive the message contents
repo must be a valid repository
Caller must check return value: 0 on success; GIT_ENOTFOUND if no message exists; other error codes possible
Caller should remove the prepared message file after creating the commit (per note)

functions.name: git_repository_message_remove
functions.description: Remove the prepared message that git_repository_message would retrieve.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
Caller must check return value for success or error

functions.name: git_repository_state_cleanup
functions.description: Remove metadata associated with an in-progress operation (e.g., MERGE_HEAD, MERGE_MSG, etc.).
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
Caller must check return value for success or error

functions.name: git_repository_fetchhead_foreach
functions.description: Iterate over each entry in FETCH_HEAD, invoking the callback. Returning non-zero from the callback terminates iteration.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
callback must be a valid function pointer of type git_repository_fetchhead_foreach_cb
payload is optional and passed to the callback; may be NULL
Caller must check return value: 0 on success; non-zero if the callback returned non-zero; GIT_ENOTFOUND if no FETCH_HEAD file; or another error code

functions.name: git_repository_mergehead_foreach
functions.description: If a merge is in progress, iterate over each OID in MERGE_HEAD and invoke the callback. Returning non-zero from the callback terminates iteration.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
callback must be a valid function pointer of type git_repository_mergehead_foreach_cb
payload is optional and passed to the callback; may be NULL
Caller must check return value: 0 on success; non-zero if the callback returned non-zero; GIT_ENOTFOUND if no MERGE_HEAD file; or another error code

functions.name: git_repository_hashfile
functions.signature: int git_repository_hashfile(git_oid *out, git_repository *repo, const char *path, git_object_t type, const char *as_path)
functions.description: Calculate the object ID of a file’s contents after applying repository filtering rules (e.g., CRLF) as appropriate. For raw hashing without filters, use git_odb_hashfile.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the computed OID
repo must be a valid repository
path must be a valid path to a file on disk (absolute or relative to the workdir)
type must be a valid object type (e.g., GIT_OBJECT_BLOB)
as_path controls which filtering rules apply: empty string disables filters; NULL means use path when inside the workdir
If core.safecrlf is set to fail and filtering would violate it, the function returns an error and no hash is produced
Caller must check return value for success or error

functions.name: git_repository_set_head
functions.description: Point HEAD to the specified reference. Attaches to a branch if refname is a branch (creating an unborn branch if it does not yet exist); detaches to a commit if refname resolves to a commit. Returns -1 if refname points to a tree/blob.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
refname must be the canonical name of a reference
Caller must check return value: 0 on success; -1 if refname is not committish; other error codes possible

functions.name: git_repository_set_head_detached
functions.description: Detach HEAD and make it point directly to the given commit OID. Returns GIT_ENOTFOUND if the object cannot be found, or -1 if the object cannot be peeled to a commit.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
committish must be a valid pointer to the target commit’s OID
Caller must check return value for 0 (success), GIT_ENOTFOUND, -1, or other errors

functions.name: git_repository_set_head_detached_from_annotated
functions.description: Detach HEAD to point to the specified annotated commit, preserving user-specified extended SHA syntax for more precise reflog messages.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
committish must be a valid pointer to an annotated commit
Caller must check return value for success or error

functions.name: git_repository_detach_head
functions.description: Detach HEAD to point directly to the peeled commit. If already detached and pointing to a commit, returns 0; if detached to a tag, updates to peeled commit and returns 0; returns -1 if currently detached to a non-committish.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
Caller must check return value: 0 on success; GIT_EUNBORNBRANCH if HEAD points to a non-existing branch; or other error codes including -1 for non-committish

functions.name: git_repository_state
functions.description: Return the current repository state code indicating whether an operation like merge, rebase, etc., is in progress.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
Return value is one of git_repository_state_t values

functions.name: git_repository_set_namespace
functions.description: Set the active reference namespace for the repository (affects all ref operations). For example, use "foo" to operate under refs/namespaces/foo/.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
nmspace should be the namespace name without the leading "refs/"
Caller must check return value: 0 on success; -1 on error

functions.name: git_repository_get_namespace
functions.description: Get the currently active namespace for the repository, or NULL if none.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
Returned pointer is owned by the repository; do not free it
May return NULL if no namespace is set

functions.name: git_repository_is_shallow
functions.description: Determine whether the repository is a shallow clone.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
Return value is 1 if shallow, 0 if not

functions.name: git_repository_ident
functions.signature: int git_repository_ident(const char **name, const char **email, const git_repository *repo)
functions.description: Retrieve the configured identity (name and email) for reflogs. Pointers are owned by the repository and must not be freed.
requirements: name must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the name pointer
email must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the email pointer
repo must be a valid repository pointer
Caller must check return value for success or error
Returned strings must not be freed by the caller

functions.name: git_repository_set_ident
functions.signature: int git_repository_set_ident(git_repository *repo, const char *name, const char *email)
functions.description: Set the identity (name and email) to use when writing reflogs. Pass NULL to unset and fall back to repository configuration.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
name and/or email may be NULL to unset; otherwise should be valid strings
Caller must check return value for success or error

functions.name: git_repository_oid_type
functions.description: Get the object ID type used by the repository (e.g., SHA1 or SHA256 depending on build/config).
requirements: repo must be a valid repository
Caller should treat the returned value as an enum/identifier for OID type

functions.name: git_repository_commit_parents
functions.description: Populate commits with the parent commits for the next commit, based on repository state. Typically the single HEAD commit, or multiple parents during a merge.
requirements: commits must be a valid pointer to a git_commitarray to receive results
repo must be a valid repository
Caller must check return value for success or error

functions.name: git_reset
functions.signature: int git_reset(git_repository *repo, const git_object *target, git_reset_t reset_type, const git_checkout_options *checkout_opts)
functions.description: Reset the current repository state to a given committish. Depending on reset_type, it will move HEAD (SOFT), additionally reset the index to the commit’s tree (MIXED), or also update the working directory to match the index (HARD). Untracked and ignored files are left untouched on HARD reset. checkout_opts is optional and only used for HARD resets (its checkout_strategy is overridden); it can carry notify/progress callbacks. Use this to move a branch/HEAD and optionally align index and working tree to the specified target. Returns 0 on success, otherwise an error code.
requirements: repo must be a valid, open git_repository for the operation.
target must belong to repo and be a git_commit or a git_tag; if a git_tag is provided, it must be dereferenceable to a git_commit whose OID is used.
reset_type must be one of {GIT_RESET_SOFT, GIT_RESET_MIXED, GIT_RESET_HARD}.
checkout_opts may be NULL; when provided, its checkout_strategy field will be overridden based on reset_type; it may be used to supply notify/progress callbacks for HARD resets.
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success; nonzero indicates an error.
A HARD reset updates the working directory to match the index and will discard changes to tracked files; untracked and ignored files are left alone.

functions.name: git_reset_from_annotated
functions.signature: int git_reset_from_annotated(git_repository *repo, const git_annotated_commit *target, git_reset_t reset_type, const git_checkout_options *checkout_opts)
functions.description: Like git_reset but takes an annotated commit to preserve the user’s original refspec/extended SHA for more precise reflog messages. Moves HEAD and optionally resets the index and working directory as determined by reset_type (SOFT/MIXED/HARD). checkout_opts is optional and used for HARD resets; its checkout_strategy is overridden. Returns 0 on success, otherwise an error code.
requirements: repo must be a valid, open git_repository for the operation.
target must be a git_annotated_commit that belongs to repo; it will be dereferenced to a git_commit whose OID is used as the reset target.
reset_type must be one of {GIT_RESET_SOFT, GIT_RESET_MIXED, GIT_RESET_HARD}.
checkout_opts may be NULL; when provided, its checkout_strategy field will be overridden based on reset_type; it may be used to supply notify/progress callbacks for HARD resets.
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success; nonzero indicates an error.
A HARD reset updates the working directory to match the index and will discard changes to tracked files; untracked and ignored files are left alone.

functions.name: git_reset_default
functions.signature: int git_reset_default(git_repository *repo, const git_object *target, const git_strarray *pathspecs)
functions.description: Update selected index entries from a target commit tree, limited to the paths matched by pathspecs. If target is NULL, remove index entries that match the pathspecs. This only operates on the index (does not describe working tree effects in this interface). Returns 0 on success, otherwise a negative error code.
requirements: repo must be a valid, open git_repository for the operation.
target, when non-NULL, must be a committish (e.g., a git_commit or a tag dereferenceable to a commit) whose tree provides content for the index updates.
If target is NULL, entries in the index matching pathspecs will be removed.
pathspecs must point to a valid git_strarray that lists the pathspecs to operate on.
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success; a value < 0 indicates an error.

functions.name: git_revert_options_init
functions.description: Initialize a git_revert_options structure with default values. Equivalent to creating an instance with GIT_REVERT_OPTIONS_INIT. Use to prepare options before calling revert-related APIs.
requirements: opts must point to a writable git_revert_options structure to be initialized.
version must be GIT_REVERT_OPTIONS_VERSION.
Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure (caller should check the return value).

functions.name: git_revert_commit
functions.signature: int git_revert_commit(git_index **out, git_repository *repo, git_commit *revert_commit, git_commit *our_commit, unsigned int mainline, const git_merge_options *merge_options);
functions.description: Revert the given commit against the specified "our" commit (e.g., HEAD) and produce an index reflecting the result of the revert. Use when you need the in-memory merge result without touching the working directory.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the resulting git_index pointer.
The returned index in *out must be freed by the caller with git_index_free.
repo must be the repository that contains both revert_commit and our_commit.
revert_commit must be the commit whose changes should be inverted.
our_commit must be the commit to revert against (e.g., HEAD).
If revert_commit is a merge commit, mainline specifies which parent to treat as the mainline.
merge_options may be NULL to use default merge options.
Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure (caller should check the return value).

functions.name: git_revert
functions.description: Revert the given commit, applying the inverse changes into the index and working directory of the repository. Use to perform a working-directory-affecting revert akin to `git revert`.
requirements: repo must be the repository to perform the revert in.
commit must be the commit to revert.
given_opts may be NULL to use default revert options.
Operation produces changes in both the index and the working directory.
Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure (caller should check the return value).

functions.name: git_revparse_single
functions.description: Parses a revision specification string and resolves it to a single object within the given repository. On success, writes the resolved object to out; the caller must release it with git_object_free. Use when you expect the spec to identify exactly one object (commit, tree, blob, or tag). Returns 0 on success or an error code such as GIT_ENOTFOUND, GIT_EAMBIGUOUS, or GIT_EINVALIDSPEC when the spec cannot be resolved uniquely.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to a git_object* storage location.
repo must be a valid, initialized git_repository opened for the target repository.
spec must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated C string using git revision syntax (see gitrevisions).
On success, the caller must free *out with git_object_free when no longer needed.
Callers must handle non-zero returns including GIT_ENOTFOUND, GIT_EAMBIGUOUS, and GIT_EINVALIDSPEC.

functions.name: git_revparse_ext
functions.signature: int git_revparse_ext(git_object **object_out, git_reference **reference_out, git_repository *repo, const char *spec);
functions.description: Parses a revision specification string and resolves it to a single object, and when applicable, the intermediate reference that led to that object (e.g., @{<-n>} or <branch>@{upstream}). On success, writes the resolved object to object_out and, if an intermediate reference was involved and reference_out is non-NULL, writes the reference there. The caller must free the object with git_object_free and the reference (if returned) with git_reference_free.
requirements: object_out must be a non-NULL pointer to a git_object* storage location.
reference_out may be NULL; if non-NULL and an intermediate reference is identified, it will be set and must be freed with git_reference_free.
repo must be a valid, initialized git_repository for the search.
spec must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated C string conforming to git revision syntax.
On success, the caller must free *object_out with git_object_free; if reference_out is non-NULL and set, it must be freed with git_reference_free.
Callers must handle non-zero returns including GIT_ENOTFOUND, GIT_EAMBIGUOUS, and GIT_EINVALIDSPEC.

functions.name: git_revparse
functions.description: Parses a revision specification string into a git_revspec structure, filling its from, to, and flags fields. The flags indicate whether the spec refers to a single object, a range, or uses merge-base semantics. Use this to interpret ranges like A..B, A...B, or single-object specs, then inspect revspec->flags and from/to. The caller must free any non-NULL from/to objects in the output with git_object_free.
requirements: revspec must be a non-NULL pointer to a caller-allocated git_revspec struct for output.
repo must be a valid, initialized git_repository.
spec must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated C string using git revision syntax.
On success, any non-NULL revspec->from and revspec->to must be freed by the caller with git_object_free when no longer needed.
Callers must examine the returned int and handle non-zero returns including GIT_EINVALIDSPEC, GIT_ENOTFOUND, and GIT_EAMBIGUOUS.
revspec->flags will be set to a combination of git_revspec_t values indicating SINGLE, RANGE, or MERGE_BASE semantics; callers should branch logic based on these flags.

functions.name: git_revwalk_new
functions.description: Allocate a new revision walker for iterating a repository’s commit graph. The walker maintains internal caches and should be reused when possible. The walker is not thread-safe and must be used from a single thread.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the newly allocated git_revwalk*
repo must be a valid, initialized git_repository* referring to the repository to walk
The resulting git_revwalk is not thread-safe and must only be used from a single thread

functions.name: git_revwalk_reset
functions.description: Reset the revision walker to its initial state, clearing all pushed and hidden commits so a new walk can be prepared. Walkers are also reset automatically when a walk completes.
requirements: walker must be a valid git_revwalk* created by git_revwalk_new

functions.name: git_revwalk_push
functions.description: Mark a commit as a root to start the walk from. The commit may be skipped if it or any of its descendants are hidden. At least one commit must be pushed before starting a walk.
requirements: walk must be a valid git_revwalk*
id must be a valid pointer to a git_oid identifying a committish in the repository being walked
At least one commit must be pushed before calling git_revwalk_next to start iteration

functions.name: git_revwalk_push_glob
functions.description: Push OIDs referenced by refs matching a glob onto the walker. A leading "refs/" is implied if absent; if the pattern contains no '?', '*', or '[', a trailing "/*" is implied. Refs not pointing to a committish are ignored.
requirements: walk must be a valid git_revwalk*
glob must be a valid NUL-terminated glob pattern string
Only references that resolve to a committish will be pushed; non-committish matches are ignored

functions.name: git_revwalk_push_head
functions.description: Push the repository’s HEAD commit onto the walker.
requirements: walk must be a valid git_revwalk*

functions.name: git_revwalk_hide
functions.description: Hide a commit and all its ancestors from the walk output.
requirements: walk must be a valid git_revwalk*
commit_id must be a valid pointer to a git_oid identifying a committish in the repository being walked

functions.name: git_revwalk_hide_glob
functions.description: Hide commits pointed to by refs matching a glob (and their ancestors). A leading "refs/" is implied if absent; if the pattern contains no '?', '*', or '[', a trailing "/*" is implied. Refs not pointing to a committish are ignored.
requirements: walk must be a valid git_revwalk*
glob must be a valid NUL-terminated glob pattern string
Only references that resolve to a committish will be considered; non-committish matches are ignored

functions.name: git_revwalk_hide_head
functions.description: Hide the commit pointed to by HEAD (and its ancestors) from the walk output.
requirements: walk must be a valid git_revwalk*

functions.name: git_revwalk_push_ref
functions.description: Push the OID pointed to by the named reference onto the walker. The reference must point to a committish.
requirements: walk must be a valid git_revwalk*
refname must be a valid NUL-terminated reference name string
The named reference must resolve to a committish

functions.name: git_revwalk_hide_ref
functions.description: Hide the OID pointed to by the named reference (and its ancestors) from the walk output. The reference must point to a committish.
requirements: walk must be a valid git_revwalk*
refname must be a valid NUL-terminated reference name string
The named reference must resolve to a committish

functions.name: git_revwalk_next
functions.description: Retrieve the next commit OID from the current walk. With time sorting, the first call is non-blocking; with topological or reverse modes, the first call may block to preprocess. Returns 0 on success or GIT_ITEROVER when the walk is exhausted. The walker is reset when iteration finishes.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the next commit oid
walk must be a valid git_revwalk*
At least one commit must have been pushed before starting iteration (e.g., via git_revwalk_push or related functions)
Caller must handle the GIT_ITEROVER return code to detect end of iteration

functions.name: git_revwalk_sorting
functions.description: Set the sorting mode for the walk using a combination of GIT_SORT_* flags (topological, time, reverse). Changing the sorting mode resets the walker.
requirements: walk must be a valid git_revwalk*
sort_mode must be a valid combination (bitwise OR) of git_sort_t flags (GIT_SORT_TOPOLOGICAL, GIT_SORT_TIME, GIT_SORT_REVERSE, or 0)
