Changing the sorting mode resets the walker; prepare pushes again after changing

functions.name: git_revwalk_push_range
functions.description: Push and hide the endpoints of a revision range. The range must be of the form "<commit>..<commit>"; the left-hand commit is hidden and the right-hand commit is pushed. Each endpoint must be parseable by git_revparse_single.
requirements: walk must be a valid git_revwalk*
range must be a valid NUL-terminated string of the form "<commit>..<commit>"
Each <commit> must be a spec accepted by git_revparse_single in the repository

functions.name: git_revwalk_simplify_first_parent
functions.description: Simplify history traversal by only enqueuing the first parent of each commit, ignoring all other parents.
requirements: walk must be a valid git_revwalk*

functions.name: git_revwalk_free
functions.description: Free a revision walker created by git_revwalk_new. Passing NULL is a no-op.
requirements: walk may be NULL (no operation) or a valid git_revwalk* previously returned by git_revwalk_new

functions.name: git_revwalk_repository
functions.description: Return the git_repository instance that the walker is operating on.
requirements: walk must be a valid git_revwalk*

functions.name: git_revwalk_add_hide_cb
functions.description: Add, change, or remove a callback used to decide whether to hide a commit (and its parents) during traversal. The callback receives the commit id and the provided payload and should return non-zero to hide the commit and its parents.
requirements: walk must be a valid git_revwalk*
hide_cb must be a function compatible with git_revwalk_hide_cb; it returns non-zero to hide the commit and its parents
payload is an opaque pointer passed through to the callback
Exact semantics for removing a callback (e.g., whether passing NULL removes it) are not specified in this header and are unknown

functions.name: git_signature_new
functions.signature: int git_signature_new(git_signature **out, const char *name, const char *email, git_time_t time, int offset);
functions.description: Create a new action signature for a person at a specific time and timezone offset. Use git_signature_free to free the returned signature. Angle brackets ('<' and '>') are not allowed in name or email.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the allocated git_signature on success
name must be a valid string and must not contain '<' or '>'
email must be a valid string and must not contain '<' or '>'
time is the action time in seconds since the Unix epoch
offset is the timezone offset in minutes for the given time
On successful return (0), the caller must free *out with git_signature_free
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; nonzero is an error code

functions.name: git_signature_now
functions.signature: int git_signature_now(git_signature **out, const char *name, const char *email);
functions.description: Create a new action signature using the current time and local timezone. Use git_signature_free to free the returned signature. Angle brackets ('<' and '>') are not allowed in name or email.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the allocated git_signature on success
name must be a valid string and should represent the person's name
email must be a valid string and should represent the person's email
On successful return (0), the caller must free *out with git_signature_free
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; nonzero is an error code

functions.name: git_signature_default_from_env
functions.description: Create author and/or committer signatures using configuration and environment variables. Honors GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/EMAIL and GIT_COMMITTER_NAME/EMAIL, falling back to user.name and user.email from config if unset. Timestamps honor GIT_AUTHOR_DATE and GIT_COMMITTER_DATE, otherwise current time. If neither date env var is set, both timestamps are the same. Returns GIT_ENOTFOUND if required identity values are missing. Use git_signature_free to free any returned signatures.
requirements: At least one of author_out or committer_out must be non-NULL
repo must be a valid git_repository pointer
On success, any non-NULL output pointer that is set must be freed with git_signature_free by the caller
Function may return GIT_ENOTFOUND if user.name or user.email are not set and there is no environment fallback; caller must handle nonzero error codes
Environment variables considered (if set): GIT_AUTHOR_NAME, GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL, GIT_AUTHOR_DATE, GIT_COMMITTER_NAME, GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL, GIT_COMMITTER_DATE

functions.name: git_signature_default
functions.description: Create a new signature using user.name and user.email from repository configuration and the current time. Does not consider environment variables. Returns GIT_ENOTFOUND if required configuration is missing. Use git_signature_free to free the returned signature.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the allocated git_signature on success
repo must be a valid git_repository pointer
On successful return (0), the caller must free *out with git_signature_free
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; GIT_ENOTFOUND if user.name or user.email are missing, otherwise another error code

functions.name: git_signature_from_buffer
functions.description: Parse a signature from a textual buffer of the form "Real Name <email> timestamp tzoffset" where timestamp is seconds since the Unix epoch and tzoffset is in hhmm format (no colon). Returns GIT_EINVALID if the buffer cannot be parsed. Use git_signature_free to free the returned signature.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the allocated git_signature on success
buf must point to a NUL-terminated string in the exact format: "Real Name <email> timestamp tzoffset"
timestamp component must be a valid integer number of seconds since the Unix epoch
tzoffset must be a valid timezone offset in hhmm format (no colon)
On successful return (0), the caller must free *out with git_signature_free
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; GIT_EINVALID if unparsable; otherwise another error code

functions.name: git_signature_dup
functions.description: Create a deep copy of an existing signature, duplicating all internal strings. Use git_signature_free to free the copy.
requirements: dest must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the duplicated git_signature on success
sig must be a valid pointer to an existing git_signature
On successful return (0), the caller must free *dest with git_signature_free
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; nonzero is an error code

functions.name: git_signature_free
functions.description: Free a git_signature previously allocated by libgit2 (e.g., via creation or duplication). The structure is not opaque; it is legal to free it manually, but this function releases the signature and its internal strings.
requirements: sig must be a valid pointer to a git_signature previously allocated/returned by libgit2 or constructed compatibly
Do not use the signature after it has been freed

functions.name: git_stash_save
functions.signature: int git_stash_save(git_oid *out, git_repository *repo, const git_signature *stasher, const char *message, uint32_t flags);
functions.description: Create a new stash from the repository’s current uncommitted changes. On success, writes the OID of the created commit to out and updates refs/stash to point to it. Typical use: provide the repository, a signature for the stasher, an optional message, and a bitmask of GIT_STASH_* flags to control behavior (e.g., keep index, include untracked/ignored). Returns 0 on success, GIT_ENOTFOUND if there is nothing to stash, otherwise an error code.
requirements: repo must refer to a valid, opened git_repository.
out must point to writable storage for a git_oid to receive the stash commit id.
stasher must be a valid git_signature identifying the stasher.
message may be NULL (it is optional).
flags must be a combination of git_stash_flags (GIT_STASH_*).
Caller must handle return values: 0 on success; GIT_ENOTFOUND when there is nothing to stash; otherwise an error code.

functions.name: git_stash_save_options_init
functions.description: Initialize a git_stash_save_options struct with default values. Equivalent to assigning GIT_STASH_SAVE_OPTIONS_INIT. Pass GIT_STASH_SAVE_OPTIONS_VERSION for version.
requirements: opts must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to git_stash_save_options to be initialized.
version must be GIT_STASH_SAVE_OPTIONS_VERSION.
Caller must check the return value: 0 on success; -1 on failure.

functions.name: git_stash_save_with_opts
functions.description: Create a new stash using an options struct to control stashing behavior (flags, stasher, optional message, and optional path filters). On success, writes the OID of the created commit to out and updates refs/stash. Returns 0 on success, GIT_ENOTFOUND if there is nothing to stash, or an error code.
requirements: repo must refer to a valid, opened git_repository.
out must point to writable storage for a git_oid to receive the stash commit id.
opts must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a properly initialized git_stash_save_options.
Within opts: flags are from git_stash_flags; stasher is the identity performing the stash; message is optional; paths (if provided) control which files are stashed.
Caller must handle return values: 0 on success; GIT_ENOTFOUND when there is nothing to stash; otherwise an error code.

functions.name: git_stash_apply_options_init
functions.description: Initialize a git_stash_apply_options struct with default values. Equivalent to assigning GIT_STASH_APPLY_OPTIONS_INIT. Pass GIT_STASH_APPLY_OPTIONS_VERSION for version.
requirements: opts must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to git_stash_apply_options to be initialized.
version must be GIT_STASH_APPLY_OPTIONS_VERSION.
Caller must check the return value: 0 on success; -1 on failure.

functions.name: git_stash_apply
functions.signature: int git_stash_apply(git_repository *repo, size_t index, const git_stash_apply_options *options);
functions.description: Apply a single stashed state from the stash list to the working directory (and optionally reinstate the index). If conflicts with local changes exist, returns GIT_EMERGECONFLICT and leaves the index and working directory unmodified (with noted exceptions for untracked/ignored restoration). Options may be NULL; when provided, they control reinstate-index behavior, checkout options, and progress callbacks.
requirements: repo must refer to a valid, opened git_repository.
index selects the stash to apply; 0 is the most recent. If index does not reference an existing stash, the function returns GIT_ENOTFOUND.
options may be NULL. If non-NULL, it should be a properly initialized git_stash_apply_options.
If GIT_STASH_APPLY_REINSTATE_INDEX is used and conflicts would occur, the function returns GIT_EMERGECONFLICT and both working directory and index remain unmodified.
Caller must handle return values: 0 on success; GIT_ENOTFOUND if no stash at index; GIT_EMERGECONFLICT if conflicts with working directory; otherwise an error code.

functions.name: git_stash_foreach
functions.description: Iterate over all stashed states in a repository, invoking the callback once per entry starting from the most recent. Iteration stops if the callback returns a non-zero value. The callback receives the index, message, and stash commit id, plus the user payload.
requirements: repo must refer to a valid, opened git_repository.
callback must be a valid function pointer; it will be called for each stash entry.
payload is passed through to the callback and may be NULL.
The callback must return 0 to continue iterating; any non-zero return stops iteration.
Caller must handle return values: 0 on success; a non-zero callback return value; or an error code.

functions.name: git_stash_drop
functions.description: Remove a single stashed state from the stash list by index. 0 refers to the most recent stash.
requirements: repo must refer to a valid, opened git_repository.
index must reference an existing stash entry; otherwise the function returns GIT_ENOTFOUND.
Caller must handle return values: 0 on success; GIT_ENOTFOUND if no stash at index; otherwise an error code.

functions.name: git_stash_pop
functions.signature: int git_stash_pop(git_repository *repo, size_t index, const git_stash_apply_options *options);
functions.description: Apply the specified stashed state and, if application succeeds, remove it from the stash list. Options may be NULL; when provided, they control apply behavior (see git_stash_apply). Returns 0 on success, GIT_ENOTFOUND if there’s no stash at the index, or an error code.
requirements: repo must refer to a valid, opened git_repository.
index selects the stash to pop; 0 is the most recent. If index does not reference an existing stash, returns GIT_ENOTFOUND.
options may be NULL. If non-NULL, it should be a properly initialized git_stash_apply_options.
Caller must handle return values: 0 on success; GIT_ENOTFOUND if no stash at index; otherwise an error code. See git_stash_apply for apply semantics and potential conflicts.

functions.name: git_status_options_init
functions.description: Initialize a git_status_options structure with default values. Use this before passing options to status APIs. Pass GIT_STATUS_OPTIONS_VERSION as version. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
requirements: opts must be a valid, writable pointer to a git_status_options structure.
version must be GIT_STATUS_OPTIONS_VERSION.
Callers should check the return value (0 on success; -1 indicates failure).

functions.name: git_status_foreach
functions.description: Iterate the repository’s status and invoke callback for each path that matches the default behavior (equivalent to defaults of the extended API). The callback receives (path, status_flags, payload). If the callback returns non-zero, iteration stops and that value is returned.
requirements: repo must be a valid, opened git_repository.
callback must be a valid function pointer conforming to int (*)(const char *path, unsigned int status_flags, void *payload).
The callback must return 0 on success; any non-zero return stops iteration and is propagated as the function’s return value.
payload is passed through to the callback and may be NULL.
Callers must check the return value: 0 on success, non-zero if callback stopped early, or negative error code.

functions.name: git_status_foreach_ext
functions.signature: int git_status_foreach_ext(git_repository *repo, const git_status_options *opts, git_status_cb callback, void *payload);
functions.description: Extended status iteration that provides fine-grained control via git_status_options (show, flags, pathspec, baseline, rename options). Invokes callback for each selected path. If the callback returns non-zero, iteration stops and that value is returned. Note: rename detection accuracy may be reduced if a pathspec filter is provided.
requirements: repo must be a valid, opened git_repository.
opts must point to an initialized git_status_options (typically via git_status_options_init); contents determine filtering, ordering, and rename detection.
callback must be a valid function pointer conforming to int (*)(const char *path, unsigned int status_flags, void *payload).
The callback must return 0 on success; any non-zero return stops iteration and is propagated as the function’s return value.
payload is passed through to the callback and may be NULL.
If opts->pathspec is used with rename detection enabled, results may be inexact; for accurate rename detection, call without a pathspec.
Callers must check the return value: 0 on success, non-zero if callback stopped early, or negative error code.

functions.name: git_status_file
functions.signature: int git_status_file(unsigned int *status_flags, git_repository *repo, const char *path);
functions.description: Query the status of a single file relative to index/HEAD and populate status_flags with a bitwise OR of git_status_t values. No rename detection is performed. Returns 0 on success, GIT_ENOTFOUND if the path does not exist in HEAD, index, or workdir; GIT_EAMBIGUOUS if the path matches multiple files (e.g., directory or case-insensitive collisions); -1 on other errors.
requirements: status_flags must be a valid, writable pointer to receive the result.
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository.
path must be a non-NULL C string, an exact path relative to the repository working directory.
Path must refer to a single file; if it refers to a directory or ambiguously matches multiple entries, the function returns GIT_EAMBIGUOUS.
Callers must handle return codes: 0 on success; GIT_ENOTFOUND if not present; GIT_EAMBIGUOUS on ambiguous match; -1 on other errors.

functions.name: git_status_list_new
functions.description: Compute repository status and produce a git_status_list with detailed entries (including optional rename detection). The resulting list must be freed with git_status_list_free. If a pathspec filter is supplied, rename detection results may be inaccurate.
requirements: out must be a valid, writable pointer to receive the created git_status_list* on success.
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository.
opts should point to an initialized git_status_options (e.g., via git_status_options_init). Whether NULL is allowed is unknown (not stated).
Callers must check the return value (0 on success; negative error code on failure).
If accurate rename detection is required, call without a pathspec in opts.

functions.name: git_status_list_entrycount
functions.description: Return the number of entries in the given status list. Returns 0 if there are no changes according to the options used when the list was created.
requirements: statuslist must be a valid git_status_list returned by git_status_list_new and not yet freed.

functions.name: git_status_byindex
functions.description: Return a const pointer to the status entry at the given index within the status list. The entry is immutable and must not be freed by the caller. Returns NULL if idx is out of bounds.
requirements: statuslist must be a valid git_status_list returned by git_status_list_new and not yet freed.
idx must be less than git_status_list_entrycount(statuslist) to obtain a non-NULL result.
Returned pointer must not be modified or freed.

functions.name: git_status_list_free
functions.description: Free a git_status_list created by git_status_list_new.
requirements: statuslist must be a git_status_list previously returned by git_status_list_new and not freed already. Whether NULL is accepted is unknown (not stated).
After this call, statuslist and any pointers obtained via git_status_byindex become invalid.

functions.name: git_status_should_ignore
functions.description: Check whether ignore rules would apply to the given path (relative to the repository workdir), independent of whether the path is tracked. Sets *ignored to 1 if the path would be ignored, 0 otherwise. Returns 0 on success, or a negative error code if rules could not be processed.
requirements: ignored must be a valid, writable pointer to an int to receive the boolean result (0 or 1).
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository.
path must be a non-NULL C string for a path rooted at the repository’s workdir.
Callers must check the return value: 0 on success; negative error code on failure.

functions.name: git_submodule_update_options_init
functions.description: Initialize a git_submodule_update_options struct with default values. Use when preparing to call submodule update/clone helpers. Pass the struct version constant. Returns 0 on success or -1 on failure.
requirements: opts must be a valid, writable pointer to a git_submodule_update_options struct.
version should be GIT_SUBMODULE_UPDATE_OPTIONS_VERSION.
On error, check git_error_last for details.

functions.name: git_submodule_update
functions.description: Update a submodule: clone it if missing and checkout the submodule to the commit specified by the superproject’s index. If the target commit is missing locally and allowed, a fetch is performed per options. If init is non-zero and the submodule is uninitialized, it will be initialized first.
requirements: submodule must refer to a valid submodule obtained via lookup/add setup and not yet freed.
If init is zero and the submodule is uninitialized, the call will error; set init non-zero to force initialization.
options may be NULL to use GIT_SUBMODULE_UPDATE_OPTIONS_INIT defaults; otherwise it must be initialized (e.g., via git_submodule_update_options_init).
The function may return any non-zero value from user callbacks inside options; negative values indicate errors. Use git_error_last for details.

functions.name: git_submodule_lookup
functions.description: Lookup a submodule by name or path within a repository and return a git_submodule descriptor. The submodule must be tracked in HEAD, index, or config. Returns GIT_EEXISTS if a repository exists only in the working directory (untracked), GIT_ENOTFOUND if no submodule exists at the path/name.
requirements: repo must be a valid git_repository.
name must be a valid C string naming the submodule or its path (trailing slashes permitted).
out may be NULL to only get the return code; otherwise it receives a new git_submodule which must be freed with git_submodule_free.
On success, caller must call git_submodule_free on the returned submodule.
Distinguish GIT_EEXISTS vs GIT_ENOTFOUND to handle WD-only repos vs absent submodules.

functions.name: git_submodule_dup
functions.description: Create an in-memory duplicate of a git_submodule descriptor. The caller owns the duplicate and must free it.
requirements: source must be a valid git_submodule that has not been freed.
out must be a valid pointer to receive the duplicate; it will be set on success.
The returned duplicate must be released with git_submodule_free.

functions.name: git_submodule_free
functions.description: Release a git_submodule instance and its resources.
requirements: submodule must be a git_submodule previously obtained (e.g., via lookup/dup/add_setup) and not already freed.

functions.name: git_submodule_foreach
functions.description: Iterate over all tracked submodules in a repository, invoking the callback for each. The callback may stop iteration by returning non-zero. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error, or the non-zero callback return value.
requirements: repo must be a valid git_repository.
callback must be a valid function pointer of type git_submodule_cb; return non-zero from the callback to terminate iteration.
payload is opaque and passed through to the callback.

functions.name: git_submodule_add_setup
functions.signature: int git_submodule_add_setup(git_submodule **out, git_repository *repo, const char *url, const char *path, int use_gitlink);
functions.description: Prepare a new submodule entry similar to `git submodule add` up to (but not including) fetch/checkout. Writes an entry to .gitmodules and creates an empty initialized submodule repository either directly in the workdir or in .git/modules with a gitlink, depending on use_gitlink. The returned submodule must be cloned (e.g., via git_submodule_clone) and finalized (git_submodule_add_finalize) to complete the add.
requirements: repo must be a valid superproject repository.
url must be a valid submodule remote URL string.
path must be a valid relative path for the submodule within the superproject.
use_gitlink controls whether a gitlink points to .git/modules (non-zero) vs a repo directly in the workdir (zero).
out must be non-NULL to receive the created submodule; the caller must free it with git_submodule_free when done.
Returns GIT_EEXISTS if the submodule already exists; negative on other errors.

functions.name: git_submodule_clone
functions.description: Perform the clone step for a newly created submodule prepared via add setup. Optionally returns an opened repository for the submodule. Clone behavior is controlled by the provided update options (including fetch/checkout settings).
requirements: submodule must be a submodule currently waiting for its clone (created by git_submodule_add_setup).
opts must point to a valid, initialized git_submodule_update_options struct (const).
out may be NULL; if non-NULL, it will receive a newly opened git_repository that the caller must free with git_repository_free.
Returns 0 on success; -1 on error (see git_clone semantics for details).

functions.name: git_submodule_add_finalize
functions.description: Finalize a submodule add by adding .gitmodules and the cloned submodule to the index, preparing for commit. Does not perform the commit.
requirements: submodule must correspond to a submodule that has been set up and cloned.
Caller should handle return code <0 as error.

functions.name: git_submodule_add_to_index
functions.description: Add the current submodule HEAD commit to the superproject’s index. Optionally writes the index immediately if write_index is non-zero; otherwise, the caller must write the index explicitly.
requirements: submodule must be valid and opened/loaded.
If write_index is zero, the caller must obtain the index and call git_index_write() to persist the change.
Returns 0 on success; negative on failure.

functions.name: git_submodule_owner
functions.description: Return the containing repository for the submodule. This is a borrowed pointer to the repo originally used to create/lookup the submodule and may dangle if that repository has been freed.
requirements: submodule must be valid.
Do not use the returned pointer if the original repository has been freed.

functions.name: git_submodule_name
functions.description: Get the submodule’s name string.
requirements: submodule must be valid.
Returned pointer is owned by the submodule object; valid while the submodule is alive.

functions.name: git_submodule_path
functions.description: Get the submodule’s path within the superproject. Path may differ from the submodule’s name.
requirements: submodule must be valid.
Returned pointer is owned by the submodule; valid while the submodule is alive.

functions.name: git_submodule_url
functions.description: Get the configured URL for the submodule.
requirements: submodule must be valid.
Returned pointer is owned by the submodule; valid while the submodule is alive.

functions.name: git_submodule_resolve_url
functions.description: Resolve a (possibly relative) submodule URL to an absolute URL in the context of the given repository and store it in the provided buffer.
requirements: out must be a valid git_buf to receive the resolved URL (must be writable/initializable per libgit2 buffer usage).
repo must be a valid git_repository.
url must be a valid C string (may be relative).
Returns 0 on success; negative on error.

functions.name: git_submodule_branch
functions.description: Get the configured branch name tracking specification for the submodule.
requirements: submodule must be valid.
Returned pointer is owned by the submodule; valid while the submodule is alive.

functions.name: git_submodule_set_branch
functions.signature: int git_submodule_set_branch(git_repository *repo, const char *name, const char *branch);
functions.description: Set the submodule’s branch in the superproject’s configuration. You may call git_submodule_sync afterwards to propagate changes into the checked-out submodule repository.
requirements: repo must be a valid git_repository.
name must be the submodule’s name string in configuration context.
branch must be a valid branch string to set.
Returns 0 on success; negative on failure.

functions.name: git_submodule_set_url
functions.signature: int git_submodule_set_url(git_repository *repo, const char *name, const char *url);
functions.description: Set the submodule’s URL in the superproject’s configuration. You may call git_submodule_sync afterwards to update the checked-out submodule repo.
requirements: repo must be a valid git_repository.
name must be the submodule’s name string in configuration context.
url must be a valid URL string.
Returns 0 on success; negative on failure.

functions.name: git_submodule_index_id
functions.description: Get the OID of the submodule recorded in the superproject’s index. Returns NULL if the submodule is not in the index.
requirements: submodule must be valid.
Caller must handle a NULL return (submodule not in index).
Returned pointer is to internal data valid while the submodule is alive.

functions.name: git_submodule_head_id
functions.description: Get the OID of the submodule as recorded in the current HEAD tree of the superproject. Returns NULL if not present in HEAD.
requirements: submodule must be valid.
Caller must handle a NULL return (not in HEAD).
Returned pointer is to internal data valid while the submodule is alive.

functions.name: git_submodule_wd_id
functions.description: Get the OID corresponding to the submodule’s checked-out HEAD in its working directory. Does not consider pending index changes inside the submodule. Returns NULL if the submodule is not checked out.
requirements: submodule must be valid.
Caller must handle a NULL return (submodule not checked out).
For a fuller picture of working directory state, use git_submodule_status.

functions.name: git_submodule_ignore
functions.description: Get the ignore rule (git_submodule_ignore_t) that controls how git_submodule_status inspects the submodule workdir (NONE, UNTRACKED, DIRTY, ALL).
requirements: submodule must be valid.

functions.name: git_submodule_set_ignore
functions.signature: int git_submodule_set_ignore(git_repository *repo, const char *name, git_submodule_ignore_t ignore);
functions.description: Set the submodule’s ignore rule in the superproject’s configuration. Does not affect already-loaded instances.
requirements: repo must be a valid git_repository.
name must be the submodule’s configuration name.
ignore must be a valid git_submodule_ignore_t value.
Returns 0 on success; negative on error.

functions.name: git_submodule_update_strategy
functions.description: Get the configured update strategy (git_submodule_update_t) used by `git submodule update` for this submodule.
requirements: submodule must be valid.

functions.name: git_submodule_set_update
functions.signature: int git_submodule_set_update(git_repository *repo, const char *name, git_submodule_update_t update);
functions.description: Set the submodule’s update strategy in the superproject’s configuration. Does not affect existing instances.
requirements: repo must be a valid git_repository.
name must be the submodule’s configuration name.
update must be a valid git_submodule_update_t value.
Returns 0 on success; negative on error.

functions.name: git_submodule_fetch_recurse_submodules
functions.description: Read the submodule.<name>.fetchRecurseSubmodules setting for the submodule. Note: at this time libgit2 does not honor this setting during fetch.
requirements: submodule must be valid.

functions.name: git_submodule_set_fetch_recurse_submodules
functions.description: Set the fetchRecurseSubmodules rule for a submodule in the superproject’s configuration. Returns the old value (per documentation) via the function return.
requirements: repo must be a valid git_repository.
name must be the submodule’s configuration name.
fetch_recurse_submodules must be a valid git_submodule_recurse_t value.
Returns old value for the setting; negative on error.

functions.name: git_submodule_init
functions.description: Copy submodule information from .gitmodules into .git/config (like `git submodule init`). You can modify the in-memory submodule object before calling to affect what is written. Existing entries are not overwritten unless overwrite is non-zero.
requirements: submodule must be valid.
If overwrite is zero, existing config entries are preserved; set non-zero to force update.
Returns 0 on success; negative on failure.

functions.name: git_submodule_repo_init
functions.signature: int git_submodule_repo_init(git_repository **out, const git_submodule *sm, int use_gitlink);
functions.description: Initialize and set up a submodule repository on disk in preparation for clone. Optionally places the repo in .git/modules with a gitlink depending on use_gitlink. Returns the created repository via out.
requirements: sm must be a valid submodule descriptor.
out must be a valid pointer to receive the created git_repository; the caller owns it and must free it with git_repository_free.
use_gitlink controls whether the workdir contains a gitlink to .git/modules (non-zero) versus a repo directly in workdir (zero).
Returns 0 on success; negative on failure.

functions.name: git_submodule_sync
functions.description: Copy submodule remote URL information from the superproject into the checked-out submodule’s config (like `git submodule sync`). Useful after changing the submodule’s URL.
requirements: submodule must be valid and refer to a checked-out submodule to update its config.
Returns 0 on success; negative on error.

functions.name: git_submodule_open
functions.description: Open and return a new git_repository object for the submodule. Only works if the submodule is checked out in the working directory. Caller must free the returned repository.
requirements: submodule must be valid and the submodule must be checked out in the workdir.
repo must be a valid pointer to receive the opened repository; on success, free with git_repository_free.
Multiple calls return distinct repository objects.

functions.name: git_submodule_reload
functions.description: Reread and refresh cached submodule information from config, index, and HEAD. If force is non-zero, force reload even if not out-of-date.
requirements: submodule must be valid.
Returns 0 on success; negative on error.

functions.name: git_submodule_status
functions.signature: int git_submodule_status(unsigned int *status, git_repository *repo, const char *name, git_submodule_ignore_t ignore);
functions.description: Compute and return the status flags for a submodule (combination of GIT_SUBMODULE_STATUS_*). The depth of examination depends on the provided ignore rule.
requirements: status must be a valid pointer to receive the bitmask result.
repo must be a valid git_repository.
name must be the submodule’s name string.
ignore must be a valid git_submodule_ignore_t value controlling workdir inspection.
Returns 0 on success; negative on error.

functions.name: git_submodule_location
functions.description: Return a mask of the first four status bits (IN_HEAD, IN_INDEX, IN_CONFIG, IN_WD) indicating which locations contain information for the submodule. Lightweight alternative to full status.
requirements: location_status must be a valid pointer to receive the bitmask.
submodule must be valid.
Returns 0 on success; negative on error.

functions.name: git_tag_lookup
functions.description: Lookup a tag object by its OID in the given repository and return it via out. Returns 0 on success or an error code. Use when you have a tag’s oid and need the git_tag object.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the result
repo must be a valid, initialized repository
id must point to a valid OID in repo
On success, the returned tag must later be freed with git_tag_free
Function returns 0 on success; non-zero indicates an error

functions.name: git_tag_lookup_prefix
functions.signature: int git_tag_lookup_prefix(git_tag **out, git_repository *repo, const git_oid *id, size_t len);
functions.description: Lookup a tag object by a short OID prefix. Returns the tag whose id matches the given prefix length. Returns 0 on success or an error code.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the result
repo must be a valid, initialized repository
id must point to a valid OID buffer; len specifies the number of prefix bytes
len must be the desired prefix length of the identifier
On success, the returned tag must later be freed with git_tag_free
Function returns 0 on success; non-zero indicates an error

functions.name: git_tag_free
functions.description: Release a tag object and its resources. After this call, the tag pointer must not be used.
requirements: tag may be NULL; if non-NULL it must be a tag previously obtained from libgit2 (e.g., via lookup/creation/dup)
After calling, the tag pointer must not be used again (dangling)
Call exactly once per acquired tag to avoid leaks or double-free

functions.name: git_tag_id
functions.description: Return the OID of the given tag object.
requirements: tag must be a valid, previously loaded tag
Return value is a pointer valid as long as tag remains alive; do not free it

functions.name: git_tag_owner
functions.description: Return the repository that contains the given tag.
requirements: tag must be a valid, previously loaded tag
Returned repository pointer is owned elsewhere; do not free via this function

functions.name: git_tag_target
functions.description: Lookup and return the object that this tag references via target_out. Returns 0 on success or an error code. Useful to resolve an annotated tag to the tagged object.
requirements: target_out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the git_object
tag must be a valid, previously loaded tag
Function returns 0 on success; non-zero indicates an error
Ownership/closing requirements for the returned git_object are not stated here; consult higher-level docs. If unsure, treat similarly to other libgit2 lookups and close with git_object_free when done

functions.name: git_tag_target_id
functions.description: Return the OID of the object that this tag points to.
requirements: tag must be a valid, previously loaded tag
Return value is a pointer valid as long as tag remains alive; do not free it

functions.name: git_tag_target_type
functions.description: Return the object type of the tagged target (e.g., commit, tree, blob).
requirements: tag must be a valid, previously loaded tag

functions.name: git_tag_name
functions.description: Return the tag’s name string.
requirements: tag must be a valid, previously loaded tag
Returned string is owned by the tag and/or repository; do not free it; valid while tag remains alive

functions.name: git_tag_tagger
functions.description: Return the tagger (author) signature for the tag, or NULL if unspecified.
requirements: tag must be a valid, previously loaded tag
Returned signature pointer is owned by the tag and valid while tag remains alive; do not free it

functions.name: git_tag_message
functions.description: Return the tag’s message, or NULL if the tag has no message.
requirements: tag must be a valid, previously loaded tag
Returned string is owned by the tag and valid while tag remains alive; do not free it

functions.name: git_tag_create
functions.signature: int git_tag_create(git_oid *oid, git_repository *repo, const char *tag_name, const git_object *target, const git_signature *tagger, const char *message, int force);
functions.description: Create a new annotated tag object in the repository and create a refs/tags/<name> reference to it. If a tag with the given name exists and force is non-zero, it will be replaced. On success, writes the new tag’s OID to oid. If the tag name already exists and not forced, returns GIT_EEXISTS and sets oid to the existing tag’s OID. The message is not prettified.
requirements: oid must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the created or existing tag OID
repo must be a valid, initialized repository

tag_name must be a valid tag name; must not contain '~', '^', ':', '\\', '?', '[', or '*', and must not contain the sequences ".." or "@{"; must not conflict with an existing tag name unless force is non-zero
target must be a git_object that belongs to repo
tagger must point to a valid signature for the tagger
message must point to the full tag message (may be empty if desired)
force controls replacement of existing references (non-zero to overwrite)
Function returns 0 on success; returns GIT_EEXISTS when tag already exists without force; may return GIT_EINVALIDSPEC or other error codes

functions.name: git_tag_annotation_create
functions.signature: int git_tag_annotation_create(git_oid *oid, git_repository *repo, const char *tag_name, const git_object *target, const git_signature *tagger, const char *message);
functions.description: Create a new annotated tag object in the object database that points to target, without creating a reference. On success, writes the new tag’s OID to oid. The message is not prettified.
requirements: oid must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the created tag OID
repo must be a valid, initialized repository
tag_name must be the desired tag’s name (no reference is created by this function)
target must be a git_object that belongs to repo
tagger must point to a valid signature for the tagger
message must point to the full tag message
Function returns 0 on success or an error code

functions.name: git_tag_create_from_buffer
functions.signature: int git_tag_create_from_buffer(git_oid *oid, git_repository *repo, const char *buffer, int force);
functions.description: Create a new tag from raw tag data provided in buffer, storing it in the repository; if a tag already exists and force is non-zero, it will be replaced. On success, writes the tag’s OID to oid.
requirements: oid must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the OID
repo must be a valid, initialized repository
buffer must point to valid raw tag data
force controls overwriting existing tags (non-zero to overwrite)
Function returns 0 on success; non-zero indicates an error

functions.name: git_tag_create_lightweight
functions.signature: int git_tag_create_lightweight(git_oid *oid, git_repository *repo, const char *tag_name, const git_object *target, int force);
functions.description: Create a new lightweight tag (a direct reference) pointing at target. Does not create an annotated tag object. On success, writes the target object’s OID to oid. If the tag exists and not forced, returns GIT_EEXISTS and sets oid to the existing pointed object’s OID.
requirements: oid must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the OID
repo must be a valid, initialized repository
tag_name must be a valid tag name (same validity rules as git_tag_create)
target must be a git_object that belongs to repo
force controls replacement of existing references (non-zero to overwrite)
Function returns 0 on success; may return GIT_EEXISTS, GIT_EINVALIDSPEC, or other error codes

functions.name: git_tag_delete
functions.description: Delete an existing tag reference with the given name from the repository. Validates the tag name.
requirements: repo must be a valid, initialized repository
tag_name must be a valid tag name as per git_tag_create rules
Function returns 0 on success; may return GIT_EINVALIDSPEC or other error codes

functions.name: git_tag_list
functions.description: Populate tag_names with all tag names in the repository. The caller owns the resulting strings and must free them with git_strarray_free.
requirements: tag_names must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a git_strarray to receive results
repo must be a valid, initialized repository
Caller must free contents of tag_names using git_strarray_free when no longer needed
Function returns 0 on success or an error code

functions.name: git_tag_list_match
functions.description: Populate tag_names with tag names in the repository that match pattern (fnmatch-style). If pattern is empty, all tags are returned. The caller owns the strings and must free them with git_strarray_free.
requirements: tag_names must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a git_strarray to receive results
pattern must be a valid C string (may be empty to match all) using standard fnmatch syntax
repo must be a valid, initialized repository
Caller must free contents of tag_names using git_strarray_free when no longer needed
Function returns 0 on success or an error code

functions.name: git_tag_foreach
functions.description: Iterate over all tags in the repository, invoking callback for each tag name and OID. Iteration stops when the callback returns non-zero or when all tags are visited.
requirements: repo must be a valid, initialized repository
callback must be a valid, non-NULL function pointer of type git_tag_foreach_cb
payload may be NULL and is passed through to the callback
Callback should return 0 to continue; non-zero to stop iteration
Function returns 0 on success or an error code

functions.name: git_tag_peel
functions.description: Recursively peel a tag until a non-tag object is found and return that object via tag_target_out. The returned object is owned by the repository and must be closed with git_object_free. Returns 0 on success or an error code.
requirements: tag_target_out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the peeled object
tag must be a valid, previously loaded tag
Caller must close the returned object with git_object_free when done
Function returns 0 on success; non-zero indicates an error

functions.name: git_tag_dup
functions.description: Create an in-memory duplicate of source and store it in out. Returns 0. The copy must be freed with git_tag_free to avoid leaks.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the duplicate
source must be a valid, previously loaded tag
Caller must free the duplicated tag with git_tag_free
Function returns 0 on success (per comment)

functions.name: git_tag_name_is_valid
functions.description: Check whether a tag name is valid, considering both reference name rules (as if under refs/tags/) and additional tag restrictions (e.g., cannot start with '-'). Sets *valid to non-zero if valid. Returns 0 on success or an error code.
requirements: valid must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the result
name must be a non-NULL C string with the tag name to test
Function returns 0 on success or an error code

functions.name: git_transaction_new
functions.description: Create a new transaction object for performing transactional reference updates in the given repository. This only initializes the transaction; it does not lock any references. Typical usage: create a transaction, lock one or more refs, stage updates, commit, then free the transaction.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to a git_transaction* variable to receive the created transaction.
repo must be a valid, initialized git_repository pointer whose references will be operated on.
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success; any non-zero value is an error code.
The created transaction does not hold any locks until you explicitly lock references with git_transaction_lock_ref.

functions.name: git_transaction_lock_ref
functions.description: Lock the specified reference within the transaction. This is the first step before updating or removing a reference in a transaction.
requirements: tx must be a valid transaction created by git_transaction_new.
refname must name an existing reference to lock (format and existence according to repository’s reference naming rules).
Call this before calling any set/remove functions for this reference.
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success; non-zero indicates an error.

functions.name: git_transaction_set_target
functions.signature: int git_transaction_set_target(git_transaction *tx, const char *refname, const git_oid *target, const git_signature *sig, const char *msg);
functions.description: Queue an update to set the target OID of a (direct) reference within the transaction. The reference must have been locked previously in this transaction. The provided signature and message will be used for the reflog entry (if applicable).
requirements: tx must be a valid transaction created by git_transaction_new.
refname must be the name of a reference that has already been locked with git_transaction_lock_ref in this transaction; otherwise this may return GIT_ENOTFOUND.
target must point to a valid git_oid designating the new object ID for the reference.
sig may be NULL to read the identity from the repository configuration; if non-NULL, it must point to a valid git_signature.
msg is a message string for the reflog; behavior for NULL is not explicitly documented.
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success; GIT_ENOTFOUND if the reference is not among the locked ones; other non-zero values indicate errors.
This function only queues the update; changes are applied when git_transaction_commit is called.

functions.name: git_transaction_set_symbolic_target
functions.signature: int git_transaction_set_symbolic_target(git_transaction *tx, const char *refname, const char *target, const git_signature *sig, const char *msg);
functions.description: Queue an update to set the target of a symbolic reference within the transaction. The reference must have been locked previously. The signature and message will be used for the reflog entry (if applicable).
requirements: tx must be a valid transaction created by git_transaction_new.
refname must be the name of a reference that has already been locked with git_transaction_lock_ref; otherwise this may return GIT_ENOTFOUND.
target must be a valid reference name string designating the symbolic target.
sig may be NULL to read the identity from the repository configuration; if non-NULL, it must point to a valid git_signature.
msg is a message string for the reflog; behavior for NULL is not explicitly documented.
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success; GIT_ENOTFOUND if the reference is not among the locked ones; other non-zero values indicate errors.
This function only queues the update; changes are applied when git_transaction_commit is called.

functions.name: git_transaction_set_reflog
functions.description: Queue an update to set the specified reference’s reflog content in the transaction. If combined with setting the reference target in the same transaction, that target update will not be written to the reflog.
requirements: tx must be a valid transaction created by git_transaction_new.
refname must be the name of a reference that has already been locked with git_transaction_lock_ref; otherwise this may return GIT_ENOTFOUND.
reflog must point to a valid git_reflog describing the entries to be written.
If used together with a target update in the same transaction, expect that the target update will not produce a reflog entry (per documentation).
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success; GIT_ENOTFOUND if the reference is not among the locked ones; other non-zero values indicate errors.
This function only queues the update; changes are applied when git_transaction_commit is called.

functions.name: git_transaction_remove
functions.description: Queue the removal of the specified reference within the transaction. The reference must be locked in this transaction before removal.
requirements: tx must be a valid transaction created by git_transaction_new.
refname must be the name of a reference that has already been locked with git_transaction_lock_ref; otherwise this may return GIT_ENOTFOUND.
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success; GIT_ENOTFOUND if the reference is not among the locked ones; other non-zero values indicate errors.
This function only queues the removal; changes are applied when git_transaction_commit is called.

functions.name: git_transaction_commit
functions.description: Apply all queued changes in the transaction. Updates are processed one by one; processing stops at the first failure and returns an error code.
requirements: tx must be a valid transaction created by git_transaction_new.
Only call after queuing desired operations (locks and set/remove calls).
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success; any non-zero value indicates an error, and processing stops at the first failure.

functions.name: git_transaction_free
functions.description: Free resources associated with the transaction. If any references are still locked, they will be unlocked and no changes will be made to them.
requirements: tx may be NULL or a valid transaction pointer; freeing a valid transaction releases all associated resources.
If called before commit, any queued changes will not be applied.
After calling this function, tx must not be used again.

functions.name: git_tree_lookup
functions.description: Lookup a tree object in the given repository by its oid. On success, writes a pointer to the loaded git_tree into out.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the result
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository
id must point to a valid tree oid present in repo
Returns 0 on success; non-zero libgit2 error code otherwise
The returned git_tree must be released with git_tree_free when no longer needed

functions.name: git_tree_lookup_prefix
functions.signature: int git_tree_lookup_prefix(git_tree **out, git_repository *repo, const git_oid *id, size_t len);
functions.description: Lookup a tree object by an abbreviated (prefix) oid. Behaves like git_object_lookup_prefix for trees.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the result
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository
id must point to an oid containing at least len bytes of the tree’s id prefix
len is the length in bytes of the short identifier to match
Returns 0 on success; non-zero libgit2 error code otherwise
The returned git_tree must be released with git_tree_free when no longer needed

functions.name: git_tree_free
functions.description: Release an open git_tree and its resources. After this call, the pointer must not be used.
requirements: tree must be a tree obtained from libgit2 (e.g., via lookup/dup) and not used after free
Do not use the tree pointer after calling this function

functions.name: git_tree_id
functions.description: Return the object id (oid) of the given tree.
requirements: tree must point to a previously loaded git_tree
Returned pointer is owned by the tree; do not free it; it becomes invalid when the tree is freed

functions.name: git_tree_owner
functions.description: Return the repository that owns/contains the given tree.
requirements: tree must point to a previously loaded git_tree
Returned repository pointer is owned elsewhere; do not free via this call

functions.name: git_tree_entrycount
functions.description: Return the number of entries in the given tree.
requirements: tree must point to a previously loaded git_tree

functions.name: git_tree_entry_byname
functions.signature: const git_tree_entry * git_tree_entry_byname(const git_tree *tree, const char *filename);
functions.description: Return the tree entry with the given filename within the tree, or NULL if not found. The entry is owned by the tree.
requirements: tree must be a previously loaded git_tree
filename must be a NUL-terminated string naming an entry in this tree (no path separators)
Returned pointer is owned by the tree; do not free; becomes invalid when the tree is freed

functions.name: git_tree_entry_byindex
functions.signature: const git_tree_entry * git_tree_entry_byindex(const git_tree *tree, size_t idx);
functions.description: Return the tree entry at the given index, or NULL if idx is out of range. The entry is owned by the tree.
requirements: tree must be a previously loaded git_tree
idx must be less than git_tree_entrycount(tree) to get a non-NULL result
Returned pointer is owned by the tree; do not free; becomes invalid when the tree is freed

functions.name: git_tree_entry_byid
functions.signature: const git_tree_entry * git_tree_entry_byid(const git_tree *tree, const git_oid *id);
functions.description: Return the tree entry with the given object id within the tree, or NULL if not found. This search is linear and not fast. The entry is owned by the tree.
requirements: tree must be a previously loaded git_tree
id must point to the oid to search for
Returned pointer is owned by the tree; do not free; becomes invalid when the tree is freed

functions.name: git_tree_entry_bypath
functions.signature: int git_tree_entry_bypath(git_tree_entry **out, const git_tree *root, const char *path);
functions.description: Retrieve a tree entry contained in the tree or its subtrees by a relative path. The returned entry is user-owned and must be freed with git_tree_entry_free.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the entry
root must be a previously loaded git_tree representing the path root
path must be a NUL-terminated relative path to an entry
On success returns 0; returns GIT_ENOTFOUND if the path does not exist; other non-zero values indicate errors
Caller must free the resulting entry with git_tree_entry_free

functions.name: git_tree_entry_dup
functions.description: Duplicate a tree entry. The copy is owned by the caller and must be freed with git_tree_entry_free.
requirements: dest must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the duplicate
source must be a valid git_tree_entry
Returns 0 on success; non-zero libgit2 error code otherwise
Caller must free the duplicated entry using git_tree_entry_free

functions.name: git_tree_entry_free
functions.description: Free a user-owned tree entry (such as one returned by git_tree_entry_dup or git_tree_entry_bypath).
requirements: entry must be a user-owned entry (not one owned by a git_tree or git_treebuilder)
Do not call on entries owned by a tree/builder; those are freed with their owner

functions.name: git_tree_entry_name
functions.description: Return the filename of the tree entry.
requirements: entry must be a valid git_tree_entry
Returned string is owned by the entry; do not free; becomes invalid when the entry is freed or its owner is freed

functions.name: git_tree_entry_id
functions.description: Return the oid of the object that the entry points to.
requirements: entry must be a valid git_tree_entry
Returned pointer is owned by the entry; do not free

functions.name: git_tree_entry_type
functions.description: Return the object type of the entry target (e.g., blob or tree).
requirements: entry must be a valid git_tree_entry

functions.name: git_tree_entry_filemode
functions.description: Return the normalized UNIX file mode of the tree entry.
requirements: entry must be a valid git_tree_entry

functions.name: git_tree_entry_filemode_raw
functions.description: Return the raw (unnormalized) UNIX file mode of the tree entry, useful for recreating the original tree object.
requirements: entry must be a valid git_tree_entry

functions.name: git_tree_entry_cmp
functions.description: Compare two tree entries for ordering. Returns <0 if e1 is before e2, 0 if equal, >0 if after.
requirements: e1 and e2 must be valid git_tree_entry pointers

functions.name: git_tree_entry_to_object
functions.description: Convert a tree entry to the git_object it references (e.g., a blob or subtree). Caller must free the resulting object with git_object_free.
requirements: object_out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the object
repo must be the repository where the pointed-to object can be looked up
entry must be a valid git_tree_entry
Returns 0 on success; non-zero libgit2 error code otherwise
Caller must free the resulting object with git_object_free

functions.name: git_treebuilder_new
functions.description: Create a new tree builder to construct or modify trees in memory. If source is non-NULL, the builder is initialized with that tree’s entries.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the builder
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository in which to store the resulting tree object(s)
source may be NULL or a valid git_tree
Returns 0 on success; non-zero libgit2 error code otherwise
Caller must free the builder with git_treebuilder_free

functions.name: git_treebuilder_clear
functions.description: Remove all entries from the tree builder.
requirements: bld must be a valid git_treebuilder
Returns 0 on success; non-zero error code otherwise

functions.name: git_treebuilder_entrycount
functions.description: Return the number of entries currently in the tree builder.
requirements: bld must be a valid git_treebuilder

functions.name: git_treebuilder_free
functions.description: Free a tree builder and its internal entries.
requirements: bld must be a git_treebuilder previously created (e.g., by git_treebuilder_new)
Do not use the builder after freeing it

functions.name: git_treebuilder_get
functions.description: Return a pointer to the builder-owned entry with the given filename, or NULL if not found. The entry is owned by the builder.
requirements: bld must be a valid git_treebuilder
filename must be a NUL-terminated name (not a path) of an entry in the builder
Returned pointer is owned by the builder; do not free

functions.name: git_treebuilder_insert
functions.signature: int git_treebuilder_insert(const git_tree_entry **out, git_treebuilder *bld, const char *filename, const git_oid *id, git_filemode_t filemode);
functions.description: Add a new entry or update an existing one in the builder with the given filename, target id, and filemode. Optionally returns a pointer to the created/updated entry.
requirements: If out is non-NULL, it will receive a pointer to the entry owned by the builder; do not free it and note it may not remain valid past the next builder operation
bld must be a valid git_treebuilder
filename must be a NUL-terminated entry name
id must point to the target object’s oid
By default, the target id must exist in the object database and be of the correct type unless the GIT_OPT_ENABLE_STRICT_OBJECT_CREATION option is set to false
Returns 0 on success; non-zero libgit2 error code otherwise

functions.name: git_treebuilder_remove
functions.description: Remove the entry with the given filename from the builder.
requirements: bld must be a valid git_treebuilder
filename must be a NUL-terminated entry name to remove
Returns 0 on success; non-zero libgit2 error code otherwise

functions.name: git_treebuilder_filter
functions.description: Call filter for each entry in the builder and remove entries for which the callback returns non-zero.
requirements: bld must be a valid git_treebuilder
filter must be a valid callback function; it will be passed each entry and the payload
payload is an opaque pointer passed through to the callback
Returns 0 on success, a non-zero callback return value if a callback indicates removal, or an error code on failure

functions.name: git_treebuilder_write
functions.description: Write the builder’s current entries as a tree object to the associated repository and return its oid in id.
requirements: id must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the new tree’s oid
bld must be a valid git_treebuilder created for a specific repository
Returns 0 on success; non-zero libgit2 error code otherwise

functions.name: git_tree_walk
functions.signature: int git_tree_walk(const git_tree *tree, git_treewalk_mode mode, git_treewalk_cb callback, void *payload);
functions.description: Traverse entries in a tree (and its subtrees) in pre- or post-order. Invokes callback per entry with the current relative root and entry.
requirements: tree must be a valid git_tree
mode must be GIT_TREEWALK_PRE or GIT_TREEWALK_POST
callback must be a valid function; it may return >0 to skip an entry (in pre-order) or <0 to stop the walk
payload is opaque and passed to each callback invocation
Returns 0 on success; non-zero libgit2 error code otherwise

functions.name: git_tree_dup
functions.description: Create an in-memory duplicate of a tree. The caller owns the copy and must free it with git_tree_free.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the duplicate
source must be a valid git_tree
Returns 0

functions.name: git_tree_create_updated
functions.signature: int git_tree_create_updated(git_oid *out, git_repository *repo, git_tree *baseline, size_t nupdates, const git_tree_update *updates);
functions.description: Create a new tree by applying a list of updates to a baseline tree. Optimized for common file/directory additions, removals, and replacements.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the new tree’s oid
repo must be the same repository that contains baseline
baseline must be a valid git_tree to base the changes on
updates must point to an array of nupdates git_tree_update items
Deleting and adding the same entry is undefined behavior
Changing a tree to a blob or a blob to a tree is not supported
Returns 0 on success; non-zero libgit2 error code otherwise

functions.name: git_worktree_list
functions.description: Lists the names of all linked worktrees for the given repository and writes them into the provided git_strarray. The caller must release the result with git_strarray_free. Returns 0 on success or a libgit2 error code on failure.
requirements: out must point to a valid, writable git_strarray structure.
The returned array must be freed with git_strarray_free by the caller.
repo must reference an opened git_repository.
Returns 0 on success; nonzero return values are error codes that must be handled by the caller.

functions.name: git_worktree_lookup
functions.description: Looks up a worktree by name within the given repository and returns a git_worktree handle via out. Returns 0 on success or an error code on failure.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the git_worktree* result.
repo must reference the repository that contains worktrees.
name must be a valid, non-NULL C string naming the worktree.
On success, the returned git_worktree must be released with git_worktree_free by the caller.
Returns 0 on success; nonzero return values are error codes that must be handled by the caller.

functions.name: git_worktree_open_from_repository
functions.description: Opens a git_worktree handle for the specified repository if that repository is a linked worktree (not the main worktree). It locates the worktree in the parent repository and creates a git_worktree object. Returns 0 on success or an error code on failure.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the git_worktree* result.
repo must reference an opened git_repository; if it is a linked worktree, the function will find its worktree in the parent repository.
On success, the returned git_worktree must be released with git_worktree_free by the caller.
Returns 0 on success; nonzero return values are error codes that must be handled by the caller.

functions.name: git_worktree_free
functions.description: Frees a previously allocated git_worktree handle. Safe to call with NULL (a no-op).
requirements: wt may be NULL; calling with NULL has no effect.
After calling, any pointers obtained from this worktree (e.g., name, path) become invalid.

functions.name: git_worktree_validate
functions.description: Checks whether a worktree is valid, i.e., both the metadata in the parent repository and the linked working copy are present. Returns 0 when valid; otherwise returns an error code.
requirements: wt must point to a git_worktree to be checked.
A return value of 0 indicates validity; negative/nonzero values indicate an error that must be handled.

functions.name: git_worktree_add_options_init
functions.description: Initializes a git_worktree_add_options struct with default values. Equivalent to assigning GIT_WORKTREE_ADD_OPTIONS_INIT. Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure.
requirements: opts must be a valid pointer to a git_worktree_add_options to initialize.
version should be GIT_WORKTREE_ADD_OPTIONS_VERSION.
The caller may pass NULL for fields documented as optional later when using the options.

functions.name: git_worktree_add
functions.signature: int git_worktree_add(git_worktree **out, git_repository *repo, const char *name, const char *path, const git_worktree_add_options *opts);
functions.description: Creates a new linked worktree for repo, sets up the necessary repository data structures, and checks out the current HEAD into the directory at path. Returns a git_worktree handle via out. Options may modify default behavior (e.g., locking, checkout behavior, HEAD ref); opts may be NULL to accept defaults.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the resulting git_worktree*.
repo must reference an opened git_repository.
name must be a valid, non-NULL C string naming the worktree.
path must be a valid, non-NULL filesystem path where the worktree will be created.
opts may be NULL; if provided, it must point to an initialized git_worktree_add_options (e.g., via GIT_WORKTREE_ADD_OPTIONS_INIT or git_worktree_add_options_init).
On success, the returned git_worktree must be freed with git_worktree_free by the caller.
Returns 0 on success; nonzero return values are error codes that must be handled by the caller.

functions.name: git_worktree_lock
functions.description: Locks a worktree if it is not already locked, optionally recording a human-readable reason string. Returns 0 on success or a nonzero error code on failure.
requirements: wt must point to a valid git_worktree to lock.
reason may be NULL or a valid C string describing the reason.
Returns 0 on success; nonzero return values are error codes that must be handled by the caller.

functions.name: git_worktree_unlock
functions.description: Unlocks a previously locked worktree. Returns 0 on success, 1 if the worktree was not locked, or an error code on failure.
requirements: wt must point to a valid git_worktree to unlock.
Caller must handle the special return code 1 indicating the worktree was not locked.
Nonzero values other than 1 indicate an error that must be handled.

functions.name: git_worktree_is_locked
functions.description: Checks whether a worktree is locked. If reason is non-NULL and the worktree is locked, the function writes the lock reason into the provided git_buf. Returns >0 if locked, 0 if not locked, or <0 on error.
requirements: wt must point to a git_worktree to check.
reason may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must point to an initialized git_buf suitable for receiving text.
Return values: >0 if locked, 0 if not locked, <0 indicates an error; the caller must branch on these cases appropriately.

functions.name: git_worktree_name
functions.description: Returns the name of the worktree. The returned pointer remains valid for the lifetime of the git_worktree object.
requirements: wt must point to a valid git_worktree.
The returned pointer becomes invalid once the git_worktree is freed; do not free the returned string.

functions.name: git_worktree_path
functions.description: Returns the filesystem path of the worktree. The returned pointer remains valid for the lifetime of the git_worktree object.
requirements: wt must point to a valid git_worktree.
The returned pointer becomes invalid once the git_worktree is freed; do not free the returned string.

functions.name: git_worktree_prune_options_init
functions.description: Initializes a git_worktree_prune_options struct with default values. Equivalent to assigning GIT_WORKTREE_PRUNE_OPTIONS_INIT. Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure.
requirements: opts must be a valid pointer to a git_worktree_prune_options to initialize.
version should be GIT_WORKTREE_PRUNE_OPTIONS_VERSION.

functions.name: git_worktree_is_prunable
functions.description: Determines if a worktree can be pruned under the given options. Returns 1 if prunable, 0 if not, or an error code on failure. If not prunable, an error message is set (visible via giterr_last) indicating why (e.g., valid or locked unless overridden by flags).
requirements: wt must point to a git_worktree to check.
opts must point to a git_worktree_prune_options; this parameter is required (not documented as optional).
Return values: 1 if prunable, 0 if not prunable, or a negative/nonzero error code; the caller must handle each case appropriately.

functions.name: git_worktree_prune
functions.description: Prunes a worktree by removing on-disk git data structures. The operation proceeds only if git_worktree_is_prunable would succeed. Options control which checks are overridden; opts may be NULL. Returns 0 on success or an error code on failure.
requirements: wt must point to a git_worktree to prune.
opts may be NULL; if provided, it must point to an initialized git_worktree_prune_options (e.g., via GIT_WORKTREE_PRUNE_OPTIONS_INIT or git_worktree_prune_options_init).
The worktree will only be pruned if the prunability checks pass (as per git_worktree_is_prunable).
Returns 0 on success; nonzero return values are error codes that must be handled by the caller.

functions.name: git_stdalloc_init_allocator
functions.description: Initializes a git_allocator instance to use libgit2’s standard allocator (“stdalloc”) functions for malloc, realloc, and free. Typical usage is to declare a git_allocator, pass its address to this function, then provide it to libgit2 APIs that accept a custom allocator. Returns 0 on success or a libgit2 error code on failure. Details about specific failure cases are not documented.
requirements: allocator must point to a valid, writable git_allocator structure (inferred from parameter description)
caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; nonzero indicates a libgit2 error code (explicitly stated as “An error code or 0”)
the initialized allocator can be used with git_allocator_setup as indicated by the documentation

functions.name: git_commit_create_from_ids
functions.signature: int git_commit_create_from_ids(git_oid *id, git_repository *repo, const char *update_ref, const git_signature *author, const git_signature *committer, const char *message_encoding, const char *message, const git_oid *tree, size_t parent_count, const git_oid *parents[])
functions.description: Create a new commit object in the given repository using raw object IDs for the tree and parents. This is a low-level, dangerous API: the provided tree and parent IDs are not validated. On success, the commit is written to the object database and (optionally) the given reference (e.g., "HEAD") is updated to point to the new commit. Typical usage is when the caller already has computed/known OIDs and wants to avoid object lookups.
requirements: id must be a non-NULL pointer to storage where the resulting commit OID will be written.
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository where the commit will be created.

update_ref may be NULL; if non-NULL and the reference exists, the first parent must be the tip of that reference; if the reference does not exist, it will be created; use "HEAD" to update the current branch’s HEAD.
author must be a valid pointer to a git_signature containing author identity and time.
committer must be a valid pointer to a git_signature containing committer identity and time.
message_encoding may be NULL; if NULL, no encoding header is written and UTF-8 is assumed; if non-NULL, it must be a standard encoding name (e.g., "UTF-8").
message should be a NUL-terminated string containing the full commit message (not explicitly documented as allowing NULL).
tree must point to a git_oid identifying the commit’s tree; no validity checks are performed, so the caller is responsible for ensuring it refers to a valid tree object (dangerous API).
parent_count is the number of parents for this commit.
parents must be an array of length parent_count of pointers to git_oid values for each parent; may be NULL if parent_count is 0 (root commit).
Return value: 0 on success; non-zero error code on failure. Callers must check the return value and handle errors.

functions.name: git_commit_create_from_callback
functions.signature: int git_commit_create_from_callback(git_oid *id, git_repository *repo, const char *update_ref, const git_signature *author, const git_signature *committer, const char *message_encoding, const char *message, const git_oid *tree, git_commit_parent_callback parent_cb, void *parent_payload)
functions.description: Create a new commit object in the given repository using a callback to supply parent OIDs and a raw tree OID. The tree OID is not validated. The parent callback is invoked with the index of the next parent to provide and should return a pointer to a git_oid for that parent, or NULL when there are no more parents. On success, writes the commit to the object database and optionally updates the given reference (e.g., "HEAD").
requirements: id must be a non-NULL pointer to storage where the resulting commit OID will be written.
repo must be a valid, opened git_repository where the commit will be created.

update_ref may be NULL; if non-NULL and the reference exists, the first parent must be the tip of that reference; if the reference does not exist, it will be created; use "HEAD" to update the current branch’s HEAD.
author must be a valid pointer to a git_signature containing author identity and time.
committer must be a valid pointer to a git_signature containing committer identity and time.
message_encoding may be NULL; if NULL, no encoding header is written and UTF-8 is assumed; if non-NULL, it must be a standard encoding name (e.g., "UTF-8").
message should be a NUL-terminated string containing the full commit message (not explicitly documented as allowing NULL).
tree must point to a git_oid identifying the commit’s tree; no validity checks are performed, so the caller is responsible for ensuring it refers to a valid tree object (dangerous API).

parent_cb must be a valid function pointer that, when invoked with successive parent indices starting at 0, returns a pointer to the git_oid of the next parent, or NULL when there are no further parents.
parent_payload is an opaque pointer passed through to parent_cb and may be NULL.
Return value: 0 on success; non-zero error code on failure. Callers must check the return value and handle errors.

functions.name: git_commit_graph_open_options_init
functions.description: Initialize a git_commit_graph_open_options struct to its default values. Call this before passing options to APIs that accept git_commit_graph_open_options. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
requirements: opts must be a valid, writable pointer (non-NULL).
version must be GIT_COMMIT_GRAPH_OPEN_OPTIONS_VERSION.
Caller must check the return value and not use uninitialized options on failure.

functions.name: git_commit_graph_open
functions.description: Open and validate a commit-graph from the given Git objects directory. On success, stores a git_commit_graph pointer in cgraph_out. Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure.
requirements: cgraph_out must be a valid pointer to receive the result (non-NULL).
objects_dir must point to a valid Git objects directory path (non-NULL, existing).
Caller must check the return value before using *cgraph_out.
On failure, the output parameter must not be used.

functions.name: git_commit_graph_free
functions.description: Free a git_commit_graph previously opened with git_commit_graph_open when ownership was not transferred to the ODB. Safe to call with NULL (no action).
requirements: Only call for commit-graph instances allocated by git_commit_graph_open that were not associated with the ODB via a successful git_odb_set_commit_graph.
cgraph may be NULL (no effect).
Do not use cgraph after freeing.

functions.name: git_commit_graph_writer_options_init
functions.description: Initialize a git_commit_graph_writer_options struct to default values (equivalent to GIT_COMMIT_GRAPH_WRITER_OPTIONS_INIT). Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure.
requirements: opts must be a valid, writable pointer (non-NULL).
version must be GIT_COMMIT_GRAPH_WRITER_OPTIONS_VERSION.
Caller must check the return value and avoid using uninitialized options on failure.

functions.name: git_commit_graph_writer_new
functions.description: Create a new writer for commit-graph files that will write into the specified objects/info directory, configured by options. Returns 0 on success or an error code.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the writer (non-NULL).
objects_info_dir must be the path to a repository's objects/info directory (non-NULL, existing).
options must point to an initialized git_commit_graph_writer_options struct.
Caller must check the return value before using *out.
On failure, the output parameter must not be used.
