functions.name: git_commit_graph_writer_free
functions.description: Free a commit-graph writer and its resources. Safe to call with NULL (no action).
requirements: w may be NULL (no effect).
Do not use the writer after freeing.

functions.name: git_commit_graph_writer_add_index_file
functions.description: Add a pack index (.idx) file to the commit-graph writer so commits from that pack can be included. Returns 0 on success or an error code.
requirements: w must be a valid, initialized writer created by git_commit_graph_writer_new.
repo must be the repository that owns the .idx file (non-NULL).
idx_path must be the filesystem path to a .idx file (non-NULL).
Caller must check the return value for success before proceeding.

functions.name: git_commit_graph_writer_add_revwalk
functions.description: Add all commits from the provided revwalk to the commit-graph writer's input set. Returns 0 on success or an error code.
requirements: w must be a valid, initialized writer created by git_commit_graph_writer_new.
walk must be a valid git_revwalk (non-NULL).
Caller must check the return value for success before proceeding.

functions.name: git_commit_graph_writer_commit
functions.description: Write the commit-graph to disk using the writer's configuration and inputs. Returns 0 on success or an error code.
requirements: w must be a valid, initialized writer created by git_commit_graph_writer_new.
Caller must check the return value to ensure the write succeeded.

functions.name: git_commit_graph_writer_dump
functions.description: Serialize the commit-graph to an in-memory buffer instead of writing to disk. Returns 0 on success or an error code.
requirements: buffer must be a valid, writable git_buf pointer (non-NULL) to receive the data.
w must be a valid, initialized writer created by git_commit_graph_writer_new.
Caller must check the return value before using the buffer contents.

functions.name: git_config_init_backend
functions.description: Initializes a git_config_backend structure with default values (equivalent to using GIT_CONFIG_BACKEND_INIT). Use this before populating callbacks or adding the backend to a config. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
requirements: backend must point to a writable git_config_backend instance.
version must be GIT_CONFIG_BACKEND_VERSION.
Call before using the backend (eg, before setting callbacks or adding it to a git_config).
On failure (return -1), the contents of backend are unspecified and should be reinitialized or discarded.

functions.name: git_config_add_backend
functions.signature: int git_config_add_backend(git_config *cfg, git_config_backend *file, git_config_level_t level, const git_repository *repo, int force);
functions.description: Adds a configuration backend to an existing git_config at the specified priority level. The git_config takes ownership and will free the backend automatically. If a backend already exists at the given level and force is nonzero, it will be replaced; otherwise the call fails with GIT_EEXISTS. Returns 0 on success or an error code.
requirements: cfg must be a valid, initialized git_config pointer.
file must be a valid git_config_backend pointer; ownership is transferred to cfg and the caller must not free it afterward.
level must be a valid git_config_level_t value.
repo may be NULL; if provided, it is used to allow parsing of conditional includes.
force controls replacement: 0 prohibits replacing an existing backend at the same level (function returns GIT_EEXISTS); nonzero permits replacement.
Do not access or free file after successful addition, since the configuration object will free it automatically.

functions.name: git_config_backend_from_string
functions.signature: int git_config_backend_from_string(git_config_backend **out, const char *cfg, size_t len, git_config_backend_memory_options *opts);
functions.description: Creates an in-memory configuration backend by parsing a buffer containing data in standard git configuration file format. On success, stores the new backend in *out. Returns 0 on success or a libgit2 error code.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created backend.
cfg must point to a buffer containing len bytes in standard git config file format; the data need not be NUL-terminated if len is provided appropriately.
len must be the number of bytes to parse from cfg.
opts may be NULL; if provided, opts->version should be set to GIT_CONFIG_BACKEND_MEMORY_OPTIONS_VERSION (use GIT_CONFIG_BACKEND_MEMORY_OPTIONS_INIT) and optional fields may be NULL.

The resulting backend can be added to a git_config; when added, the configuration object will manage its lifetime. Ownership semantics outside of being added to a git_config are not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: git_config_backend_from_values
functions.signature: int git_config_backend_from_values(git_config_backend **out, const char **values, size_t len, git_config_backend_memory_options *opts);
functions.description: Creates an in-memory configuration backend from a list of key/value pairs specified as strings in "key=value" form. On success, stores the new backend in *out. Returns 0 on success or a libgit2 error code.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created backend.
values must be a non-NULL array with at least len entries; each entry must be a NUL-terminated string of the form "key=value".
len must be the number of entries in the values array to read.
Keys and values must be valid per git configuration key syntax (value format must be acceptable to the parser).
opts may be NULL; if provided, opts->version should be GIT_CONFIG_BACKEND_MEMORY_OPTIONS_VERSION (use GIT_CONFIG_BACKEND_MEMORY_OPTIONS_INIT), and other fields may be NULL.

The resulting backend can be added to a git_config; when added, the configuration object will manage its lifetime. Ownership semantics outside of being added to a git_config are not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: git_diff_print_callback__to_buf
functions.signature: int git_diff_print_callback__to_buf(const git_diff_delta *delta, const git_diff_hunk *hunk, const git_diff_line *line, void *payload)
functions.description: Diff print callback that appends diff/patch output to a git_buf. Intended to be passed as the callback to git_diff_print or git_patch_print, not typically invoked directly. When used, provide a git_buf* via the payload; the generated text is appended to that buffer.
requirements: Must be used as a print callback for git_diff_print or git_patch_print; not intended for direct standalone calls.
payload must be a valid, writable git_buf*; content will be appended after any existing bytes.
git_buf must be initialized before use (e.g., via libgit2 buffer initialization APIs).
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; nonzero is an error code from libgit2.
The const pointers delta, hunk, and line are provided by the diff printer; callers should not modify or free them.

functions.name: git_diff_print_callback__to_file_handle
functions.signature: int git_diff_print_callback__to_file_handle(const git_diff_delta *delta, const git_diff_hunk *hunk, const git_diff_line *line, void *payload)
functions.description: Diff print callback that writes diff/patch output to a stdio FILE*. Intended for use as the callback to git_diff_print or git_patch_print. Provide a FILE* via the payload; if NULL is passed, output is written to stdout.
requirements: Must be used as a print callback for git_diff_print or git_patch_print; not intended for direct standalone calls.
payload must be a FILE* (e.g., stdout, stderr, or from fopen). If payload is NULL, stdout is used.
If a FILE* is provided, it must be a valid open stream suitable for writing.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; nonzero is an error code from libgit2.
The const pointers delta, hunk, and line are provided by the diff printer; callers should not modify or free them.

functions.name: git_diff_get_perfdata
functions.description: Retrieves performance statistics (e.g., number of stat() calls and OID calculations) for a given diff object and writes them into the provided git_diff_perfdata structure.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to writable memory for a git_diff_perfdata structure.
diff must be a valid, initialized git_diff pointer produced by libgit2 and must remain alive for the duration of the call.
Caller should check the return value: 0 on success, negative on error.
It is recommended (but not strictly required in the header) to initialize out, e.g., with GIT_DIFF_PERFDATA_INIT, or set out->version = GIT_DIFF_PERFDATA_VERSION before the call.

functions.name: git_status_list_get_perfdata
functions.description: Retrieves combined diff performance statistics associated with a git_status_list and writes them into the provided git_diff_perfdata structure.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to writable memory for a git_diff_perfdata structure.
status must be a valid, initialized git_status_list pointer produced by libgit2 and must remain alive for the duration of the call.
Caller should check the return value: 0 on success, negative on error.
It is recommended (but not strictly required in the header) to initialize out, e.g., with GIT_DIFF_PERFDATA_INIT, or set out->version = GIT_DIFF_PERFDATA_VERSION before the call.

functions.name: git_email_create_from_diff
functions.signature: int git_email_create_from_diff(git_buf *out, git_diff *diff, size_t patch_idx, size_t patch_count, const git_oid *commit_id, const char *summary, const char *body, const git_signature *author, const git_email_create_options *opts)
functions.description: Create an mbox-formatted email patch from a diff, suitable for sending via email. Typical usage is to build or obtain a git_diff for a commit (or range), then call this to serialize one patch in a multi-patch series, providing the patch’s index and total count along with commit metadata (id, summary, author). The resulting email text (including diffstat and patch) is written to the provided git_buf. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on error. Notes: the body parameter is optional text placed above the diffstat; options can customize email formatting if provided.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable git_buf; it will receive the generated email patch. It should be an initialized buffer (e.g., a zeroed/initialized git_buf) before the call (inferred from libgit2 git_buf usage patterns).
diff must be a non-NULL, valid git_diff whose lifetime extends through the call (must have been created by libgit2).
patch_count is the total number of patches in the series; it should be >= 1 (inferred from parameter description).
patch_idx is the index of this patch within the series and should be less than patch_count; indexing is typically zero-based in libgit2 (inferred from naming).
commit_id must be a non-NULL pointer to the OID of the commit being formatted.
summary must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string representing the commit message summary/subject.
body is optional; it may be NULL to omit additional text, or a NUL-terminated string to include text above the diffstat (explicitly documented as optional).
author must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid git_signature for the author of the commit.
opts may be NULL to use default behavior, or must point to an initialized git_email_create_options with a correct version field if provided (inferred from libgit2 options-struct conventions).

Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; any non-zero return indicates an error and the caller should treat output as unspecified and consult libgit2 error APIs (e.g., git_error_last) (partly inferred from libgit2 error handling patterns).

functions.name: git_error_clear

functions.name: git_hashsig_create
functions.signature: int git_hashsig_create(git_hashsig **out, const char *buf, size_t buflen, git_hashsig_option_t opts)

Returns 0 on success, GIT_EBUFS when the buffer lacks enough data for a valid signature (unless GIT_HASHSIG_ALLOW_SMALL_FILES is set), or a negative libgit2 error code.

If opts includes GIT_HASHSIG_IGNORE_WHITESPACE, the function will modify the provided buffer in place; therefore buf must reference writable memory (do not pass read-only memory like string literals when using this option).
Options GIT_HASHSIG_NORMAL, GIT_HASHSIG_IGNORE_WHITESPACE, and GIT_HASHSIG_SMART_WHITESPACE are mutually exclusive and should not be combined.
If the input does not contain enough data to compute a valid signature and GIT_HASHSIG_ALLOW_SMALL_FILES is not set, the function will fail with GIT_EBUFS; callers must check the return value.
On any non-zero return (negative error code or GIT_EBUFS), *out is not a valid signature and must not be used.

functions.signature: int git_hashsig_create_fromfile(git_hashsig **out, const char *path, git_hashsig_option_t opts)

On success, allocates a git_hashsig stored in *out; free with git_hashsig_free. Returns 0 on success, GIT_EBUFS when the file lacks enough data for a valid signature (unless GIT_HASHSIG_ALLOW_SMALL_FILES is set), or a negative libgit2 error code.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to a git_hashsig* to receive the created signature; the result must be freed with git_hashsig_free.
path must be a non-NULL path to a readable file; the file contents are treated as text for hashing.
Options GIT_HASHSIG_NORMAL, GIT_HASHSIG_IGNORE_WHITESPACE, and GIT_HASHSIG_SMART_WHITESPACE are mutually exclusive and should not be combined.
If the file does not contain enough data to compute a valid signature and GIT_HASHSIG_ALLOW_SMALL_FILES is not set, the function will fail with GIT_EBUFS; callers must check the return value.
On any non-zero return (negative error code or GIT_EBUFS), *out is not a valid signature and must not be used.

functions.name: git_hashsig_free
functions.description: Release memory associated with a similarity signature previously created by git_hashsig_create or git_hashsig_create_fromfile.
requirements: sig must be a git_hashsig previously returned by git_hashsig_create or git_hashsig_create_fromfile and not already freed.

functions.name: git_hashsig_compare

functions.name: git_mempack_new

requirements: backend must be the git_odb_backend that originally allocated the memory.
data must be a pointer previously returned by git_odb_backend_data_alloc and not already returned to libgit2.
Do not call this to free memory that has been returned to libgit2; libgit2 will free that memory.
No value is returned; callers must ensure the pointer is appropriate to free via this API.

functions.name: git_odb_backend_malloc
functions.description: Deprecated alias of git_odb_backend_data_alloc, preserved for backward compatibility when GIT_DEPRECATE_HARD is not defined. Allocates a buffer for backend read operations to return to libgit2; if not returned due to an error, free it with git_odb_backend_data_free.
requirements: Available only when GIT_DEPRECATE_HARD is not defined; prefer git_odb_backend_data_alloc.
backend must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to the allocating git_odb_backend.
len specifies the number of bytes to allocate; returns NULL if out of memory.
Buffers returned to libgit2 must not be freed by the backend; if not returned, they must be freed with git_odb_backend_data_free.
Callers must handle a NULL return for allocation failure.

functions.name: git_openssl_set_locking
functions.description: Initializes and configures OpenSSL locking for libgit2 by allocating locks and setting OpenSSL’s locking callback to use the system’s native locking primitives. This is a last-resort convenience helper; prefer your language’s OpenSSL bindings if they already set up locking. The locking function is cleared and memory freed when git_threads_sutdown() is called. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error or when libgit2 was not built with OpenSSL and threading support.
requirements: Library must be built with OpenSSL and threading support for the function to succeed (otherwise returns -1).
Caller must check the return value and handle errors (0 indicates success; -1 indicates failure).
Be aware that the installed locking function and allocated memory are cleared when git_threads_sutdown() is called; do not assume locks persist beyond that point.

functions.name: git_path_is_gitfile
functions.signature: int git_path_is_gitfile(const char *path, size_t pathlen, git_path_gitfile gitfile, git_path_fs fs);
functions.description: Checks whether the given path component refers to a Git-specific file (.gitignore, .gitmodules, or .gitattributes), applying filesystem-specific comparison rules (generic, NTFS, or HFS). Use this when a plain string comparison may be unreliable due to filesystem case-folding or normalization. Returns >0 if the component matches the requested gitfile type, 0 if it does not, and -1 on error.
requirements: path must point to a readable memory region of at least pathlen bytes; it may be non-NUL-terminated because pathlen specifies the number of bytes to check.
pathlen is the number of bytes of path to examine; use strlen(path) when passing a NUL-terminated string.
gitfile must be one of the defined git_path_gitfile enum values: GIT_PATH_GITFILE_GITIGNORE, GIT_PATH_GITFILE_GITMODULES, or GIT_PATH_GITFILE_GITATTRIBUTES.
fs must be one of the defined git_path_fs enum values: GIT_PATH_FS_GENERIC, GIT_PATH_FS_NTFS, or GIT_PATH_FS_HFS.
Callers must check the return value: >0 indicates a match, 0 indicates no match, and -1 indicates an error condition.

functions.name: git_refdb_init_backend
functions.description: Initialize a git_refdb_backend structure with default values (equivalent to assigning GIT_REFDB_BACKEND_INIT). Call this before populating or using a custom refdb backend vtable. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure. Typical usage is to pass GIT_REFDB_BACKEND_VERSION for the version parameter.
requirements: backend must be a valid, writable pointer to a git_refdb_backend to be initialized
version should be GIT_REFDB_BACKEND_VERSION (currently 1)
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success, negative indicates failure

functions.name: git_refdb_backend_fs
functions.description: Construct the default filesystem-based reference database backend for the given repository. Under normal usage this is created when opening/creating a repository, but this function allows explicitly creating one. On success, *backend_out is set to a newly constructed backend instance.
requirements: backend_out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created backend
repo must be a valid git_repository pointer associated with the repository whose refs should be accessed
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success, negative indicates failure

Ownership note: the created backend is owned by the caller until passed to git_refdb_set_backend (which takes ownership). If not set on a refdb, the caller is responsible for eventually freeing it via the backend's free callback

functions.name: git_refdb_set_backend
functions.description: Attach a custom refdb backend to an existing git_refdb. After this call, the git_refdb takes ownership of the backend and will manage its lifetime; callers should not free it themselves. Returns 0 on success, a negative error code otherwise.
requirements: refdb must be a valid git_refdb instance to which the backend will be attached
backend must be a valid, initialized git_refdb_backend instance
After a successful call, the caller must NOT free backend; the git_refdb assumes ownership
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success, negative indicates failure

functions.name: git_reference__alloc
functions.signature: git_reference *git_reference__alloc(const char *name, const git_oid *oid, const git_oid *peel);
functions.description: Allocates a new direct git_reference in memory from an object ID. Intended for low-level/internal use (sys/ API). Returns the created reference on success or NULL on error. The optional peel should be the OID of the first non-tag object corresponding to oid when the target is a tag; pass NULL if unknown or not applicable. This function allocates only; it does not itself persist the reference to a ref database.
requirements: name must be a valid git reference name (e.g., "refs/heads/main"); inferred from parameter description.
name should be non-NULL; NULL yields undefined behavior or error (inferred).
oid must be non-NULL and point to a valid git_oid for a direct reference (explicit/inferred).
peel may be NULL; if provided, it should be the OID of the first non-tag object reachable from oid (explicit).
Caller must check the return value for NULL and handle allocation/validation errors (explicit).
On success, the returned git_reference must be released with git_reference_free when no longer needed (inferred from libgit2 ownership patterns).

functions.name: git_reference__alloc_symbolic
functions.description: Allocates a new symbolic git_reference in memory that points to another reference name. Intended for low-level/internal use (sys/ API). Returns the created reference on success or NULL on error. This function allocates only; it does not itself persist the reference to a ref database.
requirements: name must be a valid git reference name; inferred from parameter description.
name should be non-NULL; NULL yields undefined behavior or error (inferred).
target should be a non-NULL, valid reference name that the symbolic reference will point to (inferred from symbolic reference semantics).
Caller must check the return value for NULL and handle errors (explicit).
On success, the returned git_reference must be released with git_reference_free when no longer needed (inferred from libgit2 ownership patterns).

functions.name: git_remote_connect_options_dispose
functions.description: Disposes (frees) libgit2-initialized fields inside a git_remote_connect_options structure that was previously returned by git_transport_remote_connect_options. Use this when you are finished with the connect options to release any internal allocations before freeing or reusing the struct. This function does not free the git_remote_connect_options object itself—only the memory referenced by its libgit2-initialized fields.
requirements: opts must point to a git_remote_connect_options that was obtained from git_transport_remote_connect_options.
This function releases only internal/libgit2-allocated fields; the caller remains responsible for the lifetime of the git_remote_connect_options struct itself.
After disposal, do not read or use the previously libgit2-initialized fields unless the struct is reinitialized.
Do not use this function on git_remote_connect_options instances that were not initialized/returned by libgit2 (per documentation: only use for git_transport_remote_connect_options results).
The function returns no status; callers should ensure preconditions are met before calling.

functions.name: git_repository_new_options_init
functions.description: Initialize a git_repository_new_options structure with default values. Use this before passing options to repository creation helpers. Equivalent to assigning GIT_REPOSITORY_NEW_OPTIONS_INIT.
requirements: opts must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a git_repository_new_options struct to be initialized.
version should be GIT_REPOSITORY_NEW_OPTIONS_VERSION.
Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure. Callers must check the return value before using the options struct.

functions.name: git_repository_new
functions.description: Create a new in-memory repository handle with no backends and no config object. This is useful when associating the repository with non-filesystem object/config backends. Note: this API only creates SHA1 repositories.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the created git_repository*.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise a negative error code. Callers must check the return value before using the output repository.
The resulting repository has no physical location; features relying on $GIT_DIR, $GIT_COMMON_DIR or $GIT_INFO_DIR may not function properly until appropriately configured.

functions.name: git_repository_new_ext
functions.description: Create a new in-memory repository handle with no backends. Options control repository creation (eg, OID type). If opts is NULL, defaults are used. Available only when compiled with GIT_EXPERIMENTAL_SHA256.
requirements: Available only if the library is built with GIT_EXPERIMENTAL_SHA256 defined; callers must ensure availability before calling.
out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the created git_repository*.
opts may be NULL for defaults; if non-NULL, it should be initialized (e.g., via git_repository_new_options_init) and its version field set appropriately.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise a negative error code. Callers must check the return value.

functions.name: git_repository__cleanup
functions.description: Reset and free all internal state, mapped memory, and cached objects in the repository, leaving it in a blank state. Typically invoked by git_repository_free; direct use is only needed for aggressive pre-free cleanup.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository pointer.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise a negative error code. Callers must check the return value before assuming the repository state has been reset.

functions.name: git_repository_reinit_filesystem
functions.description: Re-detect and update filesystem-dependent configuration (e.g., core.ignorecase, core.filemode, core.symlinks) for an open repository, useful after moving a repository to a different filesystem. Optionally recurse into submodules.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository pointer.
recurse_submodules is treated as a boolean flag indicating whether to update submodules recursively.
Returns 0 on success; < 0 on error. Callers must check the return value.

functions.name: git_repository_set_config
functions.description: Associate a configuration object with the repository. The repository will use it for all configuration queries and will retain a reference.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository pointer.
config must be a valid git_config pointer.
The repository keeps a reference; the caller must still free the config after setting it to the repository to avoid leaks.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise an error code. Callers must check the return value.

functions.name: git_repository_set_odb
functions.description: Associate an object database (ODB) with the repository for all object operations. The repository will retain a reference.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository pointer.
odb must be a valid git_odb pointer.
The repository keeps a reference; the caller must still free the ODB after setting it to the repository to avoid leaks.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise an error code. Callers must check the return value.

functions.name: git_repository_set_refdb
functions.description: Associate a reference database backend with the repository for all reference operations. The repository will retain a reference.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository pointer.
refdb must be a valid git_refdb pointer.
The repository keeps a reference; the caller must still free the refdb after setting it to the repository to avoid leaks.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise an error code. Callers must check the return value.

functions.name: git_repository_set_index
functions.description: Associate an index with the repository for all index operations. The repository will retain a reference.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository pointer.
index must be a valid git_index pointer; passing NULL is allowed to unset the index (implied by the set-bare documentation’s example).
The repository keeps a reference; the caller must still free the index after setting it to the repository to avoid leaks.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise an error code. Callers must check the return value.

functions.name: git_repository_set_bare
functions.description: Convert a repository to a bare repository: clear the working directory and set core.bare to true. Does not modify or remove the index automatically.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository pointer.
Returns 0 on success; < 0 on failure. Callers must check the return value.
If you also want to remove the index, call git_repository_set_index(repo, NULL) separately (this function will not do that).

functions.name: git_repository_submodule_cache_all
functions.description: Load and cache all submodules for the repository, turning subsequent git_submodule_lookup calls from O(N) into O(1). Useful before operations that inspect many submodules.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository pointer.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise an error code. Callers must check the return value.

functions.name: git_repository_submodule_cache_clear
functions.description: Clear the repository’s submodule cache previously populated by git_repository_submodule_cache_all. Does nothing if no cache exists.
requirements: repo must be a valid repository pointer.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise an error code. Callers must check the return value.
The cache may become invalid when configuration, working tree, index, or HEAD changes; clear it as needed.

functions.name: git_stream_register
functions.description: Registers or deregisters stream constructors used by libgit2. Pass a non-NULL registration to install constructors for the given stream type(s); pass NULL to remove any custom constructors and revert to system defaults. The type may combine git_stream_t values (per header comment). Returns 0 on success or a libgit2 error code on failure.
requirements: If registration is non-NULL, registration->version must be set to GIT_STREAM_VERSION (per struct field documentation).
If registration is NULL, the call deregisters the current constructor(s) and reverts to system defaults.
type must be one or more git_stream_t values as documented (header states it may be a bitwise AND of types).
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success; any non-zero value is an error code.
If registration->wrap is unset, HTTP CONNECT proxying will not be supported (behavioral note from documentation).

functions.name: git_stream_register_tls
functions.description: Deprecated: registers a TLS stream constructor callback. Internally forwards to git_stream_register and does not support HTTP CONNECT proxies. Prefer using git_stream_register with a git_stream_registration. Returns 0 on success or a libgit2 error code on failure.
requirements: ctor must match the git_stream_cb signature: int (*ctor)(git_stream **out, const char *host, const char *port).
The ctor is expected to create and return (via out) a valid git_stream for the given host/port and return 0 on success (implied by callback documentation).
This API is deprecated; new code should use git_stream_register with git_stream_registration instead.
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success; any non-zero value is an error code.

Streams produced by ctor must conform to git_stream requirements (the stream object must have git_stream as its first member and provide valid function pointers), as implied by the surrounding struct documentation.

functions.name: git_transport_init
functions.description: Initialize a git_transport struct with default values. Equivalent to assigning GIT_TRANSPORT_INIT. Use this before populating callbacks in a custom transport implementation.
requirements: opts must be a valid, writable pointer to a git_transport struct.
version must be GIT_TRANSPORT_VERSION.
Returns 0 on success; -1 on failure.

functions.name: git_transport_new
functions.description: Create a transport instance for the given URL by looking up a registered transport for the URL’s scheme (eg, git://, http://, https://, ssh://). The created transport is associated with the provided owner remote.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the created git_transport*.
owner must point to a valid git_remote that will own the transport.
url must be a non-NULL string with a supported scheme.
Returns 0 on success or a libgit2 error code on failure.

functions.name: git_transport_ssh_with_paths
functions.description: Create an SSH transport that uses custom paths for remote git commands. Intended for use as a transport factory callback for a remote or clone options.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the created git_transport*.
owner must point to the owning git_remote.
payload must be a pointer to a git_strarray where index 0 is the path to git-upload-pack and index 1 is the path to git-receive-pack.
Returns 0 on success or a libgit2 error code on failure.

functions.name: git_transport_register
functions.signature: int git_transport_register(const char *prefix, git_transport_cb cb, void *param)
functions.description: Register a custom transport factory to handle URLs with the given scheme prefix (e.g., "git", "https"). The callback will be invoked to create transport instances; param is passed to the callback at creation time.
requirements: prefix must be the scheme string to match (e.g., "git", "https").
cb must be a valid transport creation callback of type git_transport_cb.
param is a user-defined value that will be passed to cb on creation (may be NULL).
The caller must synchronize calls to git_transport_register and git_transport_unregister with other threads or code that instantiate transports.
Returns 0 on success or a libgit2 error code on failure.

functions.name: git_transport_unregister
functions.description: Unregister a previously-registered custom transport for the given scheme prefix.
requirements: prefix must match the scheme previously registered with git_transport_register.
The caller must synchronize calls to git_transport_register and git_transport_unregister with other threads or code that instantiate transports.
Returns 0 on success or a libgit2 error code on failure.

functions.name: git_transport_dummy
functions.description: Create an instance of the dummy transport provided by libgit2.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the created git_transport*.
owner must point to the git_remote that will own this transport.
payload must be NULL (as required by this factory).
Returns 0 on success or a libgit2 error code on failure.

functions.name: git_transport_local
functions.description: Create an instance of the local transport provided by libgit2.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the created git_transport*.
owner must point to the git_remote that will own this transport.
payload must be NULL (as required by this factory).
Returns 0 on success or a libgit2 error code on failure.

functions.name: git_transport_smart
functions.description: Create an instance of the smart transport (which speaks the Git smart protocol) using the provided subtransport definition.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the created git_transport*.
owner must point to the git_remote that will own this transport.
payload must be a pointer to a git_smart_subtransport_definition.
Returns 0 on success or a libgit2 error code on failure.

functions.name: git_transport_smart_certificate_check
functions.signature: int git_transport_smart_certificate_check(git_transport *transport, git_cert *cert, int valid, const char *hostname)
functions.description: Invoke the certificate check callback associated with a smart transport. Used by transports that perform TLS to validate the server certificate with the user’s callback.
requirements: transport must be a smart transport created via the smart transport mechanism.
cert is the certificate presented by the peer (may be transport/backend specific).
valid is a nonzero/zero indicator of the library’s belief about certificate validity to pass along to the callback.
hostname should be the hostname connected to (as a UTF-8 string).
Returns: 0 if the callback succeeded; GIT_PASSTHROUGH if no callback is registered or the callback declined to validate; < 0 on error.

functions.name: git_transport_smart_credentials
functions.signature: int git_transport_smart_credentials(git_credential **out, git_transport *transport, const char *user, int methods)
functions.description: Invoke the credentials callback for a smart transport to obtain authentication credentials.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the created git_credential*.
transport must be a smart transport created via the smart transport mechanism.
user is the username parsed from the URL (if any); may be NULL if none was present.
methods is a bitmask of available authentication methods (library-defined).
Returns: 0 if credentials were provided; GIT_PASSTHROUGH if no callback is registered or the callback declined to provide credentials; < 0 on error.

functions.name: git_transport_remote_connect_options
functions.description: Retrieve a copy of the remote connect options from a transport. The data is deep-copied and must be disposed by the caller.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to a git_remote_connect_options struct to receive the data.
transport must be a valid git_transport.
On success, the caller must free the returned data by calling git_remote_connect_options_dispose.
Returns 0 on success or a libgit2 error code on failure.

functions.name: git_smart_subtransport_http
functions.description: Create an HTTP/HTTPS subtransport instance for the smart transport. This subtransport implements stateless (request/response) communication.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the created git_smart_subtransport*.
owner must be the owning smart git_transport.
param is an optional custom parameter for the subtransport (may be NULL).
Returns 0 on success or a libgit2 error code on failure.

functions.name: git_smart_subtransport_git
functions.description: Create a git protocol (git://) subtransport instance for the smart transport. This typically implements a stateful, persistent connection.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the created git_smart_subtransport*.
owner must be the owning smart git_transport.
param is an optional custom parameter for the subtransport (may be NULL).
Returns 0 on success or a libgit2 error code on failure.

functions.name: git_smart_subtransport_ssh
functions.description: Create an SSH subtransport instance for the smart transport.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the created git_smart_subtransport*.
owner must be the owning smart git_transport.
param is an optional custom parameter for the subtransport (may be NULL).
Returns 0 on success or a libgit2 error code on failure.

// Pick a valid git_error_t class as required
unsigned int pick = *FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int);
int classes[] = {
    GIT_ERROR_NONE,
    GIT_ERROR_NOMEMORY,
    GIT_ERROR_OS,
    GIT_ERROR_INVALID,
    GIT_ERROR_REFERENCE,
    GIT_ERROR_ZLIB,
    GIT_ERROR_REPOSITORY,
    GIT_ERROR_CONFIG,
    GIT_ERROR_REGEX,
    GIT_ERROR_ODB,
    GIT_ERROR_INDEX,
    GIT_ERROR_OBJECT,
    GIT_ERROR_NET,
    GIT_ERROR_TAG,
    GIT_ERROR_TREE,
    GIT_ERROR_INDEXER,
    GIT_ERROR_SSL,
    GIT_ERROR_SUBMODULE,
    GIT_ERROR_THREAD,
    GIT_ERROR_STASH,
    GIT_ERROR_CHECKOUT,
    GIT_ERROR_FETCHHEAD,
    GIT_ERROR_MERGE,
    GIT_ERROR_SSH,
    GIT_ERROR_FILTER,
    GIT_ERROR_REVERT,
    GIT_ERROR_CALLBACK,
    GIT_ERROR_CHERRYPICK,
    GIT_ERROR_DESCRIBE,
    GIT_ERROR_REBASE,
    GIT_ERROR_FILESYSTEM,
    GIT_ERROR_PATCH,
    GIT_ERROR_WORKTREE,
    GIT_ERROR_SHA,
    GIT_ERROR_HTTP,
    GIT_ERROR_INTERNAL,
    GIT_ERROR_GRAFTS
};
int error_class = classes[pick % (sizeof(classes)/sizeof(classes[0]))];

// Generate a random message string; ensure NUL-terminated via std::string
std::string msg = FUZZ_PARAM_STR();

// Invoke and enforce return value contract (0 success, -1 failure)
int rc = git_error_set_str(error_class, msg.c_str());
if (rc != 0) { FUZZ_BAIL(); }

// Validation: Inputs are constrained; return value is checked and bails on failure. No outputs.

unharnessable_functions.name: git_blob_create_fromstream
